text:
General Terms of the Series A Notes
In this “General Terms of the Series A Notes” section, all references to the “debt securities” refer to Series A Notes issued by 
JPMorgan Chase Financial Company LLC.
The following description of the terms of the debt securities contains certain general terms that may apply to the debt securities, 
including the Callable Notes.
We have summarized below the material provisions of the 2016 Indenture and the debt securities and guarantees issued under the 
2016 Indenture.
These descriptions are only summaries, and each investor should refer to the 2016 Indenture, which describes completely the terms 
and definitions summarized below and contains additional information regarding the debt securities issued under it.  Where 
appropriate, we use parentheses to refer you to the particular sections of the 2016 Indenture.  Any reference to particular sections or 
defined terms of the 2016 Indenture in any statement under this heading qualifies the entire statement and incorporates by 
reference the applicable section or definition into that statement.
The debt securities will be the Issuer’s direct, unsecured general obligations, the payment on which is fully and unconditionally 
guaranteed by the Guarantor, and will have the same rank in liquidation as all of the Issuer’s other unsecured and unsubordinated 
debt.
The Guarantor is a holding company and conducts substantially all of its operations through subsidiaries.  As a result, claims of the 
holders of the debt securities against the Guarantor under the guarantee will generally have a junior position to claims of creditors of 
the Guarantor’s subsidiaries, except to the extent that the Guarantor may be recognized, and receives payment, as a creditor of those 
subsidiaries.  Claims of the Guarantor’s subsidiaries’ creditors other than the Guarantor include substantial amounts of long-term 
debt, deposit liabilities, federal funds purchased, securities loaned or sold under repurchase agreements, commercial paper and 
other borrowed funds.

title: Events of Default and Waivers
heading: 37.4.9.1 Events of Default and Waivers
start_phrase: An “Event of Default” with respect to a series of debt securities issued under the 2016 Indenture is defined in the 2016 Indenture as:
summary:
- Acceleration on event of default: If maturity is accelerated, the Issuer or Calculation Agent must notify the Trustee (New York office) and DTC of the cash amount due within two business days of acceleration.
- Listing: Callable Notes are listed on the NYSE under “JPM/32,” with no assurance of continued listing, liquidity, or trading market.
- Book-entry only (DTC): Notes issued solely in fully registered global form in the name of Cede & Co.; deposited with DTC; no definitive notes except in limited cases.
- Registrar/Paying agent: The Bank of New York Mellon (or affiliates) serves as registrar, transfer agent, and paying agent; additional paying agents may be designated.
- Reopening: Issuer may issue additional notes (“reopenings”) that share the same CUSIP, are fungible and trade interchangeably with existing notes; pricing set at time of offering.
- General terms/2016 Indenture overview: Summary of Series A Notes under the 2016 Indenture; debt securities are direct, unsecured, unsubordinated obligations of the Issuer, fully and unconditionally guaranteed by the Guarantor, ranking equally with other unsecured unsubordinated debt.
- Structural subordination: Claims under the guarantee are structurally junior to creditors of the Guarantor’s subsidiaries (e.g., long-term debt, deposits, repo, commercial paper, other borrowings) except to the extent the Guarantor is recognized and paid as a creditor of its subsidiaries.
- Events of Default (EoD): Include (a) 30-day interest payment default; (b) principal/other amounts unpaid when due; (c) covenant breach continuing 90 days after notice by Trustee or holders of ≥25% of affected series; (d) specified Issuer bankruptcy/insolvency/receivership/winding up/liquidation; (e) guarantee ceasing/denial subject to exceptions for Guarantor insolvency/resolution/FDIC actions; (f) any additional EoD in supplemental indentures or forms.
- Remedies/acceleration and waivers: Upon certain continuing EoDs, Trustee or holders of ≥25% may declare principal and accrued interest immediately due; automatic acceleration upon specified Issuer bankruptcy events; majority of holders may waive past defaults subject to conditions.
- Guarantor-related events: Guarantor bankruptcy/insolvency/resolution or non-payment covenant breaches by Guarantor (other than payment default) do not constitute an EoD for the notes and do not permit acceleration absent an Issuer EoD; potential adverse value impact noted.
- Trustee notices and holder rights: Trustee must give default notice within 90 days (may withhold if in holders’ interest, except for payment defaults); majority of affected holders (voting as a single class) may direct remedies; Trustee may require indemnity; individual holders’ suits restricted unless prerequisites (notice, 60-day wait, 25% request, indemnity) are met; absolute right to receive payment or sue for payment preserved.
- Annual compliance statements: Issuer and Guarantor must file annual statements with the Trustee regarding knowledge of defaults.
- Indenture modifications: With consent of holders of a majority in aggregate principal of each affected series; unanimous holder consent required for fundamental changes (maturity extension, principal/interest reductions, currency/method changes, redemption amount reductions, holder repurchase/suit rights, required consent thresholds, adverse changes to guarantee). Certain amendments permitted without holder consent (e.g., mergers evidence, Trustee replacement, curing ambiguities, non-material changes).
- Consolidation, merger, sale of assets: Conditions for Issuer and Guarantor combinations/transfers require a U.S. successor that assumes obligations and no (or continuing) EoD immediately after the transaction.
text:
Events of Default and Waivers
An “Event of Default” with respect to a series of debt securities issued under the 2016 Indenture is defined in the 2016 Indenture as:
a. default in the payment of interest on any debt securities of that series and continuance of such default for 30 days;
b. default in the payment of principal or other amounts payable on any debt securities of that series when due, at maturity, 
upon redemption, by declaration, or otherwise;
c. default in the performance, or breach, of any other covenants or warranties applicable to the Issuer contained in the 2016 
Indenture applicable to that series, and continuation of such default or breach for 90 days after written notice has been given by the Trustee to the Issuer and the Guarantor or given by holders of at least 25% in aggregate principal amount of 
the outstanding securities of all series affected thereby to the Issuer, the Guarantor and the Trustee;
d. certain events of the Issuer’s bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, winding up or liquidation, whether voluntary or 
involuntary;
e. the guarantee ceases to be in full force and effect, other than in accordance with the 2016 Indenture, or the Guarantor 
denies or disaffirms its obligations under the guarantee, provided  that no Event of Default with respect to the guarantee will 
occur as a result of, or because it is related directly or indirectly to, the insolvency of the Guarantor or the commencement of 
proceedings under Title 11 of the United States Code, or the appointment of a receiver for the Guarantor under Title II of the 
Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010, or the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation having 
separately repudiated the Guarantee in receivership, or the commencement of or certain other events of the Guarantor’s 
bankruptcy, insolvency, resolution, receivership, winding up or liquidation; or
f. any other event of default provided in the applicable supplemental indentures to the 2016 Indenture or form of security. 
(Section 5.01)
If an Event of Default occurs and is continuing because of a default in the payment of principal, interest or other amounts payable on 
the debt securities, a failure in the performance, or breach, of any covenant or agreement applicable to the Issuer, the guarantee 
ceasing to be in full force and effect, or any other event of default provided in the applicable supplemental indentures to the 2016 
Indenture or form of security, either the Trustee or the holders of not less than 25% in aggregate principal amount of the debt 
securities of such series then outstanding, treated as one class, by written notice to the Issuer and the Guarantor, may declare the 
principal of all outstanding debt securities of such series and any interest accrued thereon, to be due and payable immediately.  If a 
default due to specified events of the Issuer’s bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, winding up or liquidation, occurs and is 
continuing, the principal of all outstanding debt securities and any interest accrued thereon will automatically, and without any 
declaration or other action on the part of the Trustee or any holder, become immediately due and payable.  Subject to certain 
conditions such declarations may be annulled and past defaults may be waived by the holders of a majority in aggregate principal 
amount of the outstanding debt securities of the series affected. (Sections 5.01 and 5.10)
Events of bankruptcy, insolvency, resolution, receivership, winding up or liquidation relating to the Guarantor will not constitute an 
Event of Default with respect to any series of debt securities.  In addition, failure by the Guarantor to perform any of its covenants or 
warranties (other than a payment default) will not constitute an Event of Default with respect to any series of debt securities.  
Therefore, events of bankruptcy, resolution, receivership, insolvency, winding up or liquidation relating to the Guarantor (in the 
absence of any such event occurring with respect to the Issuer) will not permit any of the debt securities to be declared due and 
payable and the Trustee is not authorized to exercise any remedy against the Issuer or the Guarantor upon the occurrence or 
continuation of these events with respect to the Guarantor.  Instead, even if an event of bankruptcy, insolvency, resolution, 
receivership, winding up or liquidation relating to the Guarantor has occurred, the Trustee and the holders of debt securities of a 
series will not be able to declare the relevant debt securities to be immediately due and payable unless there is an Event of Default 
with respect to that series as described above, such as the Issuer’s bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, winding up or liquidation or 
a payment default by the Issuer or the Guarantor on the relevant debt securities.  The value holders receive on any series of debt 
securities may be significantly less than what holders would have otherwise received had the Issuer’s debt securities been 
declared due and payable immediately or the Trustee been authorized to exercise any remedy against the Issuer or the 
Guarantor upon the occurrence or continuation of these events with respect to the Guarantor.
An Event of Default with respect to one series of debt securities does not necessarily constitute an Event of Default with respect to 
any other series of debt securities.  The 2016 Indenture requires the Trustee to provide notice of default with respect to the debt 
securities within 90 days, unless the default is cured, but provides that the Trustee may withhold notice to the holders of the debt 
securities of any default if the board of directors, the executive committee, or a trust committee of directors or Trustees and/or 
responsible officers of the Trustee determines in good faith that it is in the interest of the holders of the debt securities of the 
applicable series to do so.  The Trustee may not withhold notice of a default in the payment of principal of, interest on or any other 
amounts due under, such debt securities. (Section 5.11)
The 2016 Indenture provides that the holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount of outstanding debt securities of each 
series affected, with all such series voting as a single class, may direct the time, method, and place of conducting any proceeding for 
any remedy available to the Trustee, or exercising any trust or power conferred on the Trustee.  The Trustee may decline to act if the 
direction is contrary to law and in certain other circumstances set forth in the 2016 Indenture. (Section 5.09)  The Trustee is not 
obligated to exercise any of its rights or powers under the 2016 Indenture at the request or direction of the holders of debt securities 
unless the holders offer the Trustee security or indemnity satisfactory to it against the costs, expenses and liabilities incurred therein 
or thereby. (Section 6.02(d))
No holder of any debt security of any affected series has the right to institute any action for remedy unless such holder has previously 
given to the Trustee written notice of default, the Trustee has failed to take action for 60 days after the holders of not less than 25% in aggregate principal amount of the debt securities of each affected series make written request upon the Trustee to institute such 
action and have offered reasonable indemnity in connection with the same and the holders of a majority in aggregate principal 
amount of the debt securities of each affected series (voting as a single class) have not given direction to the Trustee that is 
inconsistent with the written request referred to above. (Section 5.06)
However, the right of any holder of a debt security or coupon to receive payment of the principal of and interest on that debt security 
or coupon on or after its due date, or to institute suit for the enforcement of any such payment, may not be impaired or affected 
without the consent of that holder. (Section 5.07)
The 2016 Indenture requires the Issuer and the Guarantor to file annually with the Trustee a written statement as to whether or not 
the Issuer or the Guarantor, as the case may be, has knowledge of a default. (Section 3.05)

title: Modification of the 2016 Indenture
heading: 37.4.9.2 Modification of the 2016 Indenture
start_phrase: The 2016 Indenture contains provisions permitting the Issuer, the Guarantor and the Trustee to modify the 2016 Indenture or the rights of the holders of debt securities with the consent of the holders of not less than a majority in aggregate principal amount of each outstanding series of debt securities affected by the modification.
summary:
- Enforcement and trustee action: Holders of a specified aggregate principal amount of each affected series may, with a written request and reasonable indemnity, require the Trustee to act, so long as a majority in aggregate principal amount of the affected series (voting as a single class) has not directed otherwise. Individual holders’ rights to receive payment when due and to sue to enforce such payment cannot be impaired without their consent.
- Annual compliance statement: The Issuer and Guarantor must annually deliver to the Trustee a written statement indicating whether they have knowledge of any default.
- Modifications with holder consent: The Issuer, Guarantor, and Trustee may modify the Indenture or holder rights with the consent of holders of at least a majority in aggregate principal amount of each affected series. However, each affected holder must consent to changes that would: extend maturity; reduce principal, interest, or other amounts; change payment currency or related foreign currency provisions; alter payment calculation methods; reduce redemption amounts; impair the right to sue or any holder repurchase right (if applicable); lower consent thresholds; or adversely change or release the guarantee.
- Amendments without holder consent: Certain amendments are permitted to evidence mergers or trustee replacement, cure ambiguities or inconsistencies, make non-material/non-adverse changes, and for other limited purposes.
- Consolidations, mergers, and asset transfers: The Issuer and Guarantor may merge, consolidate, or transfer substantially all assets only if a U.S. successor assumes all obligations (including the guarantee for the Guarantor) and no Event of Default (or event that would become one) exists or would result immediately after the transaction.

title: Consolidations, Mergers, Sales and Transfers of Assets
heading: 37.4.9.3 Consolidations, Mergers, Sales and Transfers of Assets
start_phrase: Neither the Issuer nor the Guarantor may merge or consolidate with any other entity or sell, convey or transfer all or substantially all of their respective assets to any other entity, unless:
summary:
- Holder and trustee rights: Holders owning at least a majority in aggregate principal amount of each affected series (voting as a single class) may request the Trustee to take action with reasonable indemnity, provided no inconsistent majority direction exists (Sec. 5.06). Each holder’s right to receive due payments and to sue for enforcement cannot be impaired without that holder’s consent (Sec. 5.07). The Issuer and Guarantor must annually certify to the Trustee whether they know of any default (Sec. 3.05).
- Indenture modifications: The Issuer, Guarantor, and Trustee may modify the Indenture with consent of holders of a majority in principal amount of each affected series. Certain fundamental changes require consent of each affected holder, including extending maturity, reducing principal/interest/other amounts, changing currency or payment determination methods, reducing redemption amounts, impairing enforcement/specified repurchase rights, lowering required consent thresholds, or adversely changing/releasing the guarantee (Sec. 8.02). Amendments without holder consent are permitted for limited purposes such as mergers evidence, trustee replacement, curing ambiguities/defects, and non-material changes not adverse to holders (Sec. 8.01).
- Consolidations, mergers, and asset transfers: The Issuer and Guarantor may merge, consolidate, or sell all/substantially all assets only if the successor is a U.S. entity that assumes all obligations and no Event of Default (or potential Event of Default) exists immediately after the transaction (Secs. 9.01, 9.02). Transfers of material assets in bankruptcy or resolution proceedings are deemed sales of all or substantially all assets. There are no change-of-control, recapitalization, or highly leveraged transaction covenants; protections, if any, may be provided for specific series in a prospectus supplement.
- JPMorgan Chase guarantee: The Guarantor fully and unconditionally guarantees punctual payment of principal, interest, and other amounts when due; the guarantee is of payment, not collection (Sec. 14.01). The Guarantor is not liable for amounts the Issuer is excused from paying or amounts exceeding what is actually due, and may assert any defenses/counterclaims available to the Issuer (other than those arising solely from the Issuer’s insolvency or bankruptcy status) (Sec. 14.02).
- Trustee and agents: Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas initially serves as Trustee; The Bank of New York Mellon (and its London Branch for Euroclear/Clearstream notes) serves as paying, authenticating, registrar, and transfer agent. Given multiple roles across related securities, the Trustee may face a conflicting interest under the Trust Indenture Act upon an actual or potential default and may be required to resign, with a successor appointed.
- Governing law: The Indenture, debt securities, and guarantee are governed by New York law (Sec. 11.08).

The Guarantor will fully and unconditionally guarantee the full and punctual payment of the principal of, interest on, and all other 
amounts payable under the debt securities when the same becomes due and payable, whether at maturity, upon redemption, 
repurchase at the option of the holders of the applicable debt securities or upon acceleration.  If for any reason the Issuer does not

at the same place and in the same manner that applies to payments made by the Issuer under the 2016 Indenture.  The guarantee is

any amount of payment that the Issuer is excused from making or any amount in excess of the amount actually due and owing by the 
Issuer, and (2) any defense or counterclaims available to the Issuer (except those resulting solely from, or on account of, the Issuer’s 
insolvency or the Issuer’s status as debtor or subject of a bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding) will also be available to the Guarantor 
to the same extent as these defense or counterclaims are available to the Issuer, whether or not asserted by the Issuer. (Section 
14.02)

title: Protection-Based Vesting
heading: 38.4 Protection-Based Vesting
start_phrase: This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date(s), provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.
summary:
- Document type and scope: Exhibit outlining the Terms and Conditions for a January 17, 2023 Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) Award granted to JPMorgan Chase Operating Committee members under the Long-Term Incentive Plan; the Plan governs in case of conflict and supersedes prior related agreements.
- Acceptance mechanics: Award is effective unless declined by the specified deadline; declining cancels the award as of the Grant Date. Capitalized terms follow Plan definitions; JPMorgan Chase and its subsidiaries are referred to as the “Firm.”
- RSU form and purpose: Each RSU is a non-transferable right to one share of Common Stock at vesting; the award is intended to motivate future performance and align interests with shareholders.
- Dividend equivalents: Cash (or equivalent) payments equal to dividends on Common Stock for RSUs outstanding as of each dividend record date.
- Vesting period: Runs from Grant Date to last vesting date; the Firm may extend the vesting period or impose post-vesting restrictions on delivered shares pursuant to referenced amendment/ownership limitation provisions.
- Protection-based vesting (At Risk RSUs): Up to 50% of RSUs otherwise distributable during the vesting period may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion (subject to Compensation and Management Development Committee ratification; for CEO awards, determined by the Committee and ratified by the Board) based on:
  - Sustained underperformance of the individual or Firm versus role/Operating Committee priorities (metrics may include net income, revenue, ROE, EPS, capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income during the vesting period.
  - Cancellation of awards in a Line of Business for failing its financial threshold where the recipient had responsibility.
  - Failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
  These cancellation factors continue to apply after eligible terminations (e.g., Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability); potential acceleration may apply for Government Office due to ethics/conflict rules.
- Bonus recoupment: Award and 2022 cash incentive are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (or successor), without limiting Firm rights under that policy.
- Termination of employment: Unvested RSUs are cancelled upon termination unless specific continued vesting conditions are met.
- Continued vesting eligibility post-termination (subject to all terms, including Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Your Obligations, Remedies):
  - Job Elimination: HR determines the job was eliminated; recipient cooperates and provides requested services after notice; Release/Certification Requirements satisfied.
  - Full Career Eligibility: Voluntary termination; at least 5 years of continuous service; age + Recognized Service ≥ 60; at least 180 days’ advance written notice with cooperative service and no work for other employers during the notice period; pre-termination determination that continued vesting is appropriate based on performance and conduct; 36-month post-grant non-compete/non-practice in the recipient’s profession (government, education, and Not-for-Profit work permitted); Release/Certification Requirements satisfied. The Firm may require continued service during the 180-day period or shorten it.
text:
Protection-Based Vesting
This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date(s), provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through 
such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full 
Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.  However, vesting and the number of RSUs in which you vest are subject to 
these terms and conditions (including, but not limited to, sections captioned “ Remedies ” and the following protection-based vesting 
provision).  
Up to a total of fifty percent of your award that would otherwise be distributable to you during the vesting period (“At Risk RSUs”) 
may be cancelled if the Chief Executive Officer of JPMorgan Chase (“CEO”) determines in his or her sole discretion that cancellation of 
all or portion of the At Risk RSUs is appropriate in light of any one or a combination of the following factors:
• Your performance in relation to the priorities for your position, or the Firm’s performance in relation to the priorities for 
which you share responsibility as a member of the Operating Committee, have been unsatisfactory for a sustained period of 
time.  Among the factors the CEO may consider in assessing performance are net income, total net revenue, return on 
equity, earnings per share and capital ratios of the Firm, both on an absolute basis and, as appropriate, relative to peer 
firms. 
• For any calendar year ending during the vesting period, JPMorgan Chase’s annual pre-tax pre-provision income at the Firm level is negative.
• Awards granted to participants in a Line of Business for which you exercise, or during the vesting period exercised, direct or 
indirect responsibility, were in whole or in part cancelled because the Line of Business did not meet its annual Line of 
Business Financial Threshold.  
• The Firm does not meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
In the event that your employment terminates due to “Job Elimination”, ”Full Career Eligibility”, “Government Office” or “Disability” 
thereby entitling you to continued vesting in your award (or potentially acceleration due to satisfaction of the Government Office 
Requirements), the cancellation circumstances described above will continue to apply to your At Risk RSUs pursuant to the subsection 
captioned “Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity”.
Any determination above with respect to protection-based vesting provisions is subject to ratification by the Compensation and 
Management Development Committee of the Board of Directors of JPMorgan Chase (“Committee”).  In the case of an award to the 
CEO, all such determinations shall be made by the Committee and ratified by the Board.

start_phrase: Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, any RSUs outstanding under this award will be cancelled effective on the date your employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
summary:
- Partial terms and conditions for JPMorgan Chase At Risk RSU awards, focusing on protection-based vesting, cancellation triggers, post-termination vesting eligibility, recoupment, and employee obligations.
- Protection-based vesting/cancellations: Awards may be cancelled if a Line of Business fails its annual financial threshold or if the Firm fails the Firmwide Financial Threshold; such cancellation rules continue to apply even when vesting continues after certain terminations, including Government Office scenarios.
- Governance: Vesting protection determinations require ratification by the Compensation and Management Development Committee; for the CEO, determinations are made by the Committee and ratified by the Board.
- Bonus Recoupment: The JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy applies to both 2022 cash incentive compensation and this RSU award; the Firm’s rights under that policy are not limited by these terms.
- Termination and continued vesting: By default, unvested RSUs are cancelled upon termination. Continued vesting may apply for:
  - Job Elimination (HR determination; cooperation; execution of required release/certifications).
  - Full Career Eligibility (voluntary termination; 5+ years continuous service; age + Recognized Service ≥ 60; 180 days advance written notice and cooperation; pre-termination approval based on performance/conduct; 36-month post-grant employment restrictions—no work for a Financial Services Company or in one’s profession; permissible work for government, education, or Not-for-Profit; execution of required release/certifications).
  - Government Office (voluntary termination to accept or run for a qualifying government role; subject to Government Office Requirements).

- Employee obligations: Non-solicitation of Firm employees and customers/suppliers (including no inducing departures, no prohibited hiring shortly after separation, and no diversion of business) during employment and for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from grant date if the award remains outstanding; additional obligations include confidentiality, non-disparagement, cooperation, compliance with the Award Agreement, and adherence to any notice period policies.
text:

title: Release/Certification
heading: 38.7 Release/Certification
start_phrase: To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
summary:
- Document scope: Partial terms of an RSU Award Agreement addressing post-termination vesting eligibility, death benefits, and participant obligations/restrictions.

  - Disability: Eligibility if you cannot return to work due to long-term disability (under the Firm’s LTD Plan or equivalent/qualifying condition), contingent on: written request within 30 days of termination, required documentation, and Firm’s written consent, plus satisfaction of Release/Certification Requirements.
  - Timing note: Certain benefits/eligibility apply no earlier than meeting age and service requirements; additional advance notice may apply under the Firm’s Notice Period policy.

  - For Disability: provide required notice/documentation and obtain written consent.

text:
Release/Certification  
To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
• you must timely execute and deliver a release of claims in favor of the Firm, having such form and terms as the Firm shall 
specify,
• with respect to “Full Career Eligibility”, prior to the termination of your employment, you must confirm with management 
that you meet the eligibility criteria (including providing at least 180 days advance written notification), advise that you are 
seeking to be treated as an individual eligible for “Full Career Eligibility”, and receive written consent to such continued 
vesting,
• with respect to “Full Career Eligibility” and “Government Office”, it is your responsibility to take the appropriate steps to 
certify to the Firm prior to each vesting date while the employment restrictions are outstanding, on the authorized form of 
the Firm, that you have complied with the employment restrictions applicable to you (as described herein) from your date of 
termination of employment through the applicable vesting date,

such continued vesting, and
• in all cases, complied with all other terms of the Award Agreement.  (See section captioned “ Your Obligations ”.)

title: Death

summary:
- Covers circumstances for continued vesting of RSUs after employment ends, subject to age/service timing rules and any Notice Period policies.
- Government Office: If you resign to accept or run for an elective government position, you may qualify for continued vesting per the document’s “Government Office Requirements” and definitions.
- Disability: Continued vesting may apply if employment ends due to qualifying long-term disability (under the Firm’s LTD plan or equivalent). Requires a written request within 30 days of termination, supporting documentation, and the Firm’s written consent, plus meeting release/certification conditions.
- Release/Certification requirements for any post-termination vesting:

  - For Full Career Eligibility: before termination, confirm eligibility, give at least 180 days’ written notice, and obtain written consent.

  - For Disability: satisfy notice/documentation and receive written consent.
  - Comply with all other Award Agreement terms.
- Death: Unvested RSUs vest immediately; shares (net of taxes) are distributed to the designated beneficiary or estate, no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death (administrative practice targets registration within 60 days after required documentation), subject to local law.

text:
Death
If you die while you are eligible to vest in RSUs under this award, the RSUs will immediately vest and will be distributed in shares of 
Common Stock (after applicable tax withholding) to your designated beneficiary on file with the Firm’s Stock Administration 
Department, or if no beneficiary has been designated or survives you or if beneficiary designation is not recognized locally, then to 
your estate unless otherwise required by local legislation.  Any shares will be distributed no later than the end of the calendar year 
immediately following the calendar year which contains your date of death; however, our administrative practice is to register such 
shares in the name of your beneficiary or estate within 60 days of the Firm’s receipt of any required documentation.

start_phrase: During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date,
summary:
- Outlines scenarios for continued vesting of RSUs after employment ends, including:
  - Government Office: Eligibility to continue vesting if leaving to accept or run for a government office, subject to defined “Government Office Requirements.”
  - Disability: Continued vesting if unable to return to work under an LTD Plan or equivalent, with written request within 30 days, supporting documentation, and Firm consent.

text:
Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment 
or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date, you will not directly or 
indirectly, whether on your own behalf or on behalf of any other party, without the prior written consent of the Director of Human 
Resources: (i) solicit, induce or encourage any of the Firm’s then current employees to leave the Firm or to apply for employment 
elsewhere, unless such current employee has received official, written notice that his or her employment will be terminated due to 
job elimination, (ii) hire any employee or former employee who was employed by the Firm at the date your employment terminated, 
unless the individual’s employment terminated because his or her job was eliminated, or the individual’s employment with the Firm 
has been terminated for more than six months, (iii) to the fullest extent enforceable under applicable law, solicit or induce or attempt 
to induce to leave the Firm, or divert or attempt to divert from doing business with the Firm, any then current customers, suppliers or other persons or entities that were serviced by you or whose names became known to you by virtue of your employment with the 
Firm, or otherwise interfere with the relationship between the Firm and such customers, suppliers or other persons or entities.  This 
does not apply to publicly known institutional customers that you service after your employment with the Firm without the use of the 
Firm’s confidential or proprietary information. 
These restrictions do not apply to authorized actions you take in the normal course of your employment with the Firm, such as 
employment decisions with respect to employees you supervise or business referrals in accordance with the Firm’s policies.

title: Confidential Information
heading: 38.9.2 Confidential Information
start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, directly or indirectly (i) use or disclose to anyone any confidential information related to the Firm’s business, or (ii) communicate with the press or other media

Preserves rights to report suspected legal/Code violations to management, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts and to respond truthfully in legal/regulatory matters.
- Non-disparagement commitment during and after employment, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful participation in investigations or proceedings.
- Cooperation duty to assist the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, and governmental proceedings, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
- Compliance and disclosure: obligation to provide information to verify compliance with the Award Agreement; authorization for the Firm to disclose Award Agreement terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.

text:
Confidential Information
You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, directly or indirectly (i) use or disclose to anyone any 
confidential information related to the Firm’s business, or (ii) communicate with the press or other media about matters related to 
the Firm, its customers or employees, including matters and activities relating to your employment, or the employment of others, by 
the Firm, in the case of either (i) or (ii), except as explicitly permitted by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct and applicable policies 
or law or legal process.  In addition, following your termination of employment, you will not, without prior written authorization, 
access the Firm’s private and internal information through telephonic, intranet or internet means.  “Confidential information” shall 
have the same meaning for the Award Agreement as it has in the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct.  
Nothing in this award precludes you from reporting to the Firm’s management or directors, the government, a regulator, a self-
regulatory agency, your attorneys or a court, conduct you believe to be in violation of the law or concerns of any known or suspected 
Code of Conduct violation.  It is also not intended to prevent you from responding truthfully to questions or requests from the 
government, a regulator or in a court of law.

title: Non-Disparagement

start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, make or encourage others to make any public statement or release any information in verbal, written, electronic or any other form,

Notice Period 
If you are subject to a notice period or become subject to a notice period after the Grant Date, whether by contract or by policy, 
that requires you to provide advance written notice of your intention to terminate your employment (“Notice Period”), then as 
consideration for this award and continued employment, you will provide the Firm with the necessary advance written notice that 
applies to you, as specified by such contract or policy.  
After receipt of your notice, the Firm may choose to have you continue to provide services during the applicable Notice Period or 
may place you on a paid leave for all or part of the applicable Notice Period.  During the Notice Period, you shall continue to devote 
your full time and loyalty to the Firm by providing services in a cooperative and professional manner and not perform any services for 
any other employer and shall receive your base salary and certain benefits until your employment terminates.  You and the Firm may 
mutually agree to waive or modify the length of the Notice Period. 
Regardless of whether a Notice Period applies to you, you must comply with the 180-day advance notice period described under 
the subsection captioned “--Full Career Eligibility” in the event you wish to terminate employment under that same subsection.

title: Remedies - Introduction
heading: 38.10 Remedies
start_phrase: In addition to the cancellation provisions described under the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus Recoupment ”, and “ Termination of Employment ”, up to 100% of your outstanding RSUs under this award may be cancelled if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
summary: Outlines JPMorgan Chase’s remedies allowing cancellation of up to 100% of outstanding RSUs for detrimental or risk-related conduct and other breaches, in addition to provisions under Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, and Termination of Employment. Triggers include conduct causing material financial or reputational harm; awards based on materially inaccurate performance metrics (regardless of fault) or on the recipient’s material misrepresentation; improper or grossly negligent failure to timely identify, raise, or assess material risks; termination for Cause (or a post-termination determination that Cause existed); failure to comply with advance notice/cooperation and employment restrictions tied to termination; failure to return required Release/Certification forms by the deadline; or violation of “Your Obligations.” The Firm may suspend vesting and/or share distribution while evaluating cancellation/recovery or distribution conditions, is not liable for price fluctuations during suspension, and may reinstate suspended units per Plan procedures, with references to “Amendment,” “Definitions,” and “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations.”
text:
Remedies
 
• Detrimental Conduct, Risk Related and Other Cancellation/Recapture 
In addition to the cancellation provisions described under the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus 
Recoupment ”,  and “ Termination of Employment ”, up to 100% of your outstanding RSUs under this award may be cancelled if the 
Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
• Any of the following detrimental and risk-related conduct has occurred:
◦ you engaged in conduct detrimental to the Firm insofar as it causes material financial or reputational harm to the 
Firm or its business activities, or
◦ this award was based on materially inaccurate performance metrics, whether or not you were responsible for the 
inaccuracy, or
◦ this award was based on a material misrepresentation by you, or
◦ you improperly or with gross negligence failed to identify, raise or assess, in a timely manner and as reasonably 
expected, risks and/or concerns with respect to risks material to the Firm or its business activities, or
◦ your employment was terminated for Cause (see section captioned “ Definitions ” below) or, in the case of a 
determination after the termination of your employment, that your employment could have been terminated for 
Cause. 
• you have failed to comply with any of the advance notice/cooperation requirements or employment restrictions applicable to 
your termination of employment, or
• you have failed to return the required forms specified under the section captioned “ Release/Certification ” by the specified 
deadline, or
• you have violated any of the provisions as set forth above in the section captioned “ Your Obligations ”.
To the extent provided under the subsection captioned “--Amendment” below, JPMorgan Chase reserves the right to suspend 
vesting of this award and/or distribution of shares under this award, including, without limitation, during any period that JPMorgan 
Chase is evaluating whether this award is subject to cancellation and/or recovery and/or whether the conditions for distributions of 
shares under this award are satisfied.  JPMorgan Chase is not responsible for any price fluctuations during any period of suspension 
and, if applicable, suspended units will be reinstated consistent with Plan administration procedures. See also subsection captioned 
“--No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations”.

title: Recovery
heading: 38.10.1 Recovery
start_phrase: In addition, you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market Value (determined as of the applicable vesting date) of the gross number of shares of Common Stock previously distributed under this award as follows:
summary:
- Sets out JPMorgan Chase’s right to cancel up to 100% of outstanding RSUs for detrimental or risk-related conduct, including: causing material financial or reputational harm; awards based on materially inaccurate metrics (regardless of fault) or your misrepresentation; failure to timely identify/raise material risks; termination for Cause (or that termination could have been for Cause); failure to meet advance notice/cooperation or post-employment restrictions; failure to return required Release/Certification forms; or violation of “Your Obligations.”
- Allows the Firm to suspend vesting and/or share distributions while it evaluates cancellation, recovery, or distribution conditions; the Firm isn’t liable for market fluctuations during suspension, and suspended units may be reinstated per plan procedures; subject to other ownership/limitations provisions.
- Establishes recovery (clawback) of up to the Fair Market Value of previously distributed shares:
  - Within three years before a notice-of-recovery for fraud, knowing and willful misconduct, violations of “Your Obligations,” or violations of post-employment restrictions (Full Career Eligibility or Government Office).
  - Within one year before a notice-of-recovery for specified detrimental and risk-related conduct.
- Defines notice-of-recovery (including electronic notice) and deems good-faith delivery to the last known address sufficient; a notice that the Firm is evaluating recovery preserves its rights, and completion of the evaluation is at the Firm’s discretion.
- Clarifies tax treatment: “distributed” includes shares withheld for taxes, but the intent is to seek repayment only for shares effectively retained after taxes; no repayment required for amounts representing irrevocable tax withholdings or unrecoverable tax payments, as determined by the Firm or its nominee.
- Permits repayment in shares or cash; characterizes repayment as a lawful recovery, not a penalty; states these provisions do not limit separate “Bonus Recoupment” obligations.
text:
Recovery
In addition, you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market Value (determined as of the 
applicable vesting date) of the gross number of shares of Common Stock previously distributed under this award as follows:
• Payment may be required with respect to any shares distributed within the three year period prior to a notice-of-recovery 
under this section, if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
◦ you committed a fraudulent act, or engaged in knowing and willful misconduct related to your employment, or
◦ you violated any of the provisions as set forth above in the section captioned “ Your Obligations ”, or
◦ you violated the employment restrictions set forth in the subsection “--Full Career Eligibility” or “--Government 
Office” following the termination of your employment.
• In addition, payment may be required with respect to any shares distributed within the one year period prior to notice-of-
recovery under this section, if the Firm in its sole discretion determines appropriate as a result of the detrimental and risk-
related conduct listed in the above “Detrimental Conduct, Risk Related and Other Cancellation/Recapture” subsection.  
Notice-of-recovery under this subsection is a written (including electronic) notice from the Firm to you either requiring payment 
under this subsection or stating that JPMorgan Chase is evaluating requiring payment under this subsection.  Without limiting the 
foregoing, notice-of-recovery will be deemed provided if the Firm makes a good faith attempt to provide written (including 
electronic) notice at your last known address maintained in the Firm’s employment records.  For the avoidance of doubt, a notice-of-
recovery that the Firm is evaluating requiring payment under this subsection shall preserve JPMorgan Chase’s rights to require 
payment as set forth above in all respects and the Firm shall be under no obligation to complete its evaluation other than as the Firm 
may determine in its sole discretion.
For purposes of this subsection, shares distributed under this award include shares withheld for tax purposes.  However, it is the 
Firm’s intention that you only be required to pay the amounts under this subsection with respect to shares that are or may be 
retained by you following a determination of tax liability and that you will not be required to pay amounts with respect to shares 
representing irrevocable tax withholdings or tax payments previously made (whether by you or the Firm) that you will not be able to 
recover, recapture or reclaim (including as a tax credit, refund or other benefit).  Accordingly, JPMorgan Chase will not require you to 
pay any amount that the Firm or its nominee in his or her sole discretion determines is represented by such withholdings or tax 
payments.
Payment may be made in shares of Common Stock or in cash.  You agree that any repayment will be a lawful recovery under the 
terms and conditions of your Award Agreement and is not to be construed in any manner as a penalty.  
Nothing in the section in any way limits your obligations under “ Bonus Recoupment ”.•

title: Right to an Injunction

start_phrase: You acknowledge that a violation or attempted violation of the obligations set forth herein will cause immediate and irreparable damage to the Firm, and therefore agree that the Firm shall be entitled as a matter of right to an injunction, from any court of competent jurisdiction, restraining any violation or further violation of such obligations; such right to an injunction, however, shall be cumulative and in addition to whatever other remedies the Firm may have under law or equity.
summary:

- Right to set off: The firm may use vested shares or funds to satisfy debts you owe the firm (subject to applicable law and Section 409A), but will not recover amounts from your funds or unrestricted securities held at the firm without your consent, except for certain accounts referenced under other limitations.
- No ownership rights before vesting: RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until shares are issued post-vesting; the firm may open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares.
- Suspension/cancellation and restrictions: RSUs may be suspended or canceled per referenced provisions (Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment, Remedies, Amendment). The firm may impose post-vesting restrictions on transfer, sale, pledging, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares (voting/dividend rights remain). If recovery applies during a restricted period, you may owe the firm up to the FMV of the gross restricted shares.
- Binding agreement: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- Not an employment contract: Employment remains at-will; no promise of future awards; award value does not count for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A; includes conditions affecting specified employees upon separation from service, addressing distributions that could occur within six months (details truncated).

text:
Administrative Provisions  
Withholding Taxes : As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the 
number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary 
procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares, 
dividend equivalents and the award.  This may include but is not limited to (i) a market sale of a number of such shares on your 
behalf substantially equal to the withholding or other taxes, (ii) to the extent required by law, withhold from cash compensation, an 
amount equal to any withholding obligation with respect to the award, shares that vest under this award, and/or dividend 
equivalents, and (iii) retaining shares that vest under this award or dividend equivalents until you pay any taxes associated with the 
award, vested shares and/or the dividend equivalents directly to the competent authorities.

No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations :  RSUs do not convey the rights of ownership of Common Stock and do not carry voting

but not limited to, restricting the sale, transfer, pledging, assignment, hedging or encumbrance of such shares of Common Stock. 
Such restrictions described in the last sentence shall not impact your right to vote or receive dividends with respect to the Common

- Establishes the Firm’s right to seek immediate injunctive relief for any violation of award obligations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Details tax withholding procedures, allowing the Firm to withhold or sell shares, withhold from cash compensation, or retain vested shares/dividend equivalents to satisfy tax liabilities.
- Grants the Firm a right of set-off against vested shares/funds to satisfy debts owed by the employee, with limits on recoupment from certain unrestricted accounts without consent.
- Clarifies that RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until vesting; authorizes the Firm to open brokerage/book-entry accounts and deliver vested shares; permits suspension and cancellation of RSUs per referenced provisions.
- Allows the Firm to impose post-vesting restrictions (e.g., transfer, sale, pledge, hedge limits) and require repayment up to the fair market value of restricted shares if recovery provisions apply.
- States the Award Agreement is binding on JPMorgan Chase successors.
- Confirms employment is at-will; the award is not an employment contract, offers no right to future awards, and is not severance compensation.
- Affirms compliance intent with Section 409A; includes six-month payment delay for specified employees after separation, and defines payment timing for vested shares and dividend equivalents where applicable.
- Provides for equitable adjustments to RSUs in the event of corporate actions (splits, dividends, mergers, recapitalizations, etc.).
- Vests sole authority in the Committee to interpret and administer the award, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment and recovery provisions, decide claims, delegate authority, and make non-uniform determinations.
- Reserves the Committee’s right to amend the Award Agreement, with limits on materially adverse changes without consent except to comply with law, accounting rules, or to adjust vesting dates/impose restrictions consistent with Section 409A; amendments require HR Director’s signature.
- Includes severability and reformation of unenforceable provisions to make them enforceable.
- Permits accelerated distribution if required by government ethics/conflict-of-interest rules (subject to 409A), with rules for terminations under Government Office Requirements, Job Elimination, or Full Career Eligibility; accelerated awards remain subject to original recovery and employment restrictions.
- Acknowledges processing and disclosure of personal data to administer the award, including to service providers and tax/regulatory authorities.
text:
Section 409A Compliance :  To the extent that Section 409A of the Code is applicable to this award, distributions of shares and cash 
hereunder are intended to comply with Section 409A of the Code, and the Award Agreement, including these terms and conditions, 
shall be interpreted in a manner consistent with such intent.
Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, if you (i) are subject to taxation under the Code, (ii) are a specified employee as 
defined in the JPMorgan Chase 2005 Deferred Compensation Plan and (iii) have incurred a  separation from service (as defined in 
that Plan with the exception of death) and if any units/shares under this award represent deferred compensation as defined in 
Section 409A and such shares are distributable (under the terms of this award) within six months following, and as a result of your separation from service, then those shares will be delivered to you during the first calendar month after the expiration of six full 
months from date of your separation from service.  Further, if your award is not subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture as defined 
by regulations issued under Section 409A of the Code, then the remainder of each calendar year immediately following (i) each 
applicable vesting date set forth in your Award Agreement shall be a payment date for purposes of distributing the vested portion of 
the award and (ii) each date that JPMorgan Chase specifies for payment of dividends declared on its Common Stock, shall be the 
payment date(s) for purposes of distributing dividend equivalent payments.

title: Change in Outstanding Shares
heading: 38.11.6 Change in Outstanding Shares
start_phrase: In the event of any change in the outstanding shares of Common Stock by reason of any stock dividend or split, recapitalization, issuance of a new class of common stock, merger, consolidation, spin-off, combination or exchange of shares or other similar corporate change, or any distributions to stockholders of Common Stock other than regular cash dividends, the Committee will make an equitable substitution or proportionate adjustment, in the number or kind of shares of Common Stock or other securities issued or reserved for issuance pursuant to the Plan and to any RSUs outstanding under this award for such corporate events.
summary:
- Distribution timing and Section 409A: If you separate from service, delivery of shares may be delayed until the first calendar month after six full months post-separation to comply with Section 409A. If the award is no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, vested portions are paid on payment dates within the same calendar year following each vesting date, and dividend equivalents are paid on JPMorgan Chase’s dividend payment dates.
- Adjustments for corporate actions: In the event of stock splits/dividends, recapitalizations, new class issuance, mergers, consolidations, spin‑offs, share exchanges, or other similar events (excluding regular cash dividends), the Committee will make equitable substitutions or proportionate adjustments to shares or securities under the plan and outstanding RSUs.
- Administration and interpretation: The Committee has sole authority to interpret the plan and this award, determine termination reasons, apply post-employment and clawback provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority. Its (and the Firm’s/HR’s) determinations are binding and need not be uniform; selective, non‑uniform decisions and modifications are permitted.
- Amendment rights: The Committee (or nominee) may amend the Award Agreement at any time for any reason. No material adverse change without your consent, except as deemed advisable to comply with laws/regulations/accounting rules or to change vesting dates/impose certain restrictions consistent with Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing signed by the Director of Human Resources.
- Severability/reformation: If any portion is unenforceable, the Firm, a court/arbitrator, or the HR Director may reform it (e.g., duration, geography, scope) to make it enforceable under applicable law.
- Accelerated distribution for government ethics/conflicts: If required by applicable ethics/conflict‑of‑interest rules due to government employment, the Firm may accelerate distribution to meet divestiture deadlines, provided it does not violate Section 409A. Acceleration does not alter clawback/recovery timeframes (which track original vesting/distribution dates).
- Termination scenarios and acceleration scope: After voluntary termination meeting “Government Office Requirements,” acceleration applies to the portion that would continue to vest. If the award remains outstanding due to job elimination or full career eligibility, acceleration may apply to the full outstanding award.
- Continuing obligations after acceleration: Even if accelerated, you remain subject to all original award terms as if unaccelerated, including repayment (“Remedies”) and employment restrictions (“Protection‑Based Vesting,” “Government Office Requirements,” and “Full Career Eligibility”).
- Personal data use: By accepting the award, you consent to the Firm processing and disclosing your personal data to administer the award (e.g., share/unit registration, brokerage account setup) and to third parties such as service providers or tax/regulatory authorities for reporting and payroll.

title: Governing Law
heading: 38.11.12 Governing Law
start_phrase: This award shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts of law principles.
summary:
- Consent and data handling: Employee authorizes the firm to collect/process personal data (including for tax withholding) and transfer it internationally, potentially to jurisdictions with lower protections; revocation is allowed except for tax/regulatory purposes, but doing so cancels the award.
- Governing law: New York law applies, without regard to conflicts-of-law rules.
- Forum selection and arbitration: Disputes related to the award/Plan may be compelled to arbitration under AAA rules at the firm’s sole discretion; otherwise, exclusive jurisdiction and venue lie in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, with waivers of objections to personal jurisdiction and venue and agreement not to sue elsewhere.
- Waiver of jury and class claims: All claims must be brought on an individual basis; jury trial and participation in class, collective, representative, or joint actions are waived.
- Litigation costs: In firm-initiated actions to enforce the award where the firm prevails, the employee must pay the firm’s reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses; no right to fee advancement or indemnification under the firm’s by-laws in such suits.
- Non-transferability: RSU awards and related rights cannot be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, or subjected to liens; transfer is permitted only upon death via will, laws of descent, or a beneficiary designation with the firm.
- Application to existing awards: The stated administrative provisions apply to and amend all RSU awards outstanding as of the document date.
- Definition of “Cause”: Termination for reasons including legal/regulatory violations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, material policy/code of conduct violations or related misconduct, grossly inadequate performance or refusal to follow directives, or acts harmful to the firm’s interests or relationships.
- Definition of “Financial Services Company”: Broadly covers enterprises engaged in banking (including internet and payments), insurance, financial/investment/economic advisory and related services (e.g., investment banking, brokerage, asset/investment management, FX, hedge funds), issuance/trading/sale of asset-backed or derivative instruments, fintech (including blockchain and financial product/service offerings), private equity/real estate advising or investing, and similar activities as determined by HR leadership.

text:
Definitions
“Cause ” means a determination by the Firm that your employment terminated as a result of your (i) violation of any law, rule or 
regulation (including rules of self-regulatory bodies) related to the Firm’s business, (ii) indictment or conviction of a felony, (iii) 
commission of a fraudulent act, (iv) violation of the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct or other Firm policies or misconduct related to 
your duties to the Firm (other than immaterial and inadvertent violations or misconduct), (v) grossly inadequate performance of the 
duties associated with your position or job function or failure to follow reasonable directives of your manager, or (vi) any act or 
failure to act that is injurious to the interests of the Firm or its relationship with a customer, client or an employee.
“Financial Services Company ” means a business enterprise that engages in  any of the following services (itself or through an affiliate 
or subsidiary), regardless of whether such services are the principle strategy or revenue-generating activity:
• commercial or retail banking, including, but not limited to, commercial, institutional and personal trust, custody and/or 
lending and processing services, internet banking, originating and servicing mortgages, issuing and servicing credit cards, 
payment servicing or processing or merchant services,
• insurance, including but not limited to, guaranteeing against loss, harm, damage, illness, disability or death, providing and 
issuing annuities, acting as principal, agent or broker for purpose of the forgoing,
• financial, investment or economic advisory services, including but not limited to, investment banking services (such as 
advising on mergers or dispositions, underwriting, dealing in, or making a market in securities or other similar activities), 
brokerage services, investment management services, asset management services, foreign exchange services, interbank 
networks and hedge funds,
• issuing, trading or selling instruments representing interests in pools of assets or in derivatives instruments, 
• financial technology companies, such as those selling blockchain services, or offering or selling financial products/services,
• advising on, or investing in, private equity or real estate funds or ventures, or
• any similar activities that the Director of Human Resources or nominee determines in his or her sole discretion constitute financial services.
“Firmwide Financial Threshold” means a cumulative return on tangible common equity for calendar years 2023, 2024 and 2025 of 
not less than 15%.  Cumulative return on tangible common equity means (i) the sum of the Firm’s reported net income for all three 
calendar years, divided by (ii) reported year-end tangible equity averaged over the three years.
“Government Office” means (i) a full-time position in an elected or appointed office in local, state, or federal government (including 
equivalent positions outside the U.S. or in a supranational organization), not reasonably anticipated to be a full-career position, or (ii) 
conducting a bona fide full-time campaign for such an elective public office after formally filing for candidacy, where it is customary 
and reasonably necessary to campaign full-time for the office.
“Line of Business” means a business unit of the Firm (or one or more business units designated below under the definition “Line of 
Business Financial Threshold” of the Corporate Investment Bank).  All Corporate Functions (including the functions of the Chief 
Investment Office) are considered a single Line of Business.
“Line of Business Financial Threshold” means the financial threshold set forth below for the following Lines of Business based on 
the Firm’s management reporting system:
Asset & Wealth Management Annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income1
Card and Auto Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income2
Commercial Banking Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income2
Corporate Investment Bank Annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income1 for CIB overall or annual negative 
allocated product revenues (excluding XVA) for: 
• Fixed Income
• Equities
• Securities Services
• Global Investment Banking
• Payments
Consumer Banking, J.P. Morgan Wealth 
Management and Business Banking Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income2
Corporate Functions (including Chief 
Investment Office) Annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income1 at the Firm level
Home Lending Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income2
1Pre-tax pre-provision income means Revenue less Expenses2Pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income means Revenue less (Expenses plus Net Charge-offs)
“Not-for-Profit Organization” means an entity exempt from tax under state law and under Section 501(c)(3) of the Code.  Section 
501(c)(3) only includes entities organized and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific, testing for public safety, 
literary or educational purposes, or to foster national or international amateur sports competition or for the prevention of cruelty to 
children or animals. Not-for-Profit Organization  shall also mean entities outside the United States exempt from local and national tax 
laws because they are organized and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific, testing for public safety, literary or 
educational purposes, or to foster national or international amateur sports competition or for the prevention of cruelty to children or 
animals.
“Recognized Service” means the period of service as an employee set forth in the Firm’s applicable service-related policies.

title: Eligibility
heading: 38.13.1 Eligibility
start_phrase: Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
summary:
- Context: Partial section of a financial-services firm’s employee equity/award agreement outlining defined terms, performance thresholds, and rules for continued vesting when an employee resigns to enter government service.

- Key definitions:
  - Firmwide Financial Threshold: Cumulative return on tangible common equity of at least 15% across calendar years 2023–2025, calculated as total net income over the three years divided by average year-end tangible equity over the same period.
  - Government Office: Full-time elected or appointed public office (including outside the U.S. or supranational roles) not intended as a full-career position, or a bona fide full-time campaign after formal filing where full-time campaigning is customary.
  - Line of Business (LoB): A business unit of the firm; Corporate Functions (including the Chief Investment Office) are treated as one LoB.
  - Line of Business Financial Thresholds: Performance triggers, based on management reporting, defined as:
    - Asset & Wealth Management: Annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income (PTPP).
    - Card and Auto; Commercial Banking; Consumer Banking, J.P. Morgan Wealth Management and Business Banking; Home Lending: Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income (PTPLLRI).
    - Corporate Investment Bank (CIB): Annual negative PTPP for CIB overall, or annual negative allocated product revenues (excluding XVA) for Fixed Income, Equities, Securities Services, Global Investment Banking, Payments.
    - Corporate Functions (incl. CIO): Annual negative PTPP at the Firm level.
    - PTPP = Revenue minus Expenses; PTPLLRI = Revenue minus (Expenses + Net Charge-offs).
  - Not-for-Profit Organization: U.S. Section 501(c)(3) entities and foreign equivalents organized exclusively for specified charitable, religious, educational, scientific, public safety testing, amateur sports, or cruelty-prevention purposes.
  - Recognized Service: Employee service as determined under the firm’s service-related policies.

- Government Office Requirements (continued vesting policy upon resignation for government service or candidacy):
  - Full Career Eligibility carve-out: If an employee qualifies for Full Career Eligibility at resignation, this section does not apply.
  - Eligibility conditions for continued vesting:
    - Provide at least 60 days’ advance written notice; cooperate professionally during notice; do not work for another employer during this period (firm may shorten the notice).
    - Confirm, in a form acceptable to the firm, that continued vesting complies with law/regulation.
    - Provide satisfactory documentation that resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate.
  - Portion of awards eligible for continued vesting (the “CV Award”):
    - 50% with ≥3 and <4 years of continuous service.
    - 75% with ≥4 and <5 years.
    - 100% with ≥5 years.
    - The non-eligible portion is canceled at termination.
  - Conditions to retain continued vesting:
    - Non-elective Government Office: Serve two or more years post-termination to receive the full CV Award; if service is shorter than two years, only tranches vesting during the service period are retained.
    - Elective office campaign: Employee’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot.
  - Satisfaction of conditions:
    - If the above conditions are met (including if not elected after appearing on the ballot), any then-outstanding CV Awards continue to vest on the original schedule, subject to the same terms and employment restrictions as if the employee had resigned with Full Career Eligibility. References an “Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity” provision for cases requiring accelerated share delivery.
  - Failure to satisfy conditions:
    - Outstanding RSUs under the CV Award are canceled.
    - Clawback: Repayment of the Fair Market Value (measured at distribution date, before withholding) of shares previously distributed that would otherwise have remained outstanding as RSUs but for accelerated distribution due to government ethics/conflict requirements.

- Notes:
  - Thresholds and results are aligned with the firm’s management reporting.
  - Employment restrictions continue to apply during the vesting period for CV Awards.
  - The document references additional sections (e.g., accelerated distribution for government ethics/conflicts, Full Career Eligibility) not fully included here.
text:
Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
• At least 60 days’ advance written notice of your intention to resign to accept or pursue a Government Office (see section 
captioned “ Definitions ”), during which period you must perform in a cooperative and professional manner services 
requested by the Firm and not provide services for any other employer.  The Firm may elect to shorten this notice period at 
the Firm’s sole discretion.
• Confirmation, in a form of satisfactory to the firm, that vesting in this award pursuant to this provision would not violate any 
applicable law, regulation or rule. • Documentation in a form satisfactory to the Firm that your resignation is for the purpose of accepting a Government Office 
or becoming a candidate for a Government Office. (See Section captioned “Definitions”.)

title: Portion of Your Awards Subject to Continued Vesting
heading: 38.13.2 Portion of Your Awards Subject to Continued Vesting
start_phrase: Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of your outstanding awards that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s original schedule will be based on your years of continuous service completed with the Firm immediately preceding your termination date, as follows:
summary:
- Requires documentation acceptable to the Firm that the resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate.
- Defines the portion of outstanding awards that continue to vest (the “CV Award”) based on continuous service at termination: 50% for 3–<4 years, 75% for 4–<5 years, 100% for 5+ years; the remainder is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to retain CV Awards:
  - Non-elective Government Office: serve 2+ years post-termination to receive full CV Award; if service is under 2 years, you keep only the portions scheduled to vest during your government service.
  - Elective office campaign: your name must appear on the primary or final ballot.
- If conditions are satisfied (2+ years in office, or on the ballot and not elected), any outstanding CV Awards—and awards that would have been outstanding but for ethics/conflict-driven accelerated distributions—continue to be subject, for the remaining vesting period, to the same terms as a resignation with Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions during vesting.

text:
Portion of Your Awards Subject to Continued Vesting :
Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of your outstanding awards that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s 
original schedule will be based on your years of continuous service completed with the Firm immediately preceding your termination 
date, as follows:
• 50% if you have at least 3 but less than 4 years of continuous service,
• 75% if you have at least 4 but less than 5 years of continuous service, or
• 100% if you have 5 or more years of continuous service.
The portion of each award subject to continued vesting above is referred to as the “CV Award” and the portion not subject to 
continued vesting will be cancelled on the date your employment terminates.

start_phrase: This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date(s), provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.

- Document sets terms for a January 17, 2023 Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) award under the JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan for Operating Committee members; the Plan governs in case of conflict and, with the Prospectus, supersedes prior agreements.
