text:
Protection-Based Vesting
This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date(s), provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through 
such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full 
Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.  However, vesting and the number of RSUs in which you vest are subject to 
these terms and conditions (including, but not limited to, sections captioned “ Remedies ” and the following protection-based vesting 
provision).  
Up to a total of fifty percent of your award that would otherwise be distributable to you during the vesting period (“At Risk RSUs”) 
may be cancelled if the Chief Executive Officer of JPMorgan Chase (“CEO”) determines in his or her sole discretion that cancellation of 
all or portion of the At Risk RSUs is appropriate in light of any one or a combination of the following factors:
• Your performance in relation to the priorities for your position, or the Firm’s performance in relation to the priorities for 
which you share responsibility as a member of the Operating Committee, have been unsatisfactory for a sustained period of 
time.  Among the factors the CEO may consider in assessing performance are net income, total net revenue, return on 
equity, earnings per share and capital ratios of the Firm, both on an absolute basis and, as appropriate, relative to peer 
firms. 
• For any calendar year ending during the vesting period, JPMorgan Chase’s annual pre-tax pre-provision income at the Firm 
level is negative.
• Awards granted to participants in a Line of Business for which you exercise, or during the vesting period exercised, direct or 
indirect responsibility, were in whole or in part cancelled because the Line of Business did not meet its annual Line of 
Business Financial Threshold.  
• The Firm does not meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.In the event that your employment terminates due to “Job Elimination”, ”Full Career Eligibility”, “Government Office” or “Disability” 
thereby entitling you to continued vesting in your award (or potentially acceleration due to satisfaction of the Government Office 
Requirements), the cancellation circumstances described above will continue to apply to your At Risk RSUs pursuant to the subsection 
captioned “Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity”.
Any determination above with respect to protection-based vesting provisions is subject to ratification by the Compensation and 
Management Development Committee of the Board of Directors of JPMorgan Chase (“Committee”).  In the case of an award to the 
CEO, all such determinations shall be made by the Committee and ratified by the Board.

EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff
In consideration of grant of this award, and without prejudice to any other provision of this Award Agreement, you agree that you are 
subject to the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff (and any applicable supplement(s) to that policy) or 
successor policy as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance 
year 2022 and to this award. 
The provisions of the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff set out the terms and conditions applying to 
the grant of this award which ensure that the Firm is able to meet its regulatory obligations to operate malus (reduce) and/or 
clawback (recover) to awards in certain circumstances.  These include, but are not limited to, where (i) there is a material downturn 
in the Firm’s financial performance or (ii) where the Firm is required to hold more capital. The circumstances in which the events at 
(i) and (ii) would occur are analogous to some of the circumstances considered under the existing Firmwide terms and conditions, in 
particular the Bonus Recoupment Policy and the Protection Based Vesting provisions.  You can access this policy as currently in effect

title: Termination of Employment
heading: 38.22 Termination of Employment
start_phrase: Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, any RSUs outstanding under this award will be cancelled effective on the date your employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
summary:
Summary of main points in the partial document:

- Scope and governance: Sets terms for JPMorgan Chase RSU awards, including protection-based vesting. Any determinations on such vesting are subject to Compensation and Management Development Committee ratification; for the CEO, by the Committee and ratified by the Board.

- Interaction with government-related employment: If employment ends due to Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability, cancellation rules for At Risk RSUs still apply, including potential accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons tied to Government employment.

- Holding requirement: On each vest date, vested RSUs are distributed at fair market value net of tax withholding, then held in a restricted, non-transferable account for 12 months; these restrictions lapse upon death.

- Bonus Recoupment Policy: Award and 2022 cash incentive are subject to JPMorgan Chase’s Bonus Recoupment Policy; nothing in the award limits the Firm’s rights under that policy.

- EMEA Malus and Clawback (Identified Staff): Award and 2022 cash incentive are subject to malus/clawback provisions permitting reduction or recovery, including in a material firm performance downturn or increased capital needs; aligns with Firmwide recoupment and protection-based vesting terms.

- General termination rule: RSUs cancel upon employment termination unless specifically covered under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death. Any continued vesting remains subject to protection-based vesting, recoupment, EMEA malus/clawback, and other obligations/remedies.

- Continued vesting—Job Elimination: Requires HR determination that the role was eliminated, cooperative/professional transition services, and satisfaction of release/certification requirements.

- Continued vesting—Full Career Eligibility: Requires voluntary termination; at least 5 years continuous service; 15+ years Recognized Service or 30+ combined Recognized Service and external experience; at least 180 days advance written notice with cooperative service and no outside work during notice; a pre-termination appropriateness determination based on performance/conduct; 36 months post-grant restriction on working for a Financial Services Company or in one’s profession (government/education/not-for-profit permitted); and release/certification. The Firm may require continued service during the notice period or shorten it (not earlier than service requirement); additional notice policies may apply.

- Continued vesting—Government Office: Applies when voluntarily leaving to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to the Government Office Requirements and definitions.

- Continued vesting—Disability: Applies if termination is due to qualifying long-term disability (under the Firm’s LTD plan or equivalent, or would qualify), with a written request within 30 days, supporting documentation, Firm consent, and release/certification.

- Release/Certification requirements: Include executing a release of claims; for Full Career, pre-termination confirmation of eligibility and written consent; for Full Career and Government Office, ongoing certification of compliance with employment restrictions before each vest; for Disability, timely notice/documentation and consent; and compliance with all other award obligations.

- Death: If death occurs while eligible to vest, RSUs immediately vest and are distributed (net of withholding) to the designated beneficiary; restrictions on held distributions also lapse upon death.
text:
Termination of Employment
Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government 
Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, any RSUs outstanding under this award will be cancelled effective on 
the date your employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
Subject to these terms and conditions (including, but not limited to, sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus 
Recoupment ”,  “ EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff ”, “Your Obligations ” and “ Remedies ”), you will be eligible to 
continue to vest (as you otherwise would vest if you were still employed by JPMorgan Chase) with respect to your award in 
accordance with its terms and conditions following the termination of your employment if one of the following circumstances applies 
to you:
• Job Elimination 
In the event that the Director of Human Resources or nominee in his or her sole discretion determines that
◦ the Firm terminated your employment because your job was eliminated, and 
◦ after you are notified that your job will be eliminated, you provided such services as requested by the Firm in a cooperative 
and professional manner, and
◦ you satisfied the Release/Certification Requirements set forth below.
• Full Career Eligibility In the event that the Director of Human Resources or nominee in his or her sole discretion determines that
◦ you voluntarily terminated your employment with the Firm, had completed at least five years of continuous service with the 
Firm immediately preceding your termination date, and 
◦ your Recognized Service (as defined below) on your date of termination equaled or exceeded 15 years, or your combined 
Recognized Service with the Firm and external professional experience (as attested by you to the Firm) equaled or exceeded 
30 years, and
◦ you provided at least 180 days advance written notice to the Firm of your intention to voluntarily terminate your 
employment under this provision, during which notice period you provided such services as requested by the Firm in a 
cooperative and professional manner and you did not perform any services for any other employer, and 
◦ continued vesting shall be appropriate, which determination shall be made prior to your termination and will be based on 
your performance and conduct (before and after providing notice), and  
◦ for 36 months from the date of grant of this award you do not either perform services in any capacity ( such as an employee, 
contractor, consultant, advisor, or self-employed individual, whether paid or unpaid ) for a Financial Services Company (as 
defined below) or work in your profession (whether or not for a Financial Services Company); provided that you may work

title: Release/Certification
heading: 38.23 Release/Certification
start_phrase: To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
summary:
Summary of main points in the partial document:

- Continued vesting under “Full Career Eligibility” after voluntary termination:
  - At least 5 years of continuous service immediately before termination.
  - Either 15+ years of Recognized Service, or 30+ years combined Recognized Service and external professional experience (as attested).
  - At least 180 days’ advance written notice; during notice you must perform requested services cooperatively, professionally, and not work for any other employer.
  - Firm must determine, before termination, that continued vesting is appropriate based on your performance and conduct.
  - For 36 months from grant, you must not work in any capacity for a Financial Services Company or in your profession; exception allows work for government, education, or Not‑for‑Profit organizations.
  - Must satisfy Release/Certification Requirements.
  - Firm may require you to continue working during the notice period or may shorten it (not earlier than the date you meet the service requirement). Additional notice period policies may apply.

- Government Office:
  - Special treatment if you voluntarily leave to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to separate “Government Office Requirements” and definitions.

- Disability:
  - Continued vesting possible if employment ends due to long‑term disability (under the JPMorgan Chase LTD Plan or equivalent, or a disability that would qualify), provided you:
    - Request continued vesting in writing within 30 days of termination,
    - Provide requested documentation, and
    - Receive the Firm’s written consent,
    - And satisfy Release/Certification Requirements.

- Release/Certification Requirements for any continued vesting:
  - Execute a Firm‑specified release of claims.
  - For Full Career Eligibility: before termination, confirm eligibility (including 180‑day notice) with management and obtain written consent.
  - For Full Career Eligibility and Government Office: certify before each vesting date that you have complied with post‑termination employment restrictions.
  - For Disability: meet notice/documentation requirements and obtain written consent.
  - Comply with all other terms of the Award Agreement.

- Death:
  - If you die while eligible to vest, RSUs immediately vest and are distributed (after tax withholding) to your designated beneficiary on file; fallback recipient is referenced but the text is truncated.

- Notes/References:
  - Concepts defined elsewhere include Recognized Service, Financial Services Company, Not‑for‑Profit Organization, Government Office, and Notice Period.
text:
Release/Certification 
To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
• you must timely execute and deliver a release of claims in favor of the Firm, having such form and terms as the Firm shall 
specify,

that you meet the eligibility criteria (including providing at least 180 days advance written notification), advise that you are 
seeking to be treated as an individual eligible for “Full Career Eligibility”, and receive written consent to such continued 
vesting,
• with respect to “Full Career Eligibility” and “Government Office”, it is your responsibility to take the appropriate steps to 
certify to the Firm prior to each vesting date while the employment restrictions are outstanding, on the authorized form of 
the Firm, that you have complied with the employment restrictions applicable to you (as described herein) from your date of 
termination of employment through the applicable vesting date,
• with respect to “Disability”, you must satisfy the notice and documentation described above and receive written consent to 
such continued vesting, and

title: Notice Period
heading: 38.25.6 Notice Period
start_phrase: If you are subject to a notice period or become subject to a notice period after the Grant Date, whether by contract or by policy, that requires you to provide advance written notice of your intention to terminate your employment (“Notice Period”), then as consideration for this award and continued employment, you will provide the Firm with the necessary advance written notice that applies to you, as specified by such contract or policy.
summary:
- Establishes Notice Period obligations: if subject to a contractual or policy-based notice period, employee must give the required advance written notice to terminate employment. After notice, the Firm may require continued work or place the employee on paid leave during the period. During the Notice Period, the employee must devote full time and loyalty to the Firm, refrain from working for others, and will receive base salary and certain benefits. The length can be mutually waived/modified. Separately, a 180‑day advance notice under “Full Career Eligibility” is required when terminating under that subsection.

- Outlines Recovery (clawback) of distributed shares: employee may be required to repay up to the fair market value of gross shares previously distributed. text:
Notice Period 
If you are subject to a notice period or become subject to a notice period after the Grant Date, whether by contract or by policy, 
that requires you to provide advance written notice of your intention to terminate your employment (“Notice Period”), then as 
consideration for this award and continued employment, you will provide the Firm with the necessary advance written notice that

may place you on a paid leave for all or part of the applicable Notice Period.  During the Notice Period, you shall continue to devote 
your full time and loyalty to the Firm by providing services in a cooperative and professional manner and not perform any services for 
any other employer and shall receive your base salary and certain benefits until your employment terminates.  You and the Firm may 
mutually agree to waive or modify the length of the Notice Period.

text:
In addition to the cancellation provisions described under the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus 
Recoupment ”, “EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff ”, and “ Termination of Employment ”, up to 100% of your 
outstanding RSUs under this award may be cancelled if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
• Any of the following detrimental and risk-related conduct has occurred:
◦ you engaged in conduct detrimental to the Firm insofar as it causes material financial or reputational harm to the 
Firm or its business activities, or
◦ this award was based on materially inaccurate performance metrics, whether or not you were responsible for the 
inaccuracy, or
◦ this award was based on a material misrepresentation by you, or
◦ you improperly or with gross negligence failed to identify, raise or assess, in a timely manner and as reasonably 
expected, risks and/or concerns with respect to risks material to the Firm or its business activities, or
◦ your employment was terminated for Cause (see section captioned “ Definitions ” below) or, in the case of a 
determination after the termination of your employment, that your employment could have been terminated for 
Cause. 
• you have failed to comply with any of the advance notice/cooperation requirements or employment restrictions applicable to 
your termination of employment, or
• you have failed to return the required forms specified under the section captioned “ Release/Certification ” by the specified 
deadline, or
• you have violated any of the provisions as set forth above in the section captioned “ Your Obligations ”.
To the extent provided under the subsection captioned “--Amendment” below, JPMorgan Chase reserves the right to suspend 
vesting of this award and/or distribution of shares under this award, including, without limitation, during any period that JPMorgan

title: Recovery
heading: 38.26.2 Recovery
start_phrase: In addition, you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market Value (determined as of the applicable vesting date) of the gross number of shares of Common Stock previously distributed under this award as follows:
summary:
- Notice Period obligations: Employees subject to a contractual/policy notice period must give advance written notice as a condition of the award and continued employment. The Firm may require work or place the employee on paid leave during the Notice Period; the employee must devote full time and loyalty, not work elsewhere, and will receive base pay and certain benefits. The length may be mutually waived/modified. Separately, a 180‑day advance notice applies for terminations under “Full Career Eligibility.”
- Remedies—Cancellation/Recapture: Up to 100% of outstanding RSUs can be canceled at the Firm’s discretion for detrimental or risk‑related conduct, including material financial/reputational harm, awards based on inaccurate metrics or misrepresentation, failure to identify/escalate material risks, termination for (or that could have been for) Cause, failure to meet notice/cooperation or employment restrictions, failure to return required Release/Certification forms, or violating “Your Obligations.” The Firm may suspend vesting and/or share distributions during evaluations; it is not responsible for market fluctuations during suspension.
- Recovery (clawback): The Firm may require repayment up to the FMV of previously distributed shares (gross, as of vest dates). Recovery can apply to shares distributed within three years before notice-of-recovery for fraud, knowing/willful misconduct, violations of “Your Obligations,” or post‑termination employment restriction breaches (“Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office”). It can also apply to shares distributed within one year for the detrimental/risk‑related conduct noted above. Notice-of-recovery may be electronic and is effective upon good‑faith delivery to the last known address; evaluation notices preserve recovery rights. Recovery targets shares retained after tax liabilities; amounts representing irrevocable tax withholdings/payments will not be required. Repayment may be in shares or cash and is not a penalty. Obligations under separate Bonus Recoupment and EMEA Malus/Clawback policies remain in force.
- Right to an injunction: The Firm may seek injunctive relief for violations, in addition to other legal/equitable remedies.
- Administrative provisions:
  - Withholding taxes: The Firm may retain shares, sell shares, withhold from cash compensation, or hold shares until taxes are paid to satisfy tax obligations.
  - Right to set‑off: Subject to law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds/shares from vesting to satisfy debts owed to the Firm, but will not recover from the employee’s funds/unrestricted securities held at the Firm without consent (except for certain accounts referenced elsewhere).
  - No ownership rights/other limitations: RSUs confer no ownership or voting rights until vesting; shares are issued per Firm procedures. By accepting, the employee authorizes establishment of a brokerage/book‑entry account for delivery of vested shares. Vesting may be suspended and outstanding RSUs canceled if cancellation provisions apply. The Firm may impose post‑vesting restrictions (e.g., sale, transfer, pledge, hedging) for specified periods without affecting voting/dividend rights.
text:
Recovery
In addition, you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market Value (determined as of the 
applicable vesting date) of the gross number of shares of Common Stock previously distributed under this award as follows:
• Payment may be required with respect to any shares distributed within the three year period prior to a notice-of-recovery 
under this section, if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
◦ you committed a fraudulent act, or engaged in knowing and willful misconduct related to your employment, or
◦ you violated any of the provisions as set forth above in the section captioned “ Your Obligations ”, or
◦ you violated the employment restrictions set forth in the subsection “--Full Career Eligibility” or “--Government 
Office” following the termination of your employment.
• In addition, payment may be required with respect to any shares distributed within the one year period prior to notice-of-
recovery under this section, if the Firm in its sole discretion determines appropriate as a result of the detrimental and risk-
related conduct listed in the above “Detrimental Conduct, Risk Related and Other Cancellation/Recapture” subsection.  
Notice-of-recovery under this subsection is a written (including electronic) notice from the Firm to you either requiring payment 
under this subsection or stating that JPMorgan Chase is evaluating requiring payment under this subsection.  Without limiting the foregoing, notice-of-recovery will be deemed provided if the Firm makes a good faith attempt to provide written (including 
electronic) notice at your last known address maintained in the Firm’s employment records.  For the avoidance of doubt, a notice-of-
recovery that the Firm is evaluating requiring payment under this subsection shall preserve JPMorgan Chase’s rights to require 
payment as set forth above in all respects and the Firm shall be under no obligation to complete its evaluation other than as the Firm 
may determine in its sole discretion.
For purposes of this subsection, shares distributed under this award include shares withheld for tax purposes.  However, it is the 
Firm’s intention that you only be required to pay the amounts under this subsection with respect to shares that are or may be 
retained by you following a determination of tax liability and that you will not be required to pay amounts with respect to shares 
representing irrevocable tax withholdings or tax payments previously made (whether by you or the Firm) that you will not be able to 
recover, recapture or reclaim (including as a tax credit, refund or other benefit).  Accordingly, JPMorgan Chase will not require you to 
pay any amount that the Firm or its nominee in his or her sole discretion determines is represented by such withholdings or tax 
payments.
Payment may be made in shares of Common Stock or in cash.  You agree that any repayment will be a lawful recovery under the 
terms and conditions of your Award Agreement and is not to be construed in any manner as a penalty.  
Nothing in the section in any way limits your obligations under “ Bonus Recoupment ” and “ EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - 
Identified Staff ”.

summary:

Such restrictions described in the last sentence shall not impact your right to vote or receive dividends with respect to the Common 
Stock.  By accepting this award, you acknowledge that during such specified period should there be a determination that the recovery provisions of this award apply, then you agree that you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market 
Value (determined as of the applicable vesting date) of the gross number of shares subject to such restrictions (notwithstanding the

title: Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity
heading: 38.27.11 Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity
start_phrase: Upon receipt of satisfactory evidence that applicable United States federal, state, local, foreign or supranational ethics or conflict of interest laws or regulations require you to divest your interest in JPMorgan Chase RSUs, the Firm may accelerate the distribution of all or part of your outstanding award effective on or before the required divestiture date; provided that no accelerated distribution shall occur if the Firm determines that such acceleration will violate Section 409A of the Code.

- Governing Law: New York law.

Definitions
“Cause ” means a determination by the Firm that your employment terminated as a result of your (i) violation of any law, rule or 
regulation (including rules of self-regulatory bodies) related to the Firm’s business, (ii) indictment or conviction of a felony, (iii) 
commission of a fraudulent act, (iv) violation of the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct or other Firm policies or misconduct related to your duties to the Firm (other than immaterial and inadvertent violations or misconduct), (v) grossly inadequate performance of the 
duties associated with your position or job function or failure to follow reasonable directives of your manager, or (vi) any act or 
failure to act that is injurious to the interests of the Firm or its relationship with a customer, client or an employee.
“Financial Services Company ” means a business enterprise that engages in any of the following services (itself or through an affiliate 
or subsidiary), regardless of whether such services are the principle strategy or revenue-generating activity:
• commercial or retail banking, including, but not limited to, commercial, institutional and personal trust, custody and/or 
lending and processing services, internet banking, originating and servicing mortgages, issuing and servicing credit cards, 
payment servicing or processing or merchant services,
• insurance, including but not limited to, guaranteeing against loss, harm, damage, illness, disability or death, providing and 
issuing annuities, acting as principal, agent or broker for purpose of the forgoing,
• financial, investment or economic advisory services, including but not limited to, investment banking services (such as 
advising on mergers or dispositions, underwriting, dealing in, or making a market in securities or other similar activities), 
brokerage services, investment management services, asset management services, foreign exchange services, interbank 
networks and hedge funds,
• issuing, trading or selling instruments representing interests in pools of assets or in derivatives instruments, 
• financial technology companies, such as those selling blockchain services, or offering or selling financial products/services,
• advising on, or investing in, private equity or real estate funds or ventures, or
• any similar activities that the Director of Human Resources or nominee determines in his or her sole discretion constitute 
financial services.
“Firmwide Financial Threshold” means a cumulative return on tangible common equity for calendar years 2023, 2024 and 2025 of 
not less than 15%.  Cumulative return on tangible common equity means (i) the sum of the Firm’s reported net income for all three 
calendar years, divided by (ii) reported year-end tangible equity averaged over the three years.
“Government Office” means (i) a full-time position in an elected or appointed office in local, state, or federal government (including 
equivalent positions outside the U.S. or in a supranational organization), not reasonably anticipated to be a full-career position, or (ii) 
conducting a bona fide full-time campaign for such an elective public office after formally filing for candidacy, where it is customary 
and reasonably necessary to campaign full-time for the office.
“Line of Business” 
“Line of Business” means a business unit of the Firm (or one or more business units designated below under the definition “Line of 
Business Financial Threshold” of the Corporate Investment Bank).  All Corporate Functions (including the functions of the Chief 
Investment Office) are considered a single Line of Business.
“Line of Business Financial Threshold” means the financial threshold set forth below for the following Lines of Business based on 
the Firm’s management reporting system:
Asset & Wealth Management Annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income1
Card and Auto Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income2
Commercial Banking Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income2
Corporate Investment Bank Annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income1 for CIB overall or annual negative 
allocated product revenues (excluding XVA) for: 
• Fixed Income
• Equities
• Securities Services
• Global Investment Banking
• Payments
Consumer Banking, J.P. Morgan Wealth 
Management and Business Banking Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income2
Corporate Functions (including Chief 
Investment Office) Annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income1 at the Firm level
Home Lending Annual negative pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income2
1Pre-tax pre-provision income means Revenue less Expenses2Pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income means Revenue less (Expenses plus Net Charge-offs)
“Not-for-Profit Organization” means an entity exempt from tax under state law and under Section 501(c)(3) of the Code.  Section 
501(c)(3) only includes entities organized and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific, testing for public safety, 
literary or educational purposes, or to foster national or international amateur sports competition or for the prevention of cruelty to 
children or animals. Not-for-Profit Organization  shall also mean entities outside the United States exempt from local and national tax laws because they are organized and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific, testing for public safety, literary or 
educational purposes, or to foster national or international amateur sports competition or for the prevention of cruelty to children or 
animals.
“Recognized Service” means the period of service as an employee set forth in the Firm’s applicable service-related policies.

title: Holding Requirement
heading: 39.4 Holding Requirement
start_phrase: As of the vesting date set forth in your Award Agreement, you shall be entitled to be issued a number of shares of the Common Stock of JPMorgan Chase equal to the number of PSUs, if any, plus any additional Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units, vesting on such date, less the number withheld to satisfy tax withholding obligations.
summary:
- Document type and scope: Terms and conditions for a JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long‑Term Incentive Plan Performance Share Unit (PSU) Award for Operating Committee members, featuring protection-based vesting provisions, and governed by the Plan and Prospectus (which supersede other agreements). 
- Acceptance and governance: Award is effective on the Grant Date unless declined by the stated deadline; if declined, it is canceled as of the Grant Date. Capitalized terms follow Plan definitions. 
- Nature and purpose of award: Each PSU is a non-transferable right to receive one share of JPMorgan Chase common stock at vesting; the award is intended to drive sustained long-term performance and align interests with shareholders. 
- Vesting and payout mechanics: 
  - Number of PSUs vesting equals the Target Award Number multiplied by the Award Payout Percentage determined from a Performance Table. 
  - Performance Ranking and Award Payout Percentage are calculated by a Calculation Agent using defined metrics, including ROTCE (return on tangible common equity), Firm Reported ROTCE, Average Tangible Common Equity (if applicable), and the Performance Table (and its footnote) over the Performance Period. 
  - Delivery of vested shares occurs by a date consistent with Section 409A compliance (as referenced). 
- Dividend equivalents: During the vesting period, cash dividends on common stock are notionally reinvested into additional units (Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) based on the fair market value on each dividend payment date, but only on the actual number of shares that vest. These additional units are delivered at vesting. 
- Taxes and net share issuance: On the vesting date, shares equal to vested PSUs plus dividend equivalent units are issued net of shares withheld for tax obligations. 
- Post-vest holding requirement: Net shares are subject to a two-year transfer restriction (no transferring, assigning, hedging, selling, pledging, or encumbering). Early lapse of restrictions is allowed only upon death or for accelerated distribution due to ethics/conflict considerations tied to employment by a government entity. 
- Cancellation/forfeiture: Award may be canceled in whole or in part pursuant to the terms and conditions.
text:
Holding Requirement 
As of the vesting date set forth in your Award Agreement, you shall be entitled to be issued a number of shares of the Common Stock 
of JPMorgan Chase equal to the number of PSUs, if any, plus any additional Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units, vesting on 
such date, less the number withheld to satisfy tax withholding obligations.  The net number of shares issued to you will be held in an 
account in your name with restrictions preventing you from transferring, assigning, hedging, selling, pledging or otherwise 
encumbering such shares for a two-year period commencing as of the vesting date and ending as of the second anniversary of the 
vesting date.  Such restrictions shall only lapse, prior to the expiration of the two-year holding period, in the event of your death or 
for an accelerated distribution for ethics or conflict reasons.  See section captioned, “ Death ” and subsection captioned, “Accelerated 
Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting from Employment by a Government Entity”.

title: Calculation of Performance Ranking
heading: 39.5 Calculation of Performance Ranking
start_phrase: For purposes of the Performance Ranking, the ranking of the Firm and of each Performance Company for the Performance Period shall be determined and calculated by the Calculation Agent, using the definitions of “Average Tangible Common Equity” (if otherwise applicable), “Calculated PSUs”, “Firm Reported ROTCE”, “Performance Table” (including its footnote) and “ROTCE” as set forth in the “Definitions ” section of these terms and conditions.
summary:
- Document type and scope: Terms and conditions for a JPMorgan Chase & Co. Long-Term Incentive Plan Performance Share Unit (PSU) award for Operating Committee members, featuring protection-based vesting provisions. The Plan governs over any conflicting award terms; Award Agreement, Plan, and Prospectus supersede prior agreements.
- Acceptance/decline: Award is effective as of the Grant Date unless declined by the stated deadline; if declined, it is cancelled as of the Grant Date.
- Form and purpose: Each PSU is a non-transferable right to one share of JPMorgan Chase common stock upon vesting; designed to promote sustained long-term performance and alignment with shareholders.
- Vesting outcome: Number of PSUs that vest equals Target Award Number multiplied by an Award Payout Percentage determined via a Performance Table; performance calculations use defined metrics (e.g., ROTCE, Average Tangible Common Equity) and are binding; rounding to the nearest hundredth and tie rules apply. Delivery timing is subject to Section 409A compliance.
- Dividend equivalents: During the vesting period, cash dividends are notionally reinvested into additional units (Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) based on the fair market value on each dividend date; these vest and are delivered with the PSUs.
- Holding requirement: Net shares delivered at vest (after tax withholding) are restricted from transfer, assignment, hedging, sale, pledge, or encumbrance for two years post-vesting; restrictions can lapse earlier in case of death or an accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment.
- Capital ratio performance threshold: If the Firm’s CET1 ratio falls below a set threshold at any year-end during the performance period, up to one-third of the Target Award Number may be downward adjusted by the CMDC for each such year.
- Vesting period definition: From Grant Date to the vesting date; Firm may extend the vesting period and may restrict delivered shares post-vesting as noted.
- Protection-based vesting and potential cancellation: Award is intended to vest if continuously employed through vest date or upon qualifying termination (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability), but up to 50% of the award (including related dividend units) designated as “At Risk PSUs” may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion, subject to CMDC ratification (Board involvement for CEO awards), based on:
  - Sustained unsatisfactory performance by you or the Firm versus stated priorities (including metrics such as net income, total net revenue, EPS, capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income in any year of the vesting period.
  - RSU cancellations within a Line of Business you oversee due to failure to meet its annual financial threshold.
  - Failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
  - Cancellation may occur before the performance period ends and continues to apply after qualifying terminations that allow continued vesting.
- Tax withholding: Shares are net-settled with shares withheld to satisfy tax obligations.
- Bonus recoupment: Award and the corresponding cash incentive for the performance year are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (as amended from time to time); the policy’s rights are not limited by these terms.
- Other notes: Calculations performed by the Calculation Agent; references to defined terms and detailed performance/ranking mechanics are provided in the Definitions and Performance Table sections.
text:
Calculation of Performance Ranking 
For purposes of the Performance Ranking, the ranking of the Firm and of each Performance Company for the Performance Period 
shall be determined and calculated by the Calculation Agent, using the definitions of “Average Tangible Common Equity” (if otherwise 
applicable), “Calculated PSUs”, “Firm Reported ROTCE”, “Performance Table” (including its footnote) and “ROTCE” as set forth in the “Definitions ” section of these terms and conditions.  See section captioned “ Definitions ”.  Except for Firm Reported ROTCE, 
calculations will be expressed as a decimal to the second place (i.e. xx.yy%), rounded to the nearest hundredth.  See section 
captioned, “ Definitions --Performance Table” in the event of a tie.  All performance based calculations as set forth herein are binding 
and conclusive on you and your successors.

title: Capital Ratio Performance Threshold
heading: 39.6 Capital Ratio Performance Threshold
start_phrase: Unvested PSUs are subject to reduction if the Firm’s Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio at any year end falls below a predetermined threshold of ______%.
summary:
- This excerpt outlines key terms and conditions for JPMorgan Chase Performance Share Units (PSUs), with cross-references to the “Definitions” and “Performance Table” sections.
- Calculation standards: Except for Firm Reported ROTCE, performance calculations are shown as percentages to two decimal places, rounded to the nearest hundredth; tie-breaking rules are in the “Definitions—Performance Table.” All performance calculations are binding on recipients and their successors.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If the Firm’s CET1 ratio is below a preset threshold at any year-end during the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced for each such year by the Compensation and Management Development Committee (CMDC).
- Vesting Period: Runs from Grant Date to vesting date. The Firm may extend the vesting period and may restrict delivered shares post-vesting per referenced sections (Administrative Provision—Amendment, Holding Period, No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations).
- Protection-based vesting: Although intended to vest if employed through the vesting date or upon qualifying events (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability), up to 50% of the award (At Risk PSUs, including reinvested dividend equivalents) may be canceled at the CEO’s discretion based on:
  - Sustained underperformance by the individual or Firm against stated priorities (considering metrics such as net income, total net revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income during the vesting period.
  - RSU cancellations in a Line of Business under the recipient’s responsibility due to failing its annual Financial Threshold.
  - The Firm failing to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
  Cancellations can occur before the Performance Period ends and are capped at 50% of the Target Award. These cancellation conditions continue to apply after qualifying terminations that allow continued vesting. Determinations require CMDC ratification; for current or former CEOs, the Committee decides and the Board ratifies.
- Bonus Recoupment: The award and the cash incentive for the specified performance year are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (or successor). The policy is accessible on the Firm’s corporate governance website, and the terms do not limit the Firm’s rights under that policy.
- Additional cross-references: “Number to Vest on Vesting Date,” “Remedies,” and other administrative and holding period provisions.
text:
Capital Ratio Performance Threshold 
Unvested PSUs are subject to reduction if the Firm’s Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio at any year end falls below a 
predetermined threshold of ______%.
If the Firm’s CET1 capital ratio at any year end during the Performance Period is below this predetermined threshold, up to one-third 
of the Target Award Number of PSUs will be subject to downward adjustment by the CMDC for each such year.

title: Vesting Period
heading: 39.7 Vesting Period
start_phrase: The period from the Grant Date to the vesting date is the “Vesting Period”.
summary:
- Covers performance share unit (PSU) terms, referencing a “Definitions” section and stating that, except for Firm Reported ROTCE, all calculations are shown to two decimal places and rounded to the nearest hundredth; tie outcomes are governed by the “Definitions—Performance Table,” and all performance calculations are binding on the participant and successors.
- Establishes a Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: if the Firm’s year-end CET1 ratio falls below a predetermined percentage in any year of the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced by the Compensation and Management Development Committee (CMDC) for each such year.
- Defines the Vesting Period as the time from Grant Date to vesting date, noting the Firm’s right to extend vesting, impose post-vesting restrictions, and apply a holding period.
- Details Protection-Based Vesting: the award is intended to vest if the participant remains employed through vesting or meets continued vesting criteria (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability), but vesting remains subject to other terms including performance thresholds and remedies.
- Authorizes the CEO to cancel up to 50% of the award (including Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) as “At Risk PSUs,” based on factors such as sustained underperformance against priorities (including metrics like net income, revenue, EPS, capital ratios), negative firm-level pre-tax pre-provision income in any calendar year, cancellation of RSUs in a participant’s Line of Business due to failing its financial threshold, or failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold; cancellations can occur before the end of the Performance Period and continue to apply even if employment ends under continued-vesting scenarios.
- Requires ratification of protection-based vesting determinations by the CMDC; for any current or former CEO award, determinations are made by the Committee and ratified by the Board.
- Subjects the participant to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (as amended from time to time) for both the relevant performance year’s cash incentive and this award, without limiting the Firm’s rights under that policy.
text:
Vesting Period 
The period from the Grant Date to the vesting date is the “Vesting Period”. (See “Administrative Provision--Amendment” pursuant to 
which the Firm may extend the vesting period and “No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations” pursuant to which the Firm may place 
restrictions on delivered shares of Common Stock following the vesting date and section captioned, “Holding Period” above.)

title: Protection-Based Vesting
heading: 39.8 Protection-Based Vesting
start_phrase: This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date, provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.
summary:
- Cross-references to Definitions and Performance Table sections; performance calculations (except Firm Reported ROTCE) rounded to the nearest hundredth (xx.yy%) and deemed binding and conclusive.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If JPMorgan Chase’s year-end CET1 ratio falls below a preset threshold in any year of the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target PSUs may be reduced by the CMDC for each such year.
- Vesting Period runs from Grant Date to vesting date; the Firm may extend vesting and impose post-vesting share restrictions under separate provisions.
- Protection-Based Vesting: While awards are intended to vest with continuous employment (or upon Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability), up to 50% of the award (including reinvested dividend equivalent units) may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion, subject to CMDC ratification (and Board ratification for CEO awards), based on:
  - Sustained unsatisfactory individual or Firm performance against priorities (considering metrics such as net income, revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax, pre-provision income in any year during the vesting period.
  - Cancellation of RSUs in a Line of Business under the recipient’s responsibility due to not meeting its LOB Financial Threshold.
  - Failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
- Such cancellations can occur before the end of the Performance Period, capped at 50% of the Target Award; cancellation provisions continue to apply even if employment ends under the eligible continued-vesting scenarios.
- Bonus Recoupment: Both the cash incentive for the applicable performance year and this award are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy; nothing in the terms limits the Firm’s recoupment rights.
text:
Protection-Based Vesting 
This award is intended and expected to vest on the vesting date, provided that you are continuously employed by the Firm through 
such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full 
Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.  However, vesting and the number of PSUs that will vest are subject to 
these terms and conditions (including, but not limited to, sections captioned “ Number to Vest on Vesting Date ”, “Capital Ratio 
Performance Threshold ”, “Remedies ” and the following protection-based vesting provision).  
Up to a total of fifty percent of your award (including any associated Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) that would 
otherwise be distributable to you on the vesting date (“At Risk PSUs”) may be cancelled if the Chief Executive Officer of JPMorgan 
Chase (“CEO”) determines in his or her sole discretion that cancellation of all or portion of the At Risk PSUs is appropriate in light of 
any one or a combination of the following factors:
• Your performance in relation to the priorities for your position, or the Firm’s performance in relation to the priorities for 
which you share responsibility as a member of the Operating Committee, have been unsatisfactory for a sustained period of 
time.  Among the factors the CEO may consider in assessing performance are:  net income, total net revenue, earnings per 
share and capital ratios of the Firm, both on an absolute basis and, as appropriate, relative to peer firms. 
• For any calendar year ending during the vesting period, JPMorgan Chase’s annual pre-tax pre-provision income at the Firm 
level is negative.
• RSU awards granted to participants in a Line of Business for which you exercise, or during the vesting period exercised, 
direct or indirect responsibility, were in whole or in part cancelled because the Line of Business did not meet its annual Line 
of Business Financial Threshold.  
• The Firm does not meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold. 
For avoidance of doubt, cancellation of the At Risk PSUs, in whole or part, for one or more of the above factors may occur prior to the 
end of the Performance Period and the maximum number of At Risk PSUs subject to cancellation prior to the end of the Performance 
Period will be up to fifty percent of the Target Award Number.
In the event that your employment terminates due to “Job Elimination”, “Full Career Eligibility”, “Government Office” or “Disability” 
thereby entitling you to continued vesting in your award, (or potentially acceleration due to satisfaction of the Government Office 
Requirements), the cancellation circumstances described above will continue to apply.
Any determination above with respect to protection-based vesting provisions is subject to ratification by the Compensation and 
Management Development Committee of the Board of Directors of JPMorgan Chase (“Committee”).  In the case of an award to any 
current or former CEO, all such determinations shall be made by the Committee and ratified by the Board.

title: Bonus Recoupment
heading: 39.9 Bonus Recoupment
start_phrase: In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree that you are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (or successor policy) as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance year 20______ and to this award.
summary:
- Calculation conventions and authority: Performance calculations (except Firm Reported ROTCE) are expressed to two decimal places and rounded to the nearest hundredth; tie-handling is per the “Definitions—Performance Table.” All performance-based calculations are binding and conclusive on the participant and successors.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If the Firm’s CET1 ratio at any year-end during the Performance Period falls below a predetermined threshold (blank in excerpt), up to one-third of the Target Award Number of PSUs may be reduced for each such year at the discretion of the Compensation and Management Development Committee (CMDC).
- Vesting Period: Defined as the period from Grant Date to vesting date; the Firm may extend the vesting period and may impose post-vesting restrictions on delivered shares. References are made to related provisions (Administrative Provision—Amendment, No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations, and Holding Period).
- Protection-based vesting framework: Award is intended to vest if continuously employed through vesting, or upon meeting continued vesting conditions for Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability. Actual vesting remains subject to other sections (e.g., Number to Vest, Capital Ratio Performance Threshold, Remedies).
- At Risk PSUs and potential cancellation: Up to 50% of the award (including Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion, based on:
  - Sustained unsatisfactory performance by the participant or Firm/Operating Committee priorities (metrics may include net income, total net revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute or relative to peers).
  - Negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income in any year during the vesting period.
  - RSU cancellations within a Line of Business under the participant’s (current or prior) responsibility due to not meeting its Line of Business Financial Threshold.
  - Failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
  Cancellation can occur before the Performance Period ends, capped at 50% of the Target Award Number.
- Continued vesting scenarios: If employment ends under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office (with possible acceleration), or Disability, the cancellation conditions above still apply during continued vesting.
- Governance of determinations: Protection-based vesting decisions require ratification by the CMDC; for awards to a current or former CEO, decisions are made by the CMDC and ratified by the Board.
- Bonus Recoupment: The participant agrees to be subject to JPMorgan Chase’s Bonus Recoupment Policy (as amended from time to time) for both the cash incentive for the specified performance year (blank in excerpt) and this award; nothing in these terms limits the Firm’s rights under that policy.
text:
Bonus Recoupment
In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree that you are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy (or 
successor policy) as in effect from time to time  as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance 
year 20______ and to this award.  You can access this policy as currently in effect by clicking the following link to the JPMorgan Chase & 
Co. Corporate Governance Principles web page and scrolling to the Bonus Recoupment Policy located under the section titled “Other 
Matters ”:
https://about.jpmorganchase.com/about/governance/corporate-governance-principles  
For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in these terms and conditions in any way limits the rights of the Firm under the JPMorgan Chase 
Bonus Recoupment Policy (or successor policy).

title: Termination of Employment
heading: 39.10 Termination of Employment
start_phrase: Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, this award (for avoidance of doubt, including any associated Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) will be cancelled in full effective on the date your employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
summary:
- Core rule: Upon termination of employment for any reason, the award (including any Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) is cancelled immediately, except as provided under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death.
- Post-termination vesting: You may continue to vest as if still employed, subject to all terms (including Protection-Based Vesting, Number to Vest on Vesting Date, Bonus Recoupment, Your Obligations, and Remedies) if one of the following applies:
  - Job Elimination: HR Director (or nominee) determines your role was eliminated; you cooperated professionally after notice; and you meet the Release/Certification Requirements.
  - Full Career Eligibility: HR (or nominee) determines you voluntarily resigned; you had at least 5 years of continuous service; your age plus Recognized Service ≥ 60; you gave at least 180 days’ advance written notice, cooperated during that period, and performed no services for any other employer; HR determines before termination that continued vesting is appropriate based on your performance and conduct; for 36 months from grant you do not work in any capacity for a Financial Services Company or in your profession (government, education, or Not‑for‑Profit work permitted); and you meet the Release/Certification Requirements. The Firm may require continued service during the notice period or shorten it (not earlier than when age/service criteria are met). Additional notice policies may apply.
  - Government Office: You voluntarily leave to accept or run for an elective Government Office, per the Government Office Requirements (see Definitions).
  - Disability: Termination occurs because you cannot return to work while on LTD Plan benefits (or local equivalent), or due to a qualifying long‑term disability if not covered by the LTD Plan; you request continued vesting in writing within 30 days, provide required documentation, obtain the Firm’s written consent, and meet the Release/Certification Requirements.
- Several conditions rely on defined terms and requirements referenced elsewhere (e.g., Release/Certification Requirements, Notice Period, Definitions).
text:
Termination of Employment
Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government 
Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, this award (for avoidance of doubt, including any associated 
Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units) will be cancelled in full effective on the date your employment with the Firm terminates 
for any reason.
Subject to these terms and conditions (including, but not limited to, sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Number to Vest 
on Vesting Date ”, “Bonus Recoupment ”, “Your Obligations ” and “ Remedies ”) you will be eligible to continue to vest (as you otherwise 
would vest if you were still employed by JPMorgan Chase) with respect to your award in accordance with its terms and conditions 
following the termination of your employment if one of the following circumstances applies to you:
• Job Elimination 
In the event that the Director of Human Resources or nominee in his or her sole discretion determines that 
•the Firm terminated your employment because your job was eliminated, and  
•after you are notified that your job will be eliminated, you provided such services as requested by the Firm in a cooperative 
and professional manner, and 
•you satisfied the Release/Certification Requirements set forth below.
• Full Career Eligibility 
In the event that the Director of Human Resources or nominee in his or her sole discretion determines that 
•you voluntarily terminated your employment with the Firm, had completed at least five years of continuous service with the 
Firm immediately preceding your termination date, and 
•the sum of your age and Recognized Service (as defined below) on your date of termination equaled or exceeded 60, and
•you provided at least 180 days advance written notice to the Firm of your intention to voluntarily terminate your employment 
under this provision, during which notice period you provided such services as requested by the Firm in a cooperative and 
professional manner and you did not perform any services for any other employer, and 
•continued vesting shall be appropriate, which determination shall be made prior to your termination and will be based on 
your performance and conduct (before and after providing notice), and  
•for 36 months from the date of grant of this award, you do not either perform services in any capacity (such as an employee, 
contractor, consultant advisor, or self-employed individual, whether paid or unpaid) for a Financial Services Company (as 
defined below) or work in your profession (whether or not for a Financial Services Company); provided that you may work for 
a government, education or Not-for-Profit Organization (as defined below), and
•you satisfied the Release/Certification Requirements set forth below. 
After receipt of such advance written notice, the Firm may choose to have you continue to provide services during such 180-day 
period as a condition to continued vesting or shorten the length of the 180-day period at the Firm’s sole discretion, but to a date 
no earlier than the date you would otherwise meet the age and service requirements. 
Additional advance notice requirements may apply for employees subject to notice period policies.  (See “Notice Period” below.)
• Government Office 
In the event that you voluntarily terminate your employment with the Firm to accept a Government Office or become a candidate 
for an elective Government Office, as described at the end of these terms and conditions under the section captioned 
“Government Office Requirements ”.  See also definition of Government Office in the section captioned “ Definitions ”.
• Disability

title: Release/Certification
heading: 39.11 Release/Certification
start_phrase: To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
summary:
- Sets conditions for continued vesting after employment ends, requiring a timely release of claims and compliance certifications.
- Details “Full Career Eligibility” prerequisites: advance written notice (at least 180 days), confirmation of eligibility, and written consent; certification of compliance with employment restrictions for “Full Career Eligibility” and “Government Office.”
- Outlines requirements for continued vesting in case of Disability (notice/documentation and written consent).
- States that all other Award Agreement terms must be met to maintain vesting eligibility.
- Describes death benefits: beneficiary/estate receives shares based on completed-year performance (average of completed calendar years), vesting one-third of target PSUs per completed year, with 100% payout assumption for remaining years; includes dividend equivalent share units through date of death.
- Provides distribution timing upon death: no later than the end of the calendar year following death (administrative practice aims for registration within ~60 days after required documentation is received).
- Enumerates participant obligations tied to receiving the award: non-solicitation, confidentiality, non-disparagement, cooperation, compliance with the agreement, and notice period.
- Non-solicitation covenant: for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from grant date (if award not canceled), prohibits soliciting/inducing Firm employees, hiring recent Firm employees with limited exceptions, and soliciting/diverting Firm customers/suppliers known or serviced through employment (with a carveout for publicly known institutional customers when no confidential information is used); excludes authorized actions taken in the normal course of employment.
- Confidentiality covenant: prohibits using or disclosing Firm confidential information and communicating with media about Firm-related matters during and after employment, except as allowed by the Code of Conduct, policies, law, or legal process (section text is partially truncated).
text:
Release/Certification 
To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
• you must timely execute and deliver a release of claims in favor of the Firm, having such form and terms as the Firm shall 
specify,
• with respect to Full Career Eligibility, prior to the termination of your employment, you must confirm with management that you 
meet the eligibility criteria (including providing at least 180 days advance written notification), advise  that you are seeking to be 
treated as an individual eligible for Full Career Eligibility, and receive written consent to such continued vesting, 
• with respect to “Full Career Eligibility” and “Government Office”, it is your responsibility to take the appropriate steps to certify 
to the Firm prior to the vesting date while the employment restrictions are outstanding on the authorized form of the Firm that 
you have complied with the employment restrictions applicable to you (as described herein) from your date of termination of 
employment through the applicable vesting date,  
• with respect to Disability, you must satisfy the notice and documentation described above and receive written consent to such 
continued vesting, and
• in all cases, otherwise complied with all other terms of the Award Agreement.  (See section captioned “ Your Obligations ” below.)

title: Death
heading: 39.12 Death
start_phrase: If you die while you are eligible to vest in this award, your designated beneficiary on file with the Firm’s Stock Administration Department (or your estate or if no beneficiary has been designated or survives you or if beneficiary designation is not recognized locally) may be entitled to receive a distribution of a number of shares of Common Stock associated with your award.
summary:
- Sets conditions for continued vesting after employment termination, requiring: timely execution of a Firm-specified release of claims; for Full Career Eligibility, advance confirmation of eligibility (including at least 180 days’ written notice) and written consent; for Full Career Eligibility and Government Office, certification prior to each vesting date of compliance with post-employment restrictions; for Disability, required notice/documentation and written consent; and overall compliance with the Award Agreement.

text:
Death
If you die while you are eligible to vest in this award, your designated beneficiary on file with the Firm’s Stock Administration 
Department (or your estate or if no beneficiary has been designated or survives you or if beneficiary designation is not recognized 
locally) may be entitled to receive a distribution of a number of shares of Common Stock associated with your award.  The Award 
Payout Percentage in the case of death is based on the Number to Vest on the Vesting Date calculation described above using the 
average performance of all completed calendar years, multiplied by one-third of the Target Award Number of PSUs for each 
completed calendar year in the Performance Period, and using the Award Payout Percentage equal to 100 percent for any remaining 
calendar years in the Performance Period.  
In addition, your beneficiary or your estate shall receive additional shares of Common Stock, i.e. Reinvested Dividend Equivalent 
Share Units, as set forth in the section captioned, “ Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units ” but based on dividend equivalents up 
to the date of your death. 
Any shares will be distributed no later than the end of the calendar year immediately following the calendar year which contains your 
date of death; however, our administrative practice is to register such shares in the name of your beneficiary or estate within 60 days 
of the Firm’s receipt of any required documentation.

title: Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
heading: 39.13.1 Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
start_phrase: During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date, you will not directly or indirectly, whether on your own behalf or on behalf of any other party, without the prior written consent of the Director of Human Resources: (i) solicit, induce or encourage any of the Firm’s then current employees to leave the Firm or to apply for employment elsewhere, unless such current employee has received official, written notice that his or her employment will be terminated due to job elimination (ii) hire any employee or former employee who was employed by the Firm at the date your employment terminated, unless the individual’s employment terminated because his or her job was eliminated, or the individual’s employment with the Firm has been terminated for more than six months, (iii) to the fullest extent enforceable under applicable law, solicit or induce or attempt to induce to leave the Firm, or divert or attempt to divert from doing business with the Firm, any then current customers, suppliers or other persons or entities that were serviced by you or whose names became known to you by virtue of your employment with the Firm, or otherwise interfere with the relationship between the Firm and such customers, suppliers or other persons or entities.

During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment 
or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date, you will not directly or 
indirectly, whether on your own behalf or on behalf of any other party, without the prior written consent of the Director of 
Human Resources: (i) solicit, induce or encourage any of the Firm’s then current employees to leave the Firm or to apply for 
employment elsewhere, unless such current employee has received official, written notice that his or her employment will be 
terminated due to job elimination (ii) hire any employee or former employee who was employed by the Firm at the date your 
employment terminated, unless the individual’s employment terminated because his or her job was eliminated, or the 
individual’s employment with the Firm has been terminated for more than six months, (iii) to the fullest extent enforceable under 
applicable law, solicit or induce or attempt to induce to leave the Firm, or divert or attempt to divert from doing business with 
the Firm, any then current customers, suppliers or other persons or entities that were serviced by you or whose names became

title: Confidential Information
heading: 39.13.2 Confidential Information
start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, directly or indirectly (i) use or disclose to anyone any confidential information related to the Firm’s business, or (ii) communicate with the press or other media about matters related to the Firm, its customers or employees, including matters and activities relating to your employment, or the employment of others, by the Firm, in the case of either (i) or (ii), except as explicitly permitted by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct and applicable policies or law or legal process.
summary:
- Confidential information: Defined as in the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct; access to the Firm’s private/internal information via phone, intranet, or internet requires written authorization.
- Whistleblower and legal cooperation carve-outs: Nothing in the award restricts reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to management, directors, government, regulators, self-regulatory bodies, attorneys, or courts, or responding truthfully to official inquiries.
- Non-disparagement: During and after employment, you must not make public statements that disparage the Firm or its people as a group, with exceptions for lawful reporting and truthful participation in investigations or proceedings.
- Cooperation duty: You must fully cooperate with the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings; reasonable out-of-pocket expenses will be reimbursed.
- Compliance with the Award Agreement: You must provide information needed to assess compliance and authorize the Firm to disclose award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
- Notice Period obligations: If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, you must give the required written advance notice. The Firm may require continued services or place you on paid leave during the notice period. You must devote full time and loyalty to the Firm, not work for others, and will receive base salary and certain benefits until termination; the notice length can be mutually modified or waived. Separately, a 180-day advance notice applies for “Full Career Eligibility” terminations.
- Remedies—cancellation/recapture: In addition to other cancellation provisions (Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, Termination of Employment), up to 100% of outstanding PSUs (including Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units and Calculated PSUs) may be canceled if the Firm determines:
  - You engaged in conduct causing material financial or reputational harm to the Firm;
  - The award was based on materially inaccurate performance metrics (regardless of your responsibility);
  - The award was based on your material misrepresentation; or
  - You improperly or with gross negligence failed to timely identify, raise, or assess material risks as reasonably expected.

Remedies 
•Detrimental Conduct, Risk Related and Other Cancellation/Recapture
In addition to the cancellation provisions described under the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus 
Recoupment ” and “ Termination of Employment ”, up to 100% of your award (for the avoidance of doubt, including any 
associated Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units as well as the Calculated PSUs) your outstanding PSUs under this 
award may be cancelled if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
• Any of the following detrimental and risk-related conduct has occurred:
◦ you engaged in conduct detrimental to the Firm insofar as it causes material financial or reputational harm 
to the Firm or its business activities, or
◦ this award was based on materially inaccurate performance metrics, whether or not you were responsible 
for the inaccuracy, or
◦ this award was based on a material misrepresentation by you, or
◦ you improperly or with gross negligence failed to identify, raise or assess, in a timely manner and as 
reasonably expected, risks and/or concerns with respect to risks material to the Firm or its business 
activities, or◦ your employment was terminated for Cause (see section captioned “ Definitions ” below) or, in the case of a 
determination after the termination of your employment, that your employment could have been 
terminated for Cause.
• you have failed to comply with any of the advance notice/cooperation requirements or employment restrictions 
applicable to your termination of employment, or
• you have failed to return the required forms specified under the section captioned “ Release/Certification ” by the 
specified deadline, or
• you have violated any of the provisions as set forth above in the section captioned “ Your Obligations ”.
To the extent provided under the subsection captioned “--Amendment” below, JPMorgan Chase reserves the right to suspend 
vesting of this award and/or distribution of shares under this award, including, without limitation, during any period that 
JPMorgan Chase is evaluating whether this award is subject to cancellation and/or recovery and/or whether the conditions 
for distributions of shares under this award are satisfied.  The Firm is not responsible for any price fluctuations during any 
period of suspension and, if applicable, suspended units will be reinstated consistent with Plan administration procedures.  
See also “ Administrative Provisions —No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations”.
In addition, you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market Value (determined as of the 
applicable vesting date or acceleration date) of the gross number of shares of Common Stock previously distributed, including 
vested shares subject to the Holding Requirements, under this award as follows:
•Payment may be required with respect to any shares of Common Stock distributed within the three year period prior to a 
notice-of-recovery under this section, if the Firm in its sole discretion determines that:
◦you committed a fraudulent act, or engaged in knowing and willful misconduct related to your employment; 
◦you violated any of the provisions as set forth above in the section captioned “ Your Obligations ;” or
◦you violated the employment restrictions set forth in the subsection “Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office” 
following the termination of your employment.
•In addition, payment may be required with respect to any shares distributed within the one year period prior to notice-of-
recovery under this section, if the Firm in its sole discretion determines appropriate pursuant to the provisions in the section 
captioned “ Recapture Provisions ”.
Notice-of-recovery under this subsection is a written (including electronic) notice from the Firm to you either requiring payment 
under this subsection or stating that JPMorgan Chase is evaluating requiring payment under this subsection.  Without limiting the 
foregoing, notice-of-recovery will be deemed provided if the Firm makes a good faith attempt to provide written (including 
electronic) notice at your last known address maintained in the Firm’s employment records.  For the avoidance of doubt, a 
notice-of-recovery that the Firm is evaluating requiring payment under this subsection shall preserve JPMorgan Chase’s rights to 
require payment as set forth above in all respects and the Firm shall be under no obligation to complete its evaluation other than 
as the Firm may determine in its sole discretion.
