title: Withholding Taxes
heading: 39.15.1 Withholding Taxes
start_phrase: As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares and the award.
summary:
- Sets out cancellation and recoupment triggers for a JPMorgan Chase PSU award, including termination for Cause (or if Cause could have been determined post-termination), failure to meet advance notice/cooperation or post-employment restrictions, failure to return required Release/Certification forms by deadline, and violations of “Your Obligations.”
- Allows the Firm to suspend vesting and/or distribution of shares while it evaluates cancellation, recovery, or distribution conditions; the Firm is not liable for market price changes during suspension, and suspended units may be reinstated per plan procedures.
- Describes clawback/repayment: the Firm may require you to repay up to the Fair Market Value of shares previously distributed (including those subject to holding requirements) if, within three years before a notice-of-recovery, you committed fraud/knowing willful misconduct, violated “Your Obligations,” or breached post-employment restrictions (Full Career Eligibility or Government Office). The Firm may also require repayment for shares distributed within one year before notice under “Recapture Provisions.”
- Defines “notice-of-recovery” (written/electronic notice sent to last known address) and clarifies that a notice of evaluation preserves the Firm’s rights without obligating it to complete the evaluation.
- Clarifies that “shares distributed” include shares withheld for taxes, but the Firm intends to seek repayment only for shares you could retain after taxes; amounts representing irrevocable tax withholdings/payments not recoverable by you will not be required to be repaid.
- Permits repayment in cash or shares and states such recovery is lawful and not a penalty; does not limit separate “Bonus Recoupment” rights.
- Provides for injunctive relief: the Firm can seek an immediate court injunction for any breach or attempted breach of obligations, in addition to other legal/equitable remedies.
- Administrative tax provisions: the Firm may satisfy withholding via share retention, market sale of shares, withholding from cash compensation (if required), or by retaining vested shares until you pay taxes directly.
- Right to set-off: to the extent permitted by law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy your debts to the Firm, but will not recoup from your funds or unrestricted securities held in your personal Firm accounts without consent; certain designated accounts remain subject to plan limits.
- No ownership rights: PSUs confer no stock ownership or voting rights until shares are determined and vested. By accepting, you authorize the Firm to open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares. During any suspension, PSUs may be canceled if cancellation provisions apply. The Firm may impose post-vesting restrictions (e.g., on sale, transfer, pledge, hedging) without affecting voting/dividend rights; if recovery applies during such restrictions, you may be required to repay up to the FMV of the restricted shares.
- Confirms the Award Agreement binds any JPMorgan Chase successor.
- States the award is not an employment contract; employment remains at-will, there is no right to future awards, and the award’s value is not used to calculate severance.
- Section 409A compliance: intended to comply with Section 409A; if you are a “specified employee” who separates from service and any portion is deferred compensation payable within six months as a result of separation, delivery is delayed until the first month after six full months post-separation; provides timing rules for payments when no substantial risk of forfeiture remains.
- Change in capital structure: the Committee may make equitable substitutions/adjustments to outstanding PSUs and share reserves for stock splits, dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, exchanges, or similar corporate events.
text:
Withholding Taxes:  As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution 
the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or 
necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares and the award.  This may include but is not limited to (i) a market sale of a number of such shares on your behalf 
substantially equal to the withholding or other taxes, (ii) to the extent required by law, withhold from cash compensation, an amount 
equal to any withholding obligation with respect to the award and shares that vest under this award, and (iii) retaining shares that 
vest under this award until you pay any taxes associated with the award and vested shares directly to the competent authorities.

title: Right to Set Off
heading: 39.15.2 Right to Set Off
start_phrase: Although the Firm expects to settle this award in share(s) of Common Stock as of the applicable vesting date, as set forth in your Award Agreement, the Firm may, to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law (including Section 409A of the Code to the extent it is applicable to you), retain for itself funds or the Common Stock resulting from any vesting of this award to satisfy any obligation or debt that you owe to the Firm.
summary:

- Right to set off: Subject to law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or vested shares to satisfy debts you owe the firm. It will not recover from your other funds or unrestricted securities held at the firm without your consent, except for accounts established for this award.
- No ownership rights prior to vesting: PSUs confer no ownership or voting rights. Shares are issued only after PSUs are determined and vest, following the firm’s issuance procedures. The firm may open a brokerage/book-entry account in your name to deliver vested shares.

After vesting, the firm may impose restrictions (e.g., on sale, transfer, pledge, hedging) for a specified period; voting and dividend rights on issued shares remain during this period. If recovery provisions apply during the restriction period, you may owe up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares as of vesting, despite set-off limits.

- Employment status: The agreement is not an employment contract; employment is at-will. The award does not guarantee future awards and is not counted as compensation for severance purposes.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A. If no substantial risk of forfeiture remains, the remainder of each calendar year after the vesting date is a permissible payment date for distributing vested portions.
- Corporate changes: In the event of stock splits, dividends (other than regular cash), recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, exchanges, or similar events, equitable adjustments will be made to shares reserved/issued under the plan and to outstanding PSUs.

title: No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations
heading: 39.15.3 No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations
start_phrase: PSUs do not convey the rights of ownership of Common Stock and do not carry voting rights.
summary:
- Tax withholding: The firm may satisfy withholding and related tax obligations by selling vested shares, withholding from cash compensation as required by law, or retaining vested shares until you pay taxes to the authorities.
- Right to set off: Subject to applicable law (including Section 409A), the firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts you owe the firm. It will not recoup from funds or unrestricted securities held in your name at the firm without your consent, except for accounts established under the stock plan as described below.
- No ownership rights: PSUs do not confer ownership or voting rights. No shares are issued until PSUs are determined and vest. You authorize the firm to open a brokerage or book-entry account to deliver vested shares. PSUs may be canceled in whole or part if cancellation provisions apply during a vesting suspension.
- Post-vesting share restrictions: As of any vesting date, the firm may restrict sale, transfer, pledging, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares for a specified period. These restrictions do not affect voting or dividend rights. If recovery provisions apply during such period, you may be required to repay up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares, despite the set-off limitation.
- Binding agreement: The Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- No employment contract: Employment remains at-will. The award does not guarantee continued employment, similar future awards, or severance treatment.
- Section 409A compliance: The award is intended to comply with Section 409A. For specified employees who separate from service, deliveries that would occur within six months are delayed until the first month after six full months. Additional payment timing rules apply when amounts are no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture.
- Corporate adjustments: In the event of stock splits/dividends (other than regular cash dividends), recapitalizations, new classes of stock, mergers, spin-offs, combinations, exchanges, or similar events, equitable adjustments will be made to outstanding PSUs and shares reserved/issued under the plan.
text:

rights.  No shares of Common Stock will be issued to you until after the number of PSUs have been determined, if any, and have

With respect to any applicable vesting date, JPMorgan Chase may impose for any reason, as of such vesting date for such period as it

but not limited to, restricting the sale, transfer, pledging, assignment, hedging or encumbrance of such shares of Common Stock. 
Such restrictions described in the last sentence shall not impact your right to vote or receive dividends with respect to the Common

title: Other Equitable Adjustments
heading: 39.16 Other Equitable Adjustments
start_phrase: The Committee may make adjustments (up or down) to the award as it deems to be equitable, to maintain the intended economics of the award in light of changed circumstances, which may include unusual or non-recurring events affecting the Firm (or the Performance Companies) or its financial statements in each case resulting from changes in accounting methods, practices or policies, changes in capital structure by reason of legal or regulatory requirements and such other changed circumstances, as the Committee may deem appropriate.
summary:
- Equitable adjustments: The Committee may adjust awards up or down to preserve intended economics in response to unusual events, accounting changes, capital structure changes, or other changed circumstances.
- Interpretation and administration: The Committee has sole, binding authority to interpret the Plan/Award Agreement, determine reasons for termination, apply post-employment, cancellation, and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority. Determinations may be non-uniform and selective across participants.
- Amendment rights: The Committee or its nominee can amend the Award Agreement at any time, but not materially adversely affect participant rights without consent except to comply with laws/regulations/accounting rules or to adjust vesting dates/impose certain restrictions, subject to Section 409A. Amendments must be in writing signed by JPMorgan Chase’s Director of Human Resources.
- Severability/reformation: If any provision is unenforceable, the Firm, a court/arbitrator, or the Director of HR may reform it (e.g., service length, time, geography, scope) to make it enforceable.
- Accelerated distribution for government ethics/conflicts: If required by applicable ethics or conflict-of-interest rules due to government employment, the Firm may accelerate distribution of outstanding PSUs (including reinvested dividend equivalents) and waive holding requirements, provided this does not violate Section 409A. Acceleration does not change recovery periods under “Remedies,” which are based on original vesting/distribution dates.

Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity :  Upon receipt of 
satisfactory evidence that applicable United States federal, state, local, foreign or supranational ethics or conflict of interest laws or 
regulations require you to divest your interest in JPMorgan Chase PSUs, the Firm may accelerate the distribution of all or part of your 
outstanding award, including Reinvested Dividend Equivalent Share Units, effective on or before the required divestiture date and 
waive the Holding Requirement; provided that no accelerated distribution shall occur if the Firm determines that such acceleration 
will violate Section 409A of the Code. Accelerated distribution under this paragraph does not impact the dates as set forth in the 
“Remedies ” section above.  The time period for recovery shall be determined by the originally scheduled vesting date or distribution 
date prior to any acceleration event.
If you have voluntarily terminated your employment and have satisfied the requirements of the section captioned “ Government Office 
Requirements ”, acceleration shall apply (to extent required) to the percentage of your outstanding award that would continue to vest 
under that section. In the case of a termination of employment where the award is outstanding as a result of the subsections entitled 
“Job Elimination” or “Full Career Eligibility”, then acceleration shall apply, to the extent required, to the full outstanding award.  
Subject to the two foregoing sections, the number of shares of Common Stock to be received on acceleration shall be determined 
using the methodology set forth under the section captioned “ Death ”. 
To the extent you have vested shares under this award subject to the Holding Requirement and become subject to divestiture 
requirement as forth herein, the Firm may waive the holding period to the extent required.
Notwithstanding an accelerated distribution or waiver of the Holding Requirement pursuant to the foregoing, you will remain subject 
to the applicable terms of your Award Agreement as if your award had remained outstanding for the duration of the original vesting 
period and shares had been distributed as scheduled as of the vesting date, including, but not limited to, repayment obligations set 
forth in the section captioned “ Remedies ” and the employment restrictions in the sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ” and 
“Government Office Requirements ” and the subsection “Full Career Eligibility”.

title: Non-transferability
heading: 39.26 Non-transferability
start_phrase: Neither this award or any other outstanding awards of restricted stock units or of performance based share units, nor your interests or rights in any such awards, shall be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, hypothecated or subject to any lien.
summary:

“Average Tangible Common Equity”  means annual average common stockholders’ equity less annual average goodwill and annual 
average identifiable intangible assets.  Annual averages of the components of Average Tangible Common Equity will be calculated 
using quarterly balances as reported in publically available financial disclosures.  In the event that quarterly balances are not 
available, annual year end balances will be used. This calculation is used solely for purposes of the Performance Ranking.  
“Award Payout Percentage” means the applicable percentage specified in the footnote to the Performance Table.  
“Calculated PSUs”  means the number of PSUs determined by multiplying the Target Award Number (after giving effect to any 
cancellation thereof, in whole or in part) by the Award Payout Percentage corresponding to the Firm’s Performance Ranking based on 
the three-year average performance for the Performance Period (both percentage and ranking, as set forth in the footnote to the 
Performance Table); provided that if the average of the Firm’s Reported ROTCE for the Performance Period either equals or exceeds 
______% or is less than ______% (without taking into account any rounding conventions used), _________ percent or ________, respectively as the 
case may be, shall be substituted for the Performance Period’s Award Payout Percentage in calculating the number of PSUs to 
distribute. For avoidance of doubt, any cancellation of this award (in whole or in part) during the Performance Period will reduce the 
Target Award Number.
“Calculation Agent”  means a third party entity not owned or controlled by the Firm, such as an accounting or consulting firm, 
retained from time to time by the Director of Human Resources or his/her delegate.
“Cause”  means a determination by the Firm that your employment terminated as a result of your (i) violation of any law, rule or 
regulation (including rules of self-regulatory bodies) related to the Firm’s business, (ii) indictment or conviction of a felony, (iii) 
commission of a fraudulent act, (iv) violation of the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct or other Firm policies or misconduct related to 
your duties to the Firm (other than immaterial and inadvertent violations or misconduct), (v) grossly inadequate performance of the 
duties associated with your position or job function or failure to follow reasonable directives of your manager, or (vi) any act or 
failure to act that is injurious to the interests of the Firm or its relationship with a customer, client or an employee.
“Financial Services Company”  means a business enterprise that engages in any of the following services (itself or through an 
affiliate or subsidiary), regardless of whether such services are the principle strategy or revenue-generating activity:•commercial or retail banking, including, but not limited to, commercial, institutional and personal trust, custody and/or lending 
and processing services, internet banking, originating and servicing mortgages, issuing and servicing credit cards, payment 
servicing or processing or merchant services,
•insurance, including but not limited to, guaranteeing against loss, harm, damage, illness, disability or death, providing and issuing 
annuities, acting as principal, agent or broker for purpose of the forgoing,
•financial, investment or economic advisory services, including but not limited to, investment banking services (such as advising on 
mergers or dispositions, underwriting, dealing in, or making a market in securities or other similar activities), brokerage services, 
investment management services, asset management services, foreign exchange services, interbank networks and hedge funds,
•issuing, trading or selling instruments representing interests in pools of assets or in derivatives instruments, 
•financial technology (“Fintech”) companies, such as those selling blockchain services, or offering or selling financial products/
services,
•advising on, or investing in, private equity or real estate funds or ventures, or
•any similar activities that the Director of Human Resources or nominee determines in his or her sole discretion constitute financial 
services.
“Firm Reported ROTCE”  means the Firm’s percentage return on tangible common equity for each year in the Performance Period (as 
calculated for use in its  publicly available year-end financial disclosures without taking  into account any rounding conventions used 
for financial reporting purposes).
“Firmwide Financial Threshold”  means a cumulative return on tangible common equity for calendar years 20____, 20____ and 20____ of 
not less than ______%.  Cumulative return on tangible common equity means (i) the sum of the Firm’s reported net income for all three 
calendar years, divided by (ii) reported year-end tangible equity averaged over the three years.
“Government Office”  means (i) a full-time position in an elected or appointed office in local, state, or federal government (including 
equivalent positions outside the U.S. or in a supranational organization), not reasonably anticipated to be a full-career position, or (ii)

title: Government Office Requirements - Introduction
heading: 39.28 Government Office Requirements
start_phrase: You may be eligible to continue vesting in all or part of your award if you voluntarily resign to accept a Government Office (as defined above) or to become a candidate for an elective Government Office.
summary:
Government Office Requirements

text:
Government Office Requirements
You may be eligible to continue vesting in all or part of your award if you voluntarily resign to accept a Government Office (as defined 
above) or to become a candidate for an elective Government Office.

title: Full Career Eligibility
heading: 39.28.1 Full Career Eligibility
start_phrase: “Government Office Requirements ” does not apply to you if you satisfy the subsection captioned “--Full Career Eligibility” as of the date that you voluntarily terminate your employment with the Firm.
summary:
- Defines “Performance Companies” as peer institutions with revenue mixes overlapping the firm’s, and allows the committee to adjust the peer list prospectively for mergers, spin‑offs, bankruptcies, sales, or other material business changes (including adding acquirers).
- Sets the “Performance Period” as three specified calendar years.
- Establishes “Performance Ranking” based on the firm’s average ROTCE versus the peers’ average ROTCE, tied to a “Performance Table” that maps relative rankings/ROTCE to Award Payout Percentages.
- Provides tie‑breaking rules for rankings, stating that ties are disregarded in determining payout, with examples for how ties between the firm and peers, and among peers, are treated.
- Defines “Recognized Service” per the firm’s service‑related policies.
- Defines “ROTCE” (earnings from continuing operations less preferred dividends divided by Average Tangible Common Equity for each year) and requires recalculation and adjusted rankings if the firm or a peer restates financials within the vesting period; this calculation is solely for determining Performance Ranking.
- Defines “Target Award Number” for PSUs as specified in the Award Agreement.
- Outlines Government Office Requirements: potential eligibility to continue vesting if voluntarily resigning to accept or run for elective Government Office, unless the individual already meets Full Career Eligibility.
- States eligibility conditions for continued vesting upon Government Office resignation, including at least 60 days’ advance written notice, performing requested services cooperatively during the notice period, refraining from working for another employer during that time, and the firm’s discretion to shorten the notice period.
text:
Full Career Eligibility:   
“Government Office Requirements ” does not apply to you if you satisfy the subsection captioned “--Full Career Eligibility” as of the 
date that you voluntarily terminate your employment with the Firm.

title: Eligibility
heading: 39.28.2 Eligibility
start_phrase: Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
summary:
- Defines key terms for a PSU (Performance Share Unit) award tied to relative ROTCE performance: Performance Companies, Performance Period, Performance Ranking, Performance Table, Recognized Service, ROTCE, and Target Award Number.
- Performance Companies: peer institutions with materially similar revenue mix; Committee may prospectively remove, replace, or adjust peers after mergers, spin‑offs, bankruptcies, sales, or material business changes (including adding acquirers/new companies).
- Performance Period: three specified calendar years.
- ROTCE: calculated annually as earnings from continuing operations minus preferred dividends divided by Average Tangible Common Equity; if financials are restated, ROTCE and rankings are recalculated solely for award purposes.
- Performance Ranking and Performance Table: award payouts are determined by the Firm’s average ROTCE ranking versus peers according to a predefined payout scale; a detailed rank-to-payout mapping applies; tie-handling rules favor treating tied rankings as satisfied without penalizing the Firm and adjust peer rankings accordingly.
- Target Award Number: the number of PSUs designated in the Award Agreement.
- Recognized Service: employee service period per Firm policy, used in vesting determinations.
- Government Office Requirements: outlines eligibility for continued vesting if an employee resigns to accept or run for a Government Office, unless the employee already meets Full Career Eligibility.
- Eligibility conditions for continued vesting: at least 60 days’ advance written notice while continuing to serve the Firm and not another employer (Firm may shorten notice), confirmation of legal compliance, and documentation of government service/candidacy purpose.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award) based on continuous service at termination: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years); the remainder is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to receive CV Award: hold a non‑elective Government Office for ≥2 years (or have a vesting date occur during a shorter government service), or for elective office, have name on the primary or final ballot; performance and protection‑based vesting conditions continue to apply.
- Satisfaction of conditions: upon meeting them (including unsuccessful election after appearing on a ballot), outstanding and previously accelerated awards resume standard vesting terms and employment restrictions as if Full Career Eligibility had been met.
- Failure to satisfy conditions: CV Award PSUs are canceled; the participant must repay the Fair Market Value of shares previously accelerated that would otherwise have remained outstanding PSUs, valued as of distribution date.
- References an accelerated distribution mechanism for ethics/conflict reasons arising from government employment, with specifics cross‑referenced elsewhere in the agreement.
text:
Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
•At least 60 days’ advance written notice of your intention to resign to accept or pursue a Government Office (see section 
captioned “ Definitions ”), during which period you must perform in a cooperative and professional manner services requested by 
the Firm and not provide services for any other employer.  The Firm may elect to shorten this notice period at the Firm’s sole 
discretion.•Confirmation, in a form satisfactory to the Firm, that vesting in this award pursuant to this provision would not violate any 
applicable law, regulation or rule.
•Documentation in a form satisfactory to the Firm that your resignation is for the purpose of accepting a Government Office or 
becoming a candidate for a Government Office.  (See section captioned “ Definitions ”.)

title: Portion of Your Award Subject to Continued Vesting
heading: 39.28.3 Portion of Your Award Subject to Continued Vesting
start_phrase: Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of this award that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s original schedule will be based on your years of continuous service completed with the Firm immediately preceding your termination date, as follows:
summary:
Summary of main points:
- Purpose: Outlines when a portion of a performance share unit (PSU) award will continue to vest if an employee resigns to accept or campaign for a Government Office.
- Required documentation: (1) Confirmation that continued vesting complies with applicable laws/regulations; (2) Proof the resignation is to accept or run for a Government Office.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award): Based on continuous service at termination—50% (≥3 to <4 years), 75% (≥4 to <5 years), 100% (≥5 years); the remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions to receive CV Award: (a) Serve in a non-elective Government Office for at least two years after termination (or have a vesting date occur during a shorter non-elective term), or (b) for elective roles, have your name on the primary or final public ballot.
- Ongoing requirements: Original performance and protection-based vesting criteria still apply to the CV Award.
- If conditions are satisfied: Outstanding CV Awards (and those previously accelerated for ethics/conflict reasons) continue under the Award Agreement for the remaining vesting period as if the employee met Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions.
- If conditions are not met: Outstanding CV Award PSUs are cancelled, and the employee must repay the fair market value of any shares previously distributed early due to ethics/conflict-related accelerated distribution.
text:
Portion of Your Award Subject to Continued Vesting:
Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of this award that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s original 
schedule will be based on your years of continuous service completed with the Firm immediately preceding your termination date, as 
follows:
•50% if you have at least 3 but less than 4 years of continuous service,
•75% if you have at least 4 but less than 5 years of continuous service, or
•100% if you have 5 or more years of continuous service. 
The portion of this award subject to continued vesting above is referred to as the “CV Award” and the portion not subject to continued 
vesting will be cancelled as of the date your employment terminates.

title: Conditions for Continued Vesting of Award
heading: 39.28.4 Conditions for Continued Vesting of Award
start_phrase: You must remain in a non-elective Government Office for two or more years after your employment with the Firm terminates to be eligible to receive the CV Award; provided that if your non-elective Government Office is for a period less than two years, you will be eligible to receive the CV Award if it has a vesting date during your period of Government Service; or
summary:
- Sets documentation requirements: confirmation that continued vesting complies with applicable laws and proof that resignation is to accept or run for a Government Office.
- Defines portion of award eligible for continued vesting (CV Award) based on continuous service at termination: 50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (5+ years); non-eligible portion is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions for CV Award:
  - Non-elective Government Office: must serve at least two years post-termination; if the office term is under two years, eligibility applies only to tranches vesting during the government service.
  - Elective office candidacy: name must appear on the primary or final public ballot; if not elected, employment restrictions apply.
- Confirms that performance and protection-based vesting criteria continue to apply to the CV Award.
- Upon satisfying conditions (including unsuccessful election after appearing on a ballot), any then-outstanding CV Awards and awards that would have been outstanding but for accelerated distribution remain subject to the Award Agreement terms and employment restrictions as if the employee had Full Career Eligibility.
- Failure to satisfy conditions results in cancellation of outstanding PSUs under the CV Award and a clawback: repayment of the fair market value of shares previously distributed via accelerated distribution that would have remained outstanding PSUs, valued as of the distribution date.
- References accelerated distribution mechanisms for ethics or conflict reasons arising from government employment and reiterates ongoing employment restrictions during the remaining vesting period.
text:
Conditions for Continued Vesting of Award:
•You must remain in a non-elective Government Office for two or more years after your employment with the Firm terminates to be 
eligible to receive the CV Award; provided that if your non-elective Government Office is for a period less than two years, you will 
be eligible to receive the CV Award if it has a vesting date during your period of Government Service; or 
•In the case of resignation from the Firm to campaign for an elective Government Office, your name must be on the primary or final 
public ballot for the election. (If you are not elected, see below for employment restrictions.)
For avoidance of doubt, the performance criteria and protection based vesting set forth in these terms and conditions continue to 
apply to a CV Award.

title: Satisfaction of Conditions
heading: 39.28.5 Satisfaction of Conditions
start_phrase: If your service in a Government Office ends two years or more after your employment with the Firm terminates, or in the case of resignation from the Firm to campaign for a Government Office,
summary:
- Scope: Explains how a performance share/unit award may continue to vest when an employee resigns to accept or campaign for a Government Office.
- Required documentation: (1) Confirmation acceptable to the Firm that continued vesting would not violate any law, regulation, or rule; and (2) proof acceptable to the Firm that the resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (the “CV Award”): Based on continuous service at termination—50% (3 to <4 years), 75% (4 to <5 years), 100% (5+ years). The non-eligible portion is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to receive the CV Award:
  - Service in a non-elective Government Office for at least two years after termination; if the office term is under two years, eligibility applies if a vesting date occurs during the government service; or
  - For elective office, the individual’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot.
  - Performance and protection-based vesting criteria continue to apply to the CV Award.
- Satisfaction of conditions: If government service ends at or after two years, or the individual runs, appears on a ballot, and is not elected, then any then-outstanding CV Awards and any awards otherwise outstanding but for an accelerated distribution due to ethics/conflict from government employment will continue for the remaining vesting period under the same terms as a resignation with Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions.
- Failure to satisfy conditions: All outstanding PSUs under the CV Award are canceled. The individual must repay the fair market value (pre-withholding) of any shares previously distributed via accelerated distribution that would otherwise have remained outstanding as PSUs on the failure date, with fair market value measured as of the distribution date.
text:
Satisfaction of Conditions:
If your service in a Government Office ends two years or more after your employment with the Firm terminates, or in the case of 
resignation from the Firm to campaign for a Government Office, your name is on the primary or final public ballot for the election and 
you are not elected, any CV Awards then outstanding and any such awards that would have then been outstanding but for an 
accelerated distribution of shares (as described in the subsection captioned “--Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons 
Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity”) will be subject for the remainder of the applicable vesting period to the same 
terms and conditions of this Award Agreement, including employment restrictions during the vesting period, as if you had resigned 
from the Firm having met the  requirements for Full Career Eligibility.

title: Failure to Satisfy Conditions
heading: 39.28.6 Failure to Satisfy Conditions
start_phrase: If you do not satisfy the above “Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards”, any outstanding PSUs under the CV Award will be cancelled.
summary:
- Purpose: Outlines when and how equity awards (PSUs) may continue to vest if an employee resigns to accept or run for a Government Office.
- Required documentation: Confirmation acceptable to the Firm that continued vesting is lawful; proof that resignation is to accept a Government Office or to become a candidate (per Definitions).
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award): Based on continuous service with the Firm immediately before termination—50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years). The remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions to receive CV Award:
  - Non-elective office: Must serve 2+ years after leaving the Firm; if the term is under 2 years, eligibility applies if a vesting date occurs during the government service.
  - Elective office (campaign): Name must appear on the primary or final ballot. Notes that employment restrictions apply if not elected.

title: Calculation of Performance Ranking

start_phrase: For purposes of the Performance Ranking, the ranking of the Firm and of each Performance Company for the Performance Period shall be determined and calculated by the Calculation Agent, using the definitions of “Average Tangible Common Equity” (if otherwise applicable), “Calculated PSUs”, “Firm Reported ROTCE”, “Performance Table” (including its footnote) and “ROTCE” as set forth in the “Definitions ” section of these terms and conditions.

Calculation of Performance Ranking

“Definitions ” section of these terms and conditions.  See section captioned “ Definitions ”.  Except for Firm Reported ROTCE, 
calculations will be expressed as a decimal to the second place (i.e. xx.yy%), rounded to the nearest hundredth.  See section 
captioned, “ Definitions --Performance Table” in the event of a tie.  All performance based calculations as set forth herein are binding 
and conclusive on you and your successors.

Results (except Firm Reported ROTCE) are rounded to the nearest hundredth (xx.yy%). Tie-breaking follows the Performance Table. All calculations are final and binding.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If the firm’s CET1 ratio is below a preset threshold at any year-end, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs can be reduced by the CMDC for each such year.
- Qualitative Performance Factor: Annually, the Committee assesses performance across four categories—Client/Customer Focus; Risk, Controls & Conduct; Teamwork & Leadership; Business Results. “Meets” expectations yields a 100% factor (no reduction for that year’s one-third of Target PSUs). “Not Meet” can trigger a 0–99% factor and corresponding reduction; a 0% factor each year cancels the award. The Committee may alternatively assess performance over the full three-year period and apply one factor to all PSUs; a 0% factor cancels the award. Input is sought from the UK Remuneration Committee Chair regarding UK Senior Manager regulatory responsibilities. Up to 50% of otherwise distributable PSUs at any vesting date (“At Risk PSUs”) may be cancelled at the CEO’s discretion based on: sustained underperformance versus role or Firm/Operating Committee priorities (considering metrics such as net income, total net revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers); negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income; cancellation of RSUs in a Line of Business under the employee’s responsibility for missing its LOB Financial Threshold; or failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
text:
Capital Ratio Performance Threshold 
Unvested PSUs are subject to reduction if the Firm’s Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio at any year end falls below a 
predetermined threshold of _______%.
If the Firm’s CET1 capital ratio at any year end during the Performance Period is below this predetermined threshold, up to one-third 
of the Target Award Number of PSUs will be subject to downward adjustment by the CMDC for each such year.

title: Qualitative Performance
heading: 40.7 Qualitative Performance
start_phrase: Determination of Qualitative Performance Factor.
summary:
- Performance Ranking methodology: A Calculation Agent determines the Firm and each Performance Company’s ranking for the Performance Period using defined terms (Average Tangible Common Equity, Calculated PSUs, Firm Reported ROTCE, Performance Table and footnote, ROTCE) from the Definitions section. Calculations (except Firm Reported ROTCE) are shown to two decimal places (xx.yy%), rounded to the nearest hundredth. Tie-breaking follows the “Definitions—Performance Table.” All performance calculations are binding and conclusive.
- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: Unvested PSUs may be reduced if the Firm’s CET1 ratio falls below a preset year-end threshold. For each year below the threshold during the Performance Period, up to one-third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced by the CMDC.
- Qualitative Performance Factor: Annually assessed across four categories—Client/Customer Focus; Risk, Controls & Conduct; Teamwork & Leadership; Business Results. “Meets” expectations = 100% factor (no downward adjustment) for that year; “Not Meet” may trigger a downward adjustment to 0–99%. A 0% factor for each year would cancel the award (no shares vest). The Committee may alternatively assess qualitative performance over the entire three-year Performance Period and apply one factor to the total PSUs determined under “Number of Performance Share Units at End of the Performance Period”; a 0% factor cancels the award. Assessment incorporates feedback from the Chair of the UK Remuneration Committee for Senior Manager responsibilities in CIB UK-regulated entities. The factor applies only for periods of employment (or as soon as administratively practical).
- Protection-based vesting and potential cancellation: Awards are intended to vest on scheduled dates if continuously employed or if eligible under Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability. Vesting and PSU amounts remain subject to these terms, including “Number of PSUs at End of Performance Period,” “Capital Ratio Performance Threshold,” “Recapture Provisions,” and “Remedies.” Up to 50% of otherwise distributable PSUs at a vesting date (“At Risk PSUs”) may be cancelled at the CEO’s sole discretion based on: (1) sustained unsatisfactory performance by you or the Firm against stated priorities (considering metrics such as net income, total net revenue, EPS, and capital ratios, absolute and relative to peers); (2) negative Firm-level annual pre-tax pre-provision income; (3) cancellation of RSUs in a Line of Business you oversee due to failure to meet its LOB Financial Threshold; or (4) failure to meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold.
text:
Qualitative Performance 
Determination of Qualitative Performance Factor.  Annually during the Performance Period, the Committee will formally assess your 
qualitative performance based on four broad categories: (1) Client/Customer Focus; (2) Risk, Controls & Conduct; (3) Teamwork & 
Leadership; and (4) Business Results. If the Committee determines that your performance “Meets” expectations, no downward 
adjustment to one-third of the Target Award Number of PSUs for that year shall take place (and the Qualitative Performance Factor 
shall be 100%). If the Committee determines that your performance did “Not Meet” expectations, the Committee shall determine 
whether a downward adjustment is appropriate, and if so, to what extent.  A downward adjustment could result in a Qualitative 
Performance Factor of between 0% and 99%, depending on the circumstances.  During the Performance Period, a 0% Performance 
Factor for each year in the Performance Period would reduce your Target Award Number of PSUs to zero, resulting in the cancellation 
of award with no shares vesting. 
Additionally, the Committee may, in its sole discretion, make such assessment of your qualitative performance based on your 
performance during the entire three year Performance Period and apply the Qualitative Performance Factor to the entire number of 
PSUs determined  under  section captioned “Number of Performance Share Units at End of the Performance Period”.  In the case of a 
Qualitative Performance Factor of 0%, the award would be cancelled.
The assessment will have regard to feedback solicited from the Chair of the UK Remuneration Committee to incorporate qualitative 
performance against local regulatory responsibilities as a “Senior Manager” of the relevant CIB UK-regulated entities.
The Qualitative Performance Factor shall only be applied, if applicable, in respect of a period of your employment with the Firm, or as 
soon as administratively practical.

title: Protection-Based Vesting

- Capital Ratio Performance Threshold: If the Firm’s CET1 ratio falls below a preset threshold at any year-end during the Performance Period, up to one‑third of the Target Award PSUs may be reduced by the CMDC for each such year.

A 0% each year cancels the award. Committee may alternatively assess performance over the full three‑year period and apply one factor to all PSUs determined at period end; a 0% cancels the award. text:
Protection-Based Vesting
This award is intended and expected to vest on each vesting date set forth in your Award Agreement, provided that you are 
continuously employed by the Firm through such vesting date, or you meet the requirements for continued vesting described under 
the subsections “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability”.  However, vesting and the 
number of PSUs that will vest are subject to these terms and conditions (including, but not limited to, sections captioned “ Number of 
Performance Share Units at the end of Performance Period ”, “Capital Ratio Performance Threshold ”, “Recapture Provisions ”, 
“Remedies ” and the following protection-based vesting provision).  
Up to a total of fifty percent of your award that would otherwise be distributable to you as of any vesting date (“At Risk PSUs”) may 
be cancelled if the Chief Executive Officer of JPMorgan Chase (“CEO”) determines in his or her sole discretion that cancellation of all 
or portion of the At Risk PSUs is appropriate in light of any one or a combination of the following factors:
•Your performance in relation to the priorities for your position, or the Firm’s performance in relation to the priorities for which 
you share responsibility as a member of the Operating Committee, have been unsatisfactory for a sustained period of time.  
Among the factors the CEO may consider in assessing performance are: net income, total net revenue, earnings per share and 
capital ratios of the Firm, both on an absolute basis and, as appropriate, relative to peer firms. 
•For any calendar year ending during the vesting period, JPMorgan Chase’s annual pre-tax pre-provision income at the Firm level is 
negative.
•RSU awards granted to participants in a Line of Business for which you exercise, or during the vesting period exercised, direct or 
indirect responsibility, were in whole or in part cancelled because the Line of Business did not meet its annual Line of Business 
Financial Threshold.  
•The Firm does not meet the Firmwide Financial Threshold. For avoidance of doubt, cancellation of the At Risk PSUs, in whole or part, for one or more of the above factors may occur prior to the 
end of the Performance Period and the maximum number of At Risk PSUs subject to cancellation prior to the end of the Performance 
Period will be up to fifty percent of the Target Award Number.  
In the event that your employment terminates due to “Job Elimination”, ”Full Career Eligibility”, “Government Office” or “Disability” 
thereby entitling you to continued vesting in your award, (or potentially acceleration due to satisfaction of the Government Office 
Requirements), the cancellation circumstances described above will continue to apply.
Any determination above with respect to protection-based vesting provisions is subject to ratification by the Compensation and 
Management Development Committee of the Board of Directors of JPMorgan Chase (“Committee”).  In the case of an award to any 
current or former CEO, all such determinations shall be made by the Committee and ratified by the Board.

title: EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff
heading: 40.10 EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff
start_phrase: In consideration of grant of this award, and without prejudice to any other provision of this Award Agreement, you agree that you are subject to the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff (and any applicable supplement(s) to that policy) or successor policy as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance year ______ and to this award.
summary:
- Up to 50% of At Risk PSUs may be canceled before the end of the Performance Period based on specified factors; these cancellation conditions continue to apply even if the participant becomes entitled to continued vesting or potential acceleration due to Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, or Disability.
- Any determinations related to protection-based vesting require ratification by JPMorgan Chase’s Compensation and Management Development Committee; for current or former CEOs, the Committee makes determinations which are then ratified by the Board.
- The award and the cash incentive for the relevant performance year are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy, and nothing in the award terms limits the Firm’s rights under that policy.
- Identified Staff are also subject to the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy (and any supplements), which allows reduction or recovery of awards in circumstances such as material downturn in Firm performance or increased capital requirements; these circumstances align with existing Firmwide terms like the Bonus Recoupment Policy and Protection-Based Vesting.
- Upon termination of employment, the award is generally canceled effective on the termination date, except under specified cases (Job Elimination, Full Career Eligibility, Government Office, Disability, or Death), in which continued vesting may occur subject to all applicable terms (including Protection-Based Vesting, Bonus Recoupment, EMEA Malus and Clawback, Your Obligations, and Remedies).
- For continued vesting due to Job Elimination, the HR Director (or nominee) must determine that the job was eliminated, the participant cooperated professionally after notice as requested, and the Release/Certification Requirements were satisfied.
text:
EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff
In consideration of grant of this award, and without prejudice to any other provision of this Award Agreement, you agree that you are 
subject to the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff (and any applicable supplement(s) to that policy) or 
successor policy as in effect from time to time as it applies both to the cash incentive compensation awarded to you for performance 
year ______ and to this award. 
The provisions of the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff set out the terms and conditions applying to 
the grant of this award which ensure that the Firm is able to meet its regulatory obligations to operate malus (reduce) and/or 
clawback (recover) to awards in certain circumstances.  These include, but are not limited to, where (i) there is a material downturn 
in the Firm’s financial performance or (ii) where the Firm is required to hold more capital. The circumstances in which the events at 
(i) and (ii) would occur are analogous to some of the circumstances considered under the existing Firmwide terms and conditions, in 
particular the Bonus Recoupment Policy and the Protection Based Vesting provisions.
You can access this policy as currently in effect in My Rewards through the following link:  https://myrewards.jpmorganchase.com

title: Termination of Employment
heading: 40.11 Termination of Employment
start_phrase: Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, this award will be cancelled in full effective on the date your employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
summary:
- Clarifies that up to 50% of At Risk PSUs (relative to the Target Award Number) may be cancelled before the end of the Performance Period based on specified factors, and such cancellation rules continue to apply even if vesting continues after certain qualifying terminations.
- States that protection-based vesting determinations are subject to ratification by JPMorgan Chase’s Compensation and Management Development Committee; for current or former CEOs, the Committee makes determinations subject to Board ratification.
- Confirms the award and related cash incentive compensation are subject to the JPMorgan Chase Bonus Recoupment Policy, without limiting the Firm’s rights under that policy; provides a link to the governance page.
- Extends the JPMorgan Chase EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff to the award and related cash incentives, enabling malus/clawback in circumstances such as material financial downturns or increased capital requirements; notes alignment with Firmwide Bonus Recoupment and Protection-Based Vesting provisions; provides access via My Rewards.
- Provides that, unless specified otherwise, the award is cancelled upon employment termination; outlines exceptions allowing continued vesting if conditions are met:
  - Job Elimination: Requires HR determination of role elimination, cooperative/professional services after notice, and satisfaction of release/certification requirements.
  - Full Career Eligibility: Requires voluntary termination; at least 5 years of continuous service; 15 years Recognized Service or 30 years combined Recognized Service plus external experience; 180 days advance written notice with cooperative service and no outside work; a pre-termination determination that continued vesting is appropriate; a 36-month post-grant restriction on working for a Financial Services Company or in the same profession (with exceptions for government, education, or not-for-profit); and satisfaction of release/certification requirements. The Firm may require service during the notice period or shorten it (not earlier than meeting service requirements). Additional local notice policies may apply.
  - Government Office: Voluntary termination to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to Government Office Requirements and definitions.
  - Disability: Termination due to qualifying LTD status (or equivalent/qualifying long-term disability as determined by the Firm or its designee), with written request for continued vesting within 30 days, supporting documentation, Firm’s written consent, and satisfaction of release/certification requirements.
- Details Release/Certification requirements: execution of a Firm-specified release of claims; for Full Career Eligibility, pre-termination confirmation of eligibility and written consent; for Full Career Eligibility and Government Office, ongoing certifications before each vesting date confirming compliance with employment restrictions; for Disability, required notices/documentation and consent; and compliance with all Award Agreement terms.
- Provides death provisions: if the participant dies while eligible to vest, the designated beneficiary (or estate if none/invalid) may receive the associated shares.
text:
Termination of Employment
Except as explicitly set forth below under the subsections captioned “--Job Elimination”, “--Full Career Eligibility”, “--Government 
Office” or “--Disability” or under the section captioned “ Death ”, this award will be cancelled in full effective on the date your 
employment with the Firm terminates for any reason.
Subject to these terms and conditions (including, but not limited to, sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Bonus 
Recoupment ”, “EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy - Identified Staff ”, “Your Obligations ” and “ Remedies ”) you will be eligible to 
continue to vest (as you otherwise would vest if you were still employed by JPMorgan Chase) with respect to your award in 
accordance with its terms and conditions following the termination of your employment if one of the following circumstances applies 
to you:
•Job Elimination 
In the event that the Director of Human Resources or nominee in his or her sole discretion determines that 
•the Firm terminated your employment because your job was eliminated, and  
•after you are notified that your job will be eliminated, you provided such services as requested by the Firm in a cooperative 
and professional manner, and 
•you satisfied the Release/Certification Requirements set forth below.
•Full Career Eligibility 
In the event that the Director of Human Resources or nominee in his or her sole discretion determines that •you voluntarily terminated your employment with the Firm, had completed at least five years of continuous service with the 
Firm immediately preceding your termination date, and 
•your Recognized Service (as defined below) on your date of termination equaled or exceeded 15 years, or your combined 
Recognized Service with the Firm and external professional experience (as attested by you to the Firm) equaled or exceeded 
30 years, and
•you provided at least 180 days advance written notice to the Firm of your intention to voluntarily terminate your employment 
under this provision, during which notice period you provided such services as requested by the Firm in a cooperative and 
professional manner and you did not perform any services for any other employer, and 
•continued vesting shall be appropriate, which determination shall be made prior to your termination and will be based on 
your performance and conduct (before and after providing notice), and  
•for 36 months from the date of grant of this award, you do not either perform services in any capacity (such as an employee, 
contractor, consultant advisor, or self-employed individual, whether paid or unpaid) for a Financial Services Company (as 
defined below) or work in your profession (whether or not for a Financial Services Company); provided that you may work for 
a government, education or Not-for-Profit Organization (as defined below), and
•you satisfied the Release/Certification Requirements set forth below. 
After receipt of such advance written notice, the Firm may choose to have you continue to provide services during such 180-day 
period as a condition to continued vesting or shorten the length of the 180-day period at the Firm’s sole discretion, but to a date 
no earlier than the date you would otherwise meet the service requirement. 
Additional advance notice requirements may apply for employees subject to notice period policies.  (See “Notice Period” below.)
•Government Office 
In the event that you voluntarily terminate your employment with the Firm to accept a Government Office or become a candidate 
for an elective Government Office, as described at the end of these terms and conditions under the section captioned 
“Government Office Requirements ”.  See also definition of Government Office in the section captioned “ Definitions ”.
•Disability 
In the event that 
•your employment with the Firm terminates because (i) you are unable to return to work while you are receiving benefits 
under the JPMorgan Chase Long Term Disability Plan, or for non-U.S. employees, under the equivalent JPMorgan Chase-

title: Release/Certification
heading: 40.12 Release/Certification
start_phrase: To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
summary:
- Outlines conditions for continued vesting after voluntary termination under “Full Career Eligibility,” including:
  - At least 5 years of continuous service immediately before termination.
  - Recognized Service of 15+ years, or combined Firm Recognized Service and external professional experience totaling 30+ years.
  - At least 180 days’ advance written notice, during which the employee must perform requested services cooperatively, refrain from working for any other employer, and comply with Firm direction; Firm may require service during the notice or shorten it (not earlier than meeting service requirements).
  - Firm’s prior determination that continued vesting is appropriate based on performance and conduct.
  - For 36 months from grant, no services in any capacity for a Financial Services Company or in the employee’s profession; work allowed for government, education, or Not-for-Profit organizations.
  - Satisfaction of Release/Certification requirements.
  - Additional notice period policies may apply.
- Provides a separate path for continued vesting upon voluntary termination to accept or run for a Government Office, subject to “Government Office Requirements” and defined terms.
- Details disability-related continued vesting if employment ends due to qualifying long-term disability under the Firm’s LTD Plan (or equivalent), or a disability that would qualify:
  - Employee must request continued vesting within 30 days of termination, provide documentation, and obtain the Firm’s written consent.
  - Must also satisfy Release/Certification requirements.
- Specifies Release/Certification Requirements:
  - Execute a Firm-specified release of claims.
  - For Full Career Eligibility: confirm eligibility with management in advance (including 180-day notice) and obtain written consent.
  - For Full Career Eligibility and Government Office: certify compliance with post-employment restrictions before each vesting date while restrictions apply.
  - For Disability: meet notice/documentation requirements and obtain written consent.
  - Comply with all other Award Agreement obligations (“Your Obligations”).
- Provides death provisions: if the employee dies while eligible to vest, the designated beneficiary (or estate, as applicable) may receive shares associated with the award.
- References definitions (e.g., Recognized Service, Financial Services Company, Not-for-Profit, Government Office) and related sections (Notice Period, Government Office Requirements, Your Obligations).
text:
Release/Certification 
To qualify for continued vesting after termination of your employment under any of the foregoing circumstances:
• you must timely execute and deliver a release of claims in favor of the Firm, having such form and terms as the Firm shall 
specify,
• with respect to Full Career Eligibility, prior to the termination of your employment, you must confirm with management that you 
meet the eligibility criteria (including providing at least 180 days advance written notification), advise  that you are seeking to be 
treated as an individual eligible for Full Career Eligibility, and receive written consent to such continued vesting, 
• with respect to “Full Career Eligibility” and “Government Office”, it is your responsibility to take the appropriate steps to certify 
to the Firm prior to each vesting date while the employment restrictions are outstanding on the authorized form of the Firm that 
you have complied with the employment restrictions applicable to you (as described herein) from your date of termination of 
employment through the applicable vesting date,  
• with respect to Disability, you must satisfy the notice and documentation described above and receive written consent to such 
continued vesting, and 
• in all cases, otherwise complied with all other terms of the Award Agreement.  (See section captioned “ Your Obligations ” below.)

title: Death
heading: 40.13 Death
start_phrase: If you die while you are eligible to vest in this award, your designated beneficiary on file with the Firm’s Stock Administration Department (or your estate or if no beneficiary has been designated or survives you or if beneficiary designation is not recognized locally) may be entitled to receive a distribution of a number of shares of Common Stock associated with your award.
summary:
- Conditions for continued vesting after employment ends
  - Full Career Eligibility: requires at least 5 years of continuous service; 15+ years of Recognized Service or 30+ years combined Recognized Service and attested external professional experience; at least 180 days’ advance written notice; provision of services during the notice period without working for another employer; Firm’s prior determination that continued vesting is appropriate based on performance and conduct; and a 36‑month post‑grant restriction on working in financial services or in your profession (with exceptions for government, education, or not‑for‑profit roles). Release/Certification requirements apply. The Firm may require service during the notice period or shorten it (not earlier than meeting service requirements). Additional notice rules may apply under the Notice Period policy.
  - Government Office: eligibility to continue vesting if you resign to accept or run for an elective government office, subject to specific Government Office Requirements and definitions.
  - Disability: eligibility if employment ends due to long‑term disability qualifying under the LTD Plan or equivalent; must request continued vesting within 30 days, provide documentation, and receive the Firm’s written consent; Release/Certification requirements apply.

- Release/Certification requirements to qualify for continued vesting
  - Execute a Firm‑specified release of claims.
  - For Full Career Eligibility: confirm eligibility with management before termination (including 180‑day notice) and obtain written consent.
  - For Full Career Eligibility and Government Office: certify compliance with post‑employment restrictions prior to each vest date while restrictions apply.
  - For Disability: meet notice/documentation requirements and obtain written consent.
  - Comply with all other terms of the Award Agreement.

- Death provisions
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period, the beneficiary/estate receives shares equal to any outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, payout is based on average performance of completed calendar years, one‑third of target PSUs for each completed year, and 100% Award Payout Percentage for remaining years.
  - Distribution no later than the end of the calendar year following death (administrative practice targets registration within 60 days of receiving required documentation).

- Participant obligations tied to the award
  - Non‑Solicitation of Employees and Customers: for the longer of one year post‑termination or three years from grant date (if the award is not canceled), restrictions on soliciting/hiring Firm employees and soliciting/diverting Firm customers, with specified exceptions and alignment to applicable law.
  - Confidential Information: prohibition on using/disclosing Firm confidential information or communicating with media; no access to Firm systems post‑termination without authorization; whistleblower and legal/regulatory response carve‑outs per Code of Conduct and law.
  - Non‑Disparagement: prohibition on public statements that disparage the Firm or its stakeholders, with carve‑outs for lawful reporting and truthful regulatory/legal responses.
  - Cooperation: obligation to cooperate with the Firm and its counsel on matters such as audits, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings.

- Cross‑references and definitions noted
  - References to “Recognized Service,” “Financial Services Company,” “Not‑for‑Profit Organization,” “Government Office,” “Performance Period,” “Award Payout Percentage,” and the “Notice Period” policy, which are defined or detailed elsewhere in the full document.
text:
Death
If you die while you are eligible to vest in this award, your designated beneficiary on file with the Firm’s Stock Administration 
Department (or your estate or if no beneficiary has been designated or survives you or if beneficiary designation is not recognized 
locally) may be entitled to receive a distribution of a number of shares of Common Stock associated with your award.  Should you die after the end of the Performance Period, your beneficiary will receive shares of Common Stock equal to any 
outstanding PSUs.  
Should you die during the Performance Period, your Beneficiary will receive shares of Common Stock based on the average 
performance of all completed calendar years, multiplied by one-third of the Target Award Number of PSUs for each completed 
calendar year in the Performance Period, and using the Award Payout Percentage equal to 100 percent for any remaining calendar 
years in the Performance Period.  
Any shares will be distributed no later than the end of the calendar year immediately following the calendar year which contains your 
date of death; however, our administrative practice is to register such shares in the name of your beneficiary or estate within 60 days 
of the Firm’s receipt of any required documentation.
