Your Obligations
In consideration of the grant of this award, you agree to comply with and be bound by the obligations set forth below next to the 
subsections captioned “--Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers”, “--Confidential Information”, “--Non-Disparagement”, ”--
Cooperation”, “--Compliance with Award Agreement”, and “--Notice Period”.

title: Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
heading: 40.14.1 Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
start_phrase: During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date, you will not directly or indirectly, whether on your own behalf or on behalf of any other party, without the prior written consent of the Director of Human Resources: (i) solicit, induce or encourage any of the Firm’s then current employees to leave the Firm or to apply for employment elsewhere, unless such current employee has received official, written notice that his or her employment will be terminated due to job elimination (ii) hire any employee or former employee who was employed by the Firm at the date your employment terminated, unless the individual’s employment terminated because his or her job was eliminated, or the individual’s employment with the Firm has been terminated for more than six months, (iii) to the fullest extent enforceable under applicable law, solicit or induce or attempt to induce to leave the Firm, or divert or attempt to divert from doing business with the Firm, any then current customers, suppliers or other persons or entities that were serviced by you or whose names became known to you by virtue of your employment with the Firm, or otherwise interfere with the relationship between the Firm and such customers, suppliers or other persons or entities.
summary:
- Death benefits for PSUs:
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period ends, the beneficiary receives shares equal to any outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares based on the average performance of completed calendar years, calculated as one-third of the Target Award per completed year, and assumes a 100% Award Payout Percentage for any remaining years.
  - Distribution timing: no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, shares are typically registered to the beneficiary or estate within 60 days after required documentation is received.

- Employee obligations tied to the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers:
    - Applies during employment and for the longer of one year post-termination or three years from Grant Date if the award isn’t cancelled at termination.
    - Prohibits soliciting or encouraging Firm employees to leave; hiring certain current/former employees (with exceptions for job eliminations or if more than six months have passed since termination); and, to the extent enforceable, soliciting or diverting customers/suppliers known or serviced through employment. Publicly known institutional customers may be serviced post-employment without using Firm confidential information.
    - Excludes authorized actions taken in the normal scope of employment.
  - Confidential information:
    - Prohibits using or disclosing Firm confidential information and communicating with media about Firm matters during and after employment, except as permitted by the Code of Conduct, policies, law, or legal process.
    - Post-termination, prohibits unauthorized access to internal Firm systems.
    - Allows reporting suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations to management, regulators, government, attorneys, or courts, and truthful responses to lawful inquiries.
  - Non-disparagement:
    - Prohibits making or encouraging public statements that disparage the Firm or its stakeholders during and after employment, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with authorities or legal processes.
  - Cooperation:
    - Requires full cooperation and accurate information provision to the Firm and its counsel in audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings related to matters within the employee’s knowledge.

- The section also references obligations to comply with the Award Agreement and a Notice Period requirement (details not included in the excerpt).
text:
Non-Solicitation of Employees and Customers
During your employment by the Firm and for the longer of the (i) one year period following the termination of your employment 
or, (ii) if your award is not cancelled as of your termination date, the three year period from Grant Date, you will not directly or 
indirectly, whether on your own behalf or on behalf of any other party, without the prior written consent of the Director of 
Human Resources: (i) solicit, induce or encourage any of the Firm’s then current employees to leave the Firm or to apply for 
employment elsewhere, unless such current employee has received official, written notice that his or her employment will be 
terminated due to job elimination (ii) hire any employee or former employee who was employed by the Firm at the date your 
employment terminated, unless the individual’s employment terminated because his or her job was eliminated, or the 
individual’s employment with the Firm has been terminated for more than six months, (iii) to the fullest extent enforceable under 
applicable law, solicit or induce or attempt to induce to leave the Firm, or divert or attempt to divert from doing business with 
the Firm, any then current customers, suppliers or other persons or entities that were serviced by you or whose names became 
known to you by virtue of your employment with the Firm, or otherwise interfere with the relationship between the Firm and 
such customers, suppliers or other persons or entities.  This does not apply to publicly known institutional customers that you 
service after your employment with the Firm without the use of the Firm’s confidential or proprietary information. 
These restrictions do not apply to authorized actions you take in the normal course of your employment with the Firm, such as 
employment decisions with respect to employees you supervise or business referrals in accordance with the Firm’s policies.
•

title: Confidential Information
heading: 40.14.2 Confidential Information
start_phrase: You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, directly or indirectly (i) use or disclose to anyone any confidential information related to the Firm’s business, or (ii) communicate with the press or other media about matters related to the Firm, its customers or employees, including matters and activities relating to your employment, or the employment of others, by the Firm, in the case of either (i) or (ii), except as explicitly permitted by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct and applicable policies or law or legal process.
summary:
- Treatment of PSUs upon death:
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares equal to all outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares based on:
    - Average performance for all completed calendar years,
    - Multiplied by one-third of the Target Award for each completed year,
    - Using a 100% Award Payout Percentage for any remaining, uncompleted calendar years.
  - Distribution timing: no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, shares are typically registered to the beneficiary or estate within 60 days after required documentation is received.

- Employee obligations in exchange for the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers:
    - Applies during employment and for the longer of (i) one year post-termination or (ii) three years from Grant Date if the award is not canceled at termination.
    - Prohibits soliciting or inducing Firm employees to leave, hiring recent Firm employees (with limited exceptions), and, to the extent enforceable, soliciting or diverting Firm customers, suppliers, or relationships known through employment. Excludes publicly known institutional customers serviced without using the Firm’s confidential information and authorized actions in the normal course of duties.
  - Confidentiality:
    - No use or disclosure of the Firm’s confidential information during or after employment; no media communications about Firm matters except as permitted by policy, law, or legal process.
    - No unauthorized post-termination access to the Firm’s internal systems.
    - “Confidential information” aligns with the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct.
    - Safe-harbor for reporting concerns to management, directors, government, regulators, self-regulatory bodies, attorneys, or courts, and for truthful legal/regulatory responses.
  - Non-disparagement:
    - No public statements intended or reasonably expected to disparage the Firm or its stakeholders, with carve-outs for lawful reporting and truthful cooperation with legal/regulatory inquiries.
  - Cooperation:
    - Obligation to cooperate fully and provide accurate information to the Firm and its counsel regarding audits, tax matters, litigation, investigations, or governmental proceedings.

- Additional referenced obligations (content not fully shown here): Compliance with Award Agreement and Notice Period.
text:
Confidential Information
You will not, either during your employment with the Firm or thereafter, directly or indirectly (i) use or disclose to anyone any 
confidential information related to the Firm’s business, or (ii) communicate with the press or other media about matters related 
to the Firm, its customers or employees, including matters and activities relating to your employment, or the employment of 
others, by the Firm, in the case of either (i) or (ii), except as explicitly permitted by the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct and 
applicable policies or law or legal process.  In addition, following your termination of employment, you will not, without prior 
written authorization, access the Firm’s private and internal information through telephonic, intranet or internet means.  
“Confidential information” shall have the same meaning for the Award Agreement as it has in the JPMorgan Chase Code of 
Conduct. 
Nothing in this award precludes you from reporting to the Firm’s management or directors, the government, a regulator, a self-
regulatory agency, your attorneys or a court, conduct you believe to be in violation of the law or concerns of any known or 
suspected Code of Conduct violation.  It is also not intended to prevent you from responding truthfully to questions or requests 
from the government, a regulator or in a court of law.

title: Cooperation
heading: 40.14.4 Cooperation
start_phrase: You will cooperate fully with and provide full and accurate information to the Firm and its counsel with respect to any matter (including any audit, tax proceeding, litigation, investigation or governmental proceeding) with respect to which you may have knowledge or information, subject to reimbursement for actual, appropriate and reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by you.

- Death benefits for PSUs:
  - If death occurs after the Performance Period, the beneficiary receives shares equal to all outstanding PSUs.
  - If death occurs during the Performance Period, payout is based on the average performance of completed calendar years, multiplied by one-third of target PSUs for each completed year; remaining years assume a 100% Award Payout Percentage.
  - Shares are distributed no later than the end of the calendar year following the year of death; administratively, shares are typically registered to the beneficiary/estate within 60 days of receiving required documentation.

- Employee obligations tied to the award:
  - Non-solicitation of employees and customers:
    - Applies during employment and for the longer of (i) 1 year post-termination or (ii) 3 years from grant date if the award is not canceled at termination.
    - Prohibits soliciting or hiring certain current/former employees (with limited exceptions) and, to the fullest extent permitted by law, soliciting or diverting customers/suppliers you serviced or learned of through employment (excluding publicly known institutional customers serviced without using the Firm’s confidential information).
    - Does not restrict authorized, job-related actions per Firm policy.
  - Confidential information:
    - No use/disclosure of Firm confidential information or media communications about Firm matters during or after employment, except as allowed by policy, law, or legal process; no post-termination access to internal systems without authorization.
    - Preserves rights to report suspected legal or Code of Conduct violations and to cooperate truthfully with authorities.
  - Non-disparagement:
    - No public statements intended or reasonably expected to disparage the Firm or its people; exceptions for lawful reporting/cooperation.
  - Cooperation:
    - Ongoing duty to cooperate and provide accurate information in audits, litigation, investigations, and related matters, with reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.
  - Compliance with award agreement:
    - Provide requested compliance information; authorize the Firm to disclose award terms to affected third parties, including prospective employers.
  - Notice period:
    - If subject to a contractual/policy notice period, must give advance written notice; the Firm may require work or place you on paid leave during the period.
    - During the notice period, you must devote full time to the Firm, not work elsewhere, and will receive base salary and certain benefits; parties may agree to modify the notice length.
    - Regardless, a separate 180-day advance notice applies if invoking Full Career Eligibility.

- Remedies and enforcement:
  - Cancellation/recapture (up to 100% of outstanding PSUs and related dividend equivalents/calculated PSUs) may occur if the Firm determines:
    - Detrimental conduct causing material financial or reputational harm; award based on materially inaccurate metrics; material misrepresentation; improper/grossly negligent failure to identify/raise/assess material risks; termination for Cause or post-termination determination that Cause existed.
    - Failure to meet advance notice, cooperation, or employment restrictions tied to termination; failure to submit required Release/Certification forms on time; violation of “Your Obligations.”
  - Suspension rights:
    - The Firm may suspend vesting and/or share distribution while evaluating cancellation/recovery or distribution conditions; not responsible for market fluctuations during suspension; suspended units reinstated per plan procedures.
  - Recovery (clawback):
    - You may be required to repay up to the fair market value (as of vest/acceleration) of previously distributed shares (including those under holding requirements) for shares distributed within the three years prior to a notice-of-recovery, subject to Firm-determined conditions (further details referenced but truncated).

Remedies 
•Detrimental Conduct, Risk Related and Other Cancellation/Recapture

Performance Factor”, “Bonus Recoupment”, “EMEA Malus and Clawback Policy – Identified Staff”, “Recapture Provisions” and

title: Administrative Provisions
heading: 40.16 Administrative Provisions
start_phrase: Withholding Taxes: As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the vested shares and the award.
summary:
- Clawback/recapture triggers: repayment or cancellation may be required if you commit fraud, willful misconduct, violate “Your Obligations,” or breach post-employment restrictions (“Full Career Eligibility” or “Government Office”), including detrimental or risk-related conduct.
- One-year lookback: the Firm may require repayment for shares distributed within the year prior to a notice-of-recovery tied to such conduct.
- Notice-of-recovery: written (including electronic) notice to your last known address; notice that the Firm is evaluating recovery preserves its full rights without any obligation to complete the evaluation.
- Tax treatment in recovery: “shares distributed” includes shares withheld for taxes, but the Firm intends not to seek repayment for irrevocable tax withholdings/payments you cannot recover; the Firm/its nominee determines the amount represented by such taxes.
- Repayment form and characterization: repayment may be made in shares or cash and is deemed a lawful recovery, not a penalty; obligations under “Bonus Recoupment” and “EMEA Malus & Clawback Policy – Identified Staff” remain unaffected.
- Injunctive relief: the Firm can obtain an injunction for violations or attempted violations of obligations, in addition to other legal or equitable remedies.
- Tax withholding mechanics: the Firm may satisfy tax obligations by retaining vested shares, selling shares to cover taxes, withholding from cash compensation, or holding vested shares until you pay required taxes.
- Right to set-off: subject to law (including Section 409A), the Firm may retain funds or shares from vesting to satisfy debts you owe; it will not recover amounts from your funds or unrestricted securities held at the Firm without your consent, except for certain award-related accounts referenced below.
- No ownership rights until issuance: PSUs don’t convey stock ownership or voting rights until PSUs are determined and vest; the Firm may open a brokerage/book-entry account to deliver vested shares; PSUs can be canceled if cancellation provisions apply during suspended vesting.
- Post-vesting share restrictions: the Firm may temporarily restrict sale, transfer, pledging, assignment, hedging, or encumbrance of issued shares; these restrictions do not affect voting or dividend rights; if recovery applies during a restriction period, you may owe up to the fair market value of the gross restricted shares.
- Successors: the Award Agreement binds JPMorgan Chase’s successors.
- Employment status: the award is not an employment contract; employment is at-will; no right to future awards; award value does not count for severance.
- Section 409A compliance: the award is intended to comply with 409A; for specified employees, distributions triggered by separation may be delayed six months; payment timing rules for vested portions are defined.
- Corporate actions: equitable adjustments to PSUs/shares may be made for stock splits, dividends, recapitalizations, mergers, spin-offs, or similar events.
- Other equitable adjustments: excluding the “Qualitative Performance Factor,” the Committee may adjust the award up or down to preserve intended economics given unusual events, accounting changes, regulatory capital changes, or similar circumstances.
- Interpretation and administration: the Committee has sole authority to interpret the Plan/Award, determine employment termination reasons, apply post-employment, cancellation, and recovery provisions, decide claims, and delegate authority; determinations need not be uniform and may be selective.
text:
Administrative Provisions 
Withholding Taxes:  As a result of legal and/or tax obligations the Firm, in its sole discretion, may (i) retain from each distribution 
the number of shares of Common Stock required to satisfy applicable tax obligations or (ii) implement any other desirable or 
necessary procedures, so that appropriate withholding and other taxes are paid to the competent authorities with respect to the 
vested shares and the award.  This may include but is not limited to (i) a market sale of a number of such shares on your behalf 
substantially equal to the withholding or other taxes, (ii) to the extent required by law, withhold from cash compensation, an amount 
equal to any withholding obligation with respect to the award and shares that vest under this award, and (iii) retaining shares that 
vest under this award until you pay any taxes associated with the award and vested shares directly to the competent authorities.  
Right to Set Off:  Although the Firm expects to settle this award in share(s) of Common Stock as of the applicable vesting date, as set 
forth in your Award Agreement, the Firm may, to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law (including Section 409A of the 
Code to the extent it is applicable to you), retain for itself funds or the Common Stock resulting from any vesting of this award to 
satisfy any obligation or debt that you owe to the Firm. Notwithstanding any account agreement with the Firm to the contrary, the 
Firm will not recoup or recover any amount owed from any funds or unrestricted securities held in your name and maintained at the 
Firm pursuant to such account agreement to satisfy any obligation or debt or obligation owed by you under this award without your 
consent.  This restriction on the Firm does not apply to accounts described and authorized in “No Ownership Rights/Other 
Limitations” described below.
No Ownership Rights/Other Limitations :  PSUs do not convey the rights of ownership of Common Stock and do not carry voting 
rights.  No shares of Common Stock will be issued to you until after the number of PSUs have been determined, if any, and have 
vested.  Shares will be issued in accordance with JPMorgan Chase’s procedures for issuing stock.  By accepting this award, you 
authorize the Firm, in its sole discretion, to establish on your behalf a brokerage account in your name with the Firm or book-entry 
account with our stock plan administrator and/or transfer agent and deliver to that account any vested shares derived from the 
award.  You also acknowledge that should there be a determination that the cancellation provisions of this award apply during the period when the vesting of any outstanding PSUs has been suspended, then you agree that such PSUs may be cancelled in whole or 
part. (See Sections captioned “ Protection-Based Vesting ”, “Qualitative Performance Factor”, “ Bonus Recoupment ”, “EMEA Malus & 
Clawback Policy - Identified Staff ”, “Termination of Employment ” and “ Remedies ”, as well as the subsection captioned “--
Amendment” permitting suspension of vesting.)
With respect to any applicable vesting date, JPMorgan Chase may impose for any reason, as of such vesting date for such period as it 
may specify in its sole discretion, such restrictions on the Common Stock to be issued to you as it may deem appropriate, including, 
but not limited to, restricting the sale, transfer, pledging, assignment, hedging or encumbrance of such shares of Common Stock. 
Such restrictions described in the last sentence shall not impact your right to vote or receive dividends with respect to the Common 
Stock.  By accepting this award, you acknowledge that during such specified period should there be a determination that the recovery 
provisions of this award apply, then you agree that you may be required to pay the Firm up to an amount equal to the Fair Market 
Value (determined as of the applicable vesting date) of the gross number of shares subject to such restrictions (notwithstanding the 
limitation set forth in the “Right to Set Off” subsection above).  (See sections captioned “ Bonus Recoupment ” and “ Remedies ”.)   
Binding Agreement :  The Award Agreement will be binding upon any successor in interest to JPMorgan Chase, by merger or 
otherwise.
Not a Contract of Employment : Nothing contained in the Award Agreement constitutes a contract of employment or continued 
employment.  Employment is “at-will” and may be terminated by either you or JPMorgan Chase for any reason at any time.  This 
award does not confer any right or entitlement to, nor does the award impose any obligation on the Firm to provide, the same or any 
similar award in the future and its value is not compensation for purposes of determining severance.
Section 409A Compliance :  To the extent that Section 409A of the Code is applicable to this award, distributions of shares hereunder

title: Litigation
heading: 40.25 Litigation
start_phrase: By accepting any award under the Plan, you agree (and have agreed) that in any action or proceeding by the Firm (other than a derivative suit in the right of the Firm) to enforce the terms and conditions of this Award Agreement or any other Award Agreement where the Firm is the prevailing party, the Firm shall be entitled to recover from you its reasonable attorney fees and expenses incurred in such action or proceeding.
summary:
- Requires all claims to be brought on an individual basis; waives the right to participate in class, collective, or other representative actions.
- Litigation/fee-shifting: If the Firm sues to enforce the award terms and prevails, it may recover reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses; the participant agrees not to seek advancement of fees or indemnification under the Firm’s By-Laws in such suits.
- Non-transferability: RSU/PSU awards and related rights cannot be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, hypothecated, or subjected to liens; transfer permitted only upon death via will, laws of descent, or a beneficiary designation on file.
- Definitions included:
  - Average Tangible Common Equity: Annual average common equity minus goodwill and identifiable intangibles, based on publicly disclosed quarterly (or year-end) balances; used solely for Performance Ranking.
  - Award Payout Percentage: As specified in the Performance Table footnote.
  - Calculated PSUs: Target Award Number multiplied by the Award Payout Percentage tied to the Firm’s three-year average Performance Ranking, with an override based on average Firm Reported ROTCE thresholds; any award cancellation reduces the Target Award Number.
  - Calculation Agent: Independent third party (e.g., accounting/consulting firm) retained by HR.
  - Cause: Termination for reasons including legal/regulatory violations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, material policy/code violations, grossly inadequate performance or failure to follow directives, or conduct injurious to the Firm or its relationships.
  - Financial Services Company: Broadly defined to include banking, insurance, advisory/investment banking, brokerage, asset/wealth management, payments/merchant services, FX, securitization/derivatives, fintech, private equity/real estate activities, and similar services as determined by HR.
  - Firm Reported ROTCE: Annual return on tangible common equity as reported in public year-end disclosures, without reporting rounding conventions.

title: Definitions
heading: 40.27 Definitions
start_phrase: “Average Tangible Common Equity” means annual average common stockholders’ equity less annual average goodwill and annual average identifiable intangible assets.
summary:
- Dispute and litigation terms:
  - All claims must be brought on an individual basis; you waive participation in class, collective, or other representative actions.
  - In Firm-initiated actions to enforce the Award Agreement where the Firm prevails, the Firm may recover its reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses.
  - You agree not to seek advancement of fees or indemnification under the Firm’s by-laws in such suits.

- Transfer restrictions:
  - Awards (including RSUs and PSUs) and related rights may not be assigned, pledged, transferred, hedged, or otherwise encumbered.
  - Transfer is allowed only upon death via will, laws of descent, or a beneficiary designation on file.

- Core performance share unit (PSU) framework and calculations:
  - Target Award Number: the baseline number of PSUs designated in the Award Agreement; reduced by any cancellations.
  - Performance Period: a specified three-calendar-year span.
  - Firm Reported ROTCE and Average Tangible Common Equity (ATCE) defined and used solely for Performance Ranking; ROTCE recalculated if financials are restated.
  - Calculated PSUs: Target Award Number multiplied by an Award Payout Percentage tied to the Firm’s three-year average ROTCE ranking versus a defined peer set (“Performance Companies”).
  - Award Payout mechanics:
    - Performance Table maps absolute ROTCE levels and relative ROTCE rankings to specific payout percentages.
    - Substitution rules apply if the Firm’s average ROTCE meets/exceeds an upper threshold or falls below a lower threshold.
    - Tie-handling rules clarify how equal rankings affect payout determinations.
  - Independent Calculation Agent (not owned/controlled by the Firm) may be retained to perform calculations.

- Financial thresholds:
  - Firmwide Financial Threshold: a minimum cumulative ROTCE over the three-year period (formula specified).
  - Line of Business (LOB) Financial Thresholds:
    - Thresholds defined primarily as annual negative pre-tax pre-provision income or pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income, depending on LOB.
    - Applies to AWM, Card & Auto, Commercial Banking, CIB (overall or specified products excluding XVA), Consumer/Wealth/Business Banking, Corporate Functions (including CIO), and Home Lending.
    - Clarifies definitions of pre-tax pre-provision income and pre-tax pre-loan loss reserve income.
  - Corporate Functions (including CIO) treated as a single LOB.

- Peer group governance:
  - “Performance Companies” are peers with business mixes overlapping the Firm’s; the Committee may adjust the list prospectively for mergers, spin-offs, business mix changes, or cessation.

- Employment and eligibility definitions:
  - Cause: includes legal/regulatory violations, felony indictment/conviction, fraud, Code of Conduct/policy violations, grossly inadequate performance or refusal to follow directives, and acts injurious to the Firm’s interests.
  - Recognized Service: as defined in Firm policies.

- Sector and role definitions:
  - Financial Services Company: broadly defined to include banking, insurance, advisory, brokerage, asset management, FX, payment processing, securitization, fintech (including blockchain/financial products), private equity/real estate, and similar activities per HR discretion.
  - Not-for-Profit Organization: 501(c)(3) entities or foreign equivalents with identical purposes.
  - Government Office: full-time elected/appointed roles not expected to be full career, or bona fide full-time campaigns after formal filing.

- Administrative notes:
  - Many percentages, years, firms, and rankings are placeholders to be filled in the Award Agreement.
  - Calculations and definitions are expressly for determining PSU payouts and Performance Ranking.
text:
Definitions
“Average Tangible Common Equity”  means annual average common stockholders’ equity less annual average goodwill and annual 
average identifiable intangible assets.  Annual averages of the components of Average Tangible Common Equity will be calculated 
using quarterly balances as reported in publically available financial disclosures.  In the event that quarterly balances are not 
available, annual year end balances will be used. This calculation is used solely for purposes of the Performance Ranking.  
“Award Payout Percentage” means the applicable percentage specified in the footnote to the Performance Table.  
“Calculated PSUs”  means the number of PSUs determined by multiplying the Target Award Number (after giving effect to any 
cancellation thereof, in whole or in part) by the Award Payout Percentage corresponding to the Firm’s Performance Ranking based on 
the three-year average performance for the Performance Period (both percentage and ranking, as set forth in the footnote to the 
Performance Table); provided that if the average of the Firm’s Reported ROTCE for the Performance Period either equals or exceeds 
_____% or is less than _____% (without taking into account any rounding conventions used), _______ percent or _______, respectively as the 
case may be, shall be substituted for the Performance Period’s Award Payout Percentage in calculating the number of PSUs to 
distribute. For avoidance of doubt, any cancellation of this award (in whole or in part) during the Performance Period will reduce the 
Target Award Number.
“Calculation Agent”  means a third party entity not owned or controlled by the Firm, such as an accounting or consulting firm, 
retained from time to time by the Director of Human Resources or his/her delegate.
“Cause”  means a determination by the Firm that your employment terminated as a result of your (i) violation of any law, rule or 
regulation (including rules of self-regulatory bodies) related to the Firm’s business, (ii) indictment or conviction of a felony, (iii) 
commission of a fraudulent act, (iv) violation of the JPMorgan Chase Code of Conduct or other Firm policies or misconduct related to 
your duties to the Firm (other than immaterial and inadvertent violations or misconduct), (v) grossly inadequate performance of the 
duties associated with your position or job function or failure to follow reasonable directives of your manager, or (vi) any act or 
failure to act that is injurious to the interests of the Firm or its relationship with a customer, client or an employee.
“Financial Services Company”  means a business enterprise that engages in any of the following services (itself or through an 
affiliate or subsidiary), regardless of whether such services are the principle strategy or revenue-generating activity:
•commercial or retail banking, including, but not limited to, commercial, institutional and personal trust, custody and/or lending 
and processing services, internet banking, originating and servicing mortgages, issuing and servicing credit cards, payment 
servicing or processing or merchant services,
•insurance, including but not limited to, guaranteeing against loss, harm, damage, illness, disability or death, providing and issuing 
annuities, acting as principal, agent or broker for purpose of the forgoing,
•financial, investment or economic advisory services, including but not limited to, investment banking services (such as advising on 
mergers or dispositions, underwriting, dealing in, or making a market in securities or other similar activities), brokerage services, 
investment management services, asset management services, foreign exchange services, interbank networks and hedge funds,
•issuing, trading or selling instruments representing interests in pools of assets or in derivatives instruments, 
•financial technology (“Fintech”) companies, such as those selling blockchain services, or offering or selling financial products/
services,
•advising on, or investing in, private equity or real estate funds or ventures, or
•any similar activities that the Director of Human Resources or nominee determines in his or her sole discretion constitute financial 
services.
“Firm Reported ROTCE”  means the Firm’s percentage return on tangible common equity for each year in the Performance Period (as 
calculated for use in its  publicly available year-end financial disclosures without taking  into account any rounding conventions used 
for financial reporting purposes).“Firmwide Financial Threshold”  means a cumulative return on tangible common equity for calendar years 20____, 20____ and 20____ of 
not less than ______%.  Cumulative return on tangible common equity means (i) the sum of the Firm’s reported net income for all three 
calendar years, divided by (ii) reported year-end tangible equity averaged over the three years.
 “Government Office”  means (i) a full-time position in an elected or appointed office in local, state, or federal government (including 
equivalent positions outside the U.S. or in a supranational organization), not reasonably anticipated to be a full-career position, or (ii) 
conducting a bona fide full-time campaign for such an elective public office after formally filing for candidacy, where it is customary 
and reasonably necessary to campaign full-time for the office.

heading: 40.28 Government Office Requirements
start_phrase: You may be eligible to continue vesting in all or part of your award if you voluntarily resign to accept a Government Office (as defined above) or to become a candidate for an elective Government Office.
summary:

text:
Government Office Requirements
You may be eligible to continue vesting in all or part of your award if you voluntarily resign to accept a Government Office (as defined 
above) or to become a candidate for an elective Government Office.

title: Full Career Eligibility
heading: 40.28.1 Full Career Eligibility
start_phrase: “Government Office Requirements ” does not apply to you if you satisfy the subsection captioned “--Full Career Eligibility” as of the date that you voluntarily terminate your employment with the Firm.
summary:
- Purpose: Outlines when an employee who resigns to accept or run for a Government Office may continue vesting in all or part of an equity award.
- Full Career Eligibility carve-out: These Government Office provisions do not apply if the employee qualifies for Full Career Eligibility at the time of resignation.
- Eligibility requirements:
  - Provide at least 60 days’ written notice to resign for Government Office; cooperate during notice and do not work for another employer; Firm may shorten the notice.
  - Provide confirmation that continued vesting is legally permissible.
  - Provide documentation that the resignation is to accept or seek Government Office.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award), following the original vesting schedule:
  - 50% with ≥3 and <4 years of continuous service.
  - 75% with ≥4 and <5 years.
  - 100% with ≥5 years.
  - Non-CV portion is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to maintain continued vesting:
  - For non-elective Government Office: remain in that office for at least two years after leaving the Firm; if the office term is shorter, eligibility applies if a vesting date occurs during the government service.
  - For elective office: the employee’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot.
  - Performance and protection-based vesting conditions still apply to the CV Award.
- Satisfaction of conditions:
  - If the government service ends after two or more years, or if the employee campaigned, appeared on the ballot, and was not elected, any outstanding CV Awards (including those previously accelerated for ethics/conflict reasons) continue under the Award Agreement as if the employee had Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions during the vesting period.
- Failure to satisfy conditions:
  - Any outstanding PSUs in the CV Award are canceled.
  - Repayment required of the Fair Market Value of shares previously distributed due to accelerated distribution for ethics/conflict reasons that would have remained outstanding PSUs at the failure date; FMV measured on the distribution date.
text:

title: Eligibility
heading: 40.28.2 Eligibility
start_phrase: Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
summary:
- Scope: Outlines conditions under which an employee who voluntarily resigns to accept or campaign for a Government Office may continue vesting in all or part of an equity award.
- Full Career Eligibility carve-out: These Government Office Requirements do not apply if the employee qualifies for Full Career Eligibility at termination.
- Eligibility prerequisites:
  - Provide at least 60 days’ advance written notice (the Firm may shorten this), cooperate during the notice period, and refrain from working for any other employer.
  - Provide confirmation acceptable to the Firm that continued vesting is legally permissible.
  - Provide documentation acceptable to the Firm that the resignation is to accept or pursue a Government Office.
- Portion of award that can continue vesting (CV Award), based on continuous service at termination:
  - 50% for ≥3 and <4 years,
  - 75% for ≥4 and <5 years,
  - 100% for ≥5 years.
  - The remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions for continued vesting:
  - Non-elective office: Must remain in such office for at least two years after termination; if the office term is under two years, eligibility applies if a vesting date occurs during government service.
  - Elective office campaign: The employee’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot. If not elected, specific employment restrictions apply during the remaining vesting period.
  - Performance and protection-based vesting conditions still apply to the CV Award.
- Satisfaction of conditions:
  - If the government service lasts ≥2 years (non-elective) or the employee appears on the ballot (elective) and is not elected, any outstanding CV Awards (and awards previously accelerated for ethics/conflict reasons) continue under the Award Agreement for the remaining vesting period as if the employee met Full Career Eligibility, including employment restrictions during vesting.
- Failure to satisfy conditions:
  - Any outstanding PSUs under the CV Award are cancelled.
  - The employee must repay the Fair Market Value (as of distribution date) of shares previously distributed that would have remained outstanding PSUs but for an accelerated distribution due to ethics/conflict considerations related to government employment.
text:
Eligibility for continued vesting is conditioned on your providing the Firm:
•At least 60 days’ advance written notice of your intention to resign to accept or pursue a Government Office (see section 
captioned “ Definitions ”), during which period you must perform in a cooperative and professional manner services requested by 
the Firm and not provide services for any other employer.  The Firm may elect to shorten this notice period at the Firm’s sole 
discretion.
•Confirmation, in a form satisfactory to the Firm, that vesting in this award pursuant to this provision would not violate any 
applicable law, regulation or rule.
•Documentation in a form satisfactory to the Firm that your resignation is for the purpose of accepting a Government Office or 
becoming a candidate for a Government Office.  (See section captioned “ Definitions ”.)

title: Portion of Your Award Subject to Continued Vesting
heading: 40.28.3 Portion of Your Award Subject to Continued Vesting
start_phrase: Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of this award that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s original schedule will be based on your years of continuous service completed with the Firm immediately preceding your termination date, as follows:
summary:
- Purpose: Outlines when an employee who resigns to accept or run for a Government Office may continue vesting in an equity award.
- Full Career Eligibility carve-out: These Government Office Requirements do not apply if the employee already meets Full Career Eligibility at resignation.
- Eligibility prerequisites:
  - Provide at least 60 days’ written notice (Firm may shorten), work cooperatively during notice, and not work elsewhere.
  - Provide confirmation that continued vesting is legally permissible.
  - Provide documentation that the resignation is to accept or to campaign for a Government Office.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award) based on continuous service at termination:
  - 50% for 3–<4 years; 75% for 4–<5 years; 100% for 5+ years. The non-eligible portion is canceled at termination.
- Conditions to receive the CV Award:
  - Non-elective office: remain in that office for 2+ years post-termination; if the term is under 2 years, eligibility applies if a vesting date falls during the government service.
  - Elective office campaign: the employee’s name must appear on the primary or final public ballot. If not elected, employment restrictions apply as noted.
- Ongoing terms: Performance and protection-based vesting conditions continue to apply to the CV Award.
- Upon satisfying conditions:
  - Any outstanding CV Awards (including those previously accelerated for ethics/conflict reasons) are subject, for the remaining vesting period, to the same terms and employment restrictions as if the employee had resigned with Full Career Eligibility.
- Failure to satisfy conditions:
  - Outstanding PSUs under the CV Award are canceled.
  - Clawback: repay the Fair Market Value (determined as of the distribution date) of shares previously distributed that would have remained as PSUs but for accelerated distribution tied to government employment ethics/conflict rules.
text:
Portion of Your Award Subject to Continued Vesting:
Subject to the conditions below, the percentage of this award that will continue to vest in accordance with this award’s original

•75% if you have at least 4 but less than 5 years of continuous service, or
•100% if you have 5 or more years of continuous service. 
The portion of this award subject to continued vesting above is referred to as the “CV Award” and the portion not subject to continued

- Failure to satisfy conditions:

  - Clawback: repay Fair Market Value (measured on distribution date) of any shares previously distributed early that would have remained outstanding as PSUs absent the accelerated distribution.
- Notes: References definitions of Government Office and an accelerated distribution subsection for ethics/conflict reasons; firm retains discretion over notice period and satisfactory forms of confirmation/documentation.
text:

title: Satisfaction of Conditions
heading: 40.28.5 Satisfaction of Conditions
start_phrase: If your service in a Government Office ends two years or more after your employment with the Firm terminates, or in the case of resignation from the Firm to campaign for a Government Office,
summary:
- Purpose: Explains when and how an employee who resigns to accept or campaign for a Government Office can continue vesting in all or part of an equity award.
- Applicability: Does not apply if the employee qualifies for Full Career Eligibility at termination.
- Eligibility requirements: Provide at least 60 days’ written notice (Firm may shorten), cooperate and not work elsewhere during notice, confirm no legal/regulatory conflicts, and submit documentation proving the Government Office acceptance or candidacy.
- Portion eligible for continued vesting (CV Award): Based on continuous service at termination—50% (3–<4 years), 75% (4–<5 years), 100% (≥5 years); the remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions to receive the CV Award:
  - Non-elective Government Office: Must serve 2+ years post-termination; if the term is under 2 years, eligibility applies if a vesting date occurs during the government service.
  - Elective Government Office: Name must appear on the primary or final public ballot.
  - Performance and protection-based vesting conditions continue to apply.
- If conditions are satisfied: Any outstanding CV Awards (and those that would have been outstanding but for ethics/conflict-driven accelerated distributions) continue under the award’s original terms and employment restrictions for the remaining vesting period, as if the employee had resigned with Full Career Eligibility.
- If conditions are not satisfied: Outstanding CV PSUs are cancelled, and the employee must repay the fair market value of any shares previously distributed due to an accelerated distribution for government ethics/conflict reasons (FMV measured on the distribution date).
- Cross-references: Definitions and an accelerated distribution provision for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment.

Satisfaction of Conditions:
If your service in a Government Office ends two years or more after your employment with the Firm terminates, or in the case of 
resignation from the Firm to campaign for a Government Office, your name is on the primary or final public ballot for the election and 
you are not elected, any CV Awards then outstanding and any such awards that would have then been outstanding but for an 
accelerated distribution of shares (as described in the subsection captioned “--Accelerated Distribution for Ethics or Conflict Reasons 
Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity”) will be subject for the remainder of the applicable vesting period to the same 
terms and conditions of this Award Agreement, including employment restrictions during the vesting period, as if you had resigned 
from the Firm having met the  requirements for Full Career Eligibility.

title: Failure to Satisfy Conditions
heading: 40.28.6 Failure to Satisfy Conditions
start_phrase: If you do not satisfy the above “Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards”, any outstanding PSUs under the CV Award will be cancelled.
summary:
- Policy purpose: Outlines conditions under which an employee who resigns to accept or run for a Government Office may continue vesting in all or part of an equity award.
- Full Career Eligibility carve-out: The “Government Office Requirements” section does not apply if the employee qualifies for Full Career Eligibility at the time of resignation.
- Eligibility prerequisites for continued vesting:
  - Provide at least 60 days’ advance written notice; cooperate during the notice period and refrain from other employment (Firm may shorten the period).
  - Provide confirmation that continued vesting is legally permissible.
  - Provide satisfactory documentation that the resignation is to accept or pursue a Government Office.
- Portion of award eligible for continued vesting (CV Award) based on continuous service at resignation:
  - 50% for 3 to <4 years,
  - 75% for 4 to <5 years,
  - 100% for 5+ years; the remainder is cancelled at termination.
- Conditions to receive the CV Award:
  - Hold a non-elective Government Office for at least two years after termination (or qualify if a vest date occurs during a shorter non-elective term), or
  - For elective office, appear on the primary or final public ballot.
  - Performance and protection-based vesting terms continue to apply.
- Satisfaction of conditions: If met (including not being elected after appearing on the ballot), outstanding CV Awards continue on the original schedule and are governed as if the employee resigned with Full Career Eligibility, including ongoing employment restrictions during vesting; provisions address any prior accelerated distributions made for ethics/conflict reasons tied to government employment.
- Failure to satisfy conditions: CV Award PSUs are cancelled and the employee must repay the fair market value of shares previously distributed that would otherwise have remained outstanding PSUs but for accelerated distribution related to government ethics/conflict requirements.
- Exhibit 21: Lists JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s significant legal entity subsidiaries as of December 31, 2022, per SEC rules; includes certain material legal entities for Dodd-Frank resolution planning even if not “significant,” and excludes entities that are not significant in aggregate.
- Sample subsidiaries and jurisdictions include: JPMorgan Chase Bank, National Association (US); Paymentech, LLC (US); J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (US); J.P. Morgan Securities PLC (UK); J.P. Morgan SE (Germany); JPMorgan Securities Japan Co., Ltd. (Japan); J.P. Morgan Services India Private Limited (India); and multiple asset management entities in the US, UK, and Luxembourg.
text:
Failure to Satisfy Conditions:
If you do not satisfy the above “Conditions for Continued Vesting of Awards”, any outstanding PSUs under the CV Award will be 
cancelled. You also will be required to repay the Fair Market Value of the number of shares (before tax and other withholdings) of 
Common Stock distributed to you that would have been outstanding as PSUs on the date you failed to satisfy the “Conditions for 
Continued Vesting of Award” but for their accelerated distribution (as described in subsection captioned,  “Accelerated Distribution 
for Ethics or Conflict Reasons Resulting From Employment by a Government Entity”). Fair Market Value for this purpose will be 
determined as the date that the shares were distributed.

title: CERTIFICATION
heading: Exhibit 31.1 JPMorgan Chase & Co. CERTIFICATION
start_phrase: 1. I have reviewed this Annual Report on Form 10-K of JPMorgan Chase & Co.;
summary:
- Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 of JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Form 10-K contain Sarbanes-Oxley Section 302 certifications by CEO James Dimon and CFO Jeremy Barnum, dated February 21, 2023.
- Both officers certify they have reviewed the 10-K; it contains no untrue statements or material omissions; and the financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the company’s financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows for the periods presented.
- They state responsibility for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting (ICFR); that such controls were designed under their supervision; that the effectiveness of disclosure controls was evaluated as of period-end; and that any changes in ICFR during the most recent fiscal quarter that materially affected or are likely to materially affect ICFR were disclosed.
- They confirm disclosure to the auditors and audit committee of all significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in ICFR, and any fraud (whether or not material) involving management or employees with significant ICFR roles.
- Signatures and titles: James Dimon, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; Jeremy Barnum, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.
text:
Exhibit 31.1
JPMorgan Chase & Co.
CERTIFICATION
I, James Dimon, certify that:
1. I have reviewed this Annual Report on Form 10-K of JPMorgan Chase & Co.;
2. Based on my knowledge, this report does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit to state a material 
fact necessary to make the statements made, in light of the circumstances under which such statements were made, not 
misleading with respect to the period covered by this report;
3. Based on my knowledge, the financial statements, and other financial information included in this report, fairly present in 
all material respects the financial condition, results of operations and cash flows of the registrant as of, and for, the periods 
presented in this report;
4. The registrant’s other certifying officer and I are responsible for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and 
procedures (as defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e)) and internal control over financial reporting (as 
defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f)) for the registrant and have:
(a)  Designed such disclosure controls and procedures, or caused such disclosure controls and procedures to be designed 
under our supervision, to ensure that material information relating to the registrant, including its consolidated 
subsidiaries, is made known to us by others within those entities, particularly during the period in which this report is 
being prepared;
(b)  Designed such internal control over financial reporting, or caused such internal control over financial reporting to be 
designed under our supervision, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and 
the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting 
principles;
(c)  Evaluated the effectiveness of the registrant’s disclosure controls and procedures and presented in this report our 
conclusions about the effectiveness of the disclosure controls and procedures, as of the end of the period covered by 
this report based on such evaluation; and
(d)  Disclosed in this report any change in the registrant’s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during 
the registrant’s most recent fiscal quarter (the registrant’s fourth quarter in the case of an annual report) that has 
materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the registrant’s internal control over financial 
reporting; and
5. The registrant’s other certifying officer and I have disclosed, based on our most recent evaluation of internal control over 
financial reporting, to the registrant’s auditors and the audit committee of the registrant’s board of directors (or persons 
performing the equivalent function):
(a)  All significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in the design or operation of internal control over financial 
reporting which are reasonably likely to adversely affect the registrant’s ability to record, process, summarize and 
report financial information; and
(b)  Any fraud, whether or not material, that involves management or other employees who have a significant role in the 
registrant’s internal control over financial reporting.

/s/ James Dimon
James Dimon
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
